backlog.title: Multi-Select Component
backlog.body:
What

We are looking to implement a component that is a hybrid version of: Selects, Checkboxes and Search boxes. The multi-select component provides the following functionality:

A select like component that can store a large list of selectable items in a collapsable control
The ability to search for items and order the most relevant items to the top of the list
Options to select/deselect all items with one click
Options to select/deselect one or more items in the list


Example


Collapsed initial state of the multi-select component with no selected items
Expanded state of the multi-select component with a dynamic search bar at the top of the component (default focus), select/deselect all items underneath; followed by a list of remaining items with 2 items having been selected
Collapsed final state of the multi-select component with 2 selected items

Why

The need for a multi-select component is required for making large lists of items (30+ items) searchable and selectable. By integrating a multi-select component within the GOV.UK Design System, we are supporting the functionality required by users to traverse and select large lists of items efficiently.

Perks

Streamlines the selection process
Improves similar filters such as scrollable checkboxes
Enhances the user interface by minimising the display space through the implementation of collapsable filters

Anything else

React Multi-Select Component Example

backlog.title: Highlighting information
backlog.body:
What

Give a brief description of the style, component or pattern you want to propose.

A number of internal services across government (examples below) have implemented a highlight pattern to focus a user's attention to particular parts of data. The pattern is used to visually highlight text to differentiate it from other information on the screen.

The following use cases of the pattern have been identified so far:

To highlight to users where data has changed - NHS cervical screening
To highlight to users where data is different when comparing - Identity verification, Home Office
To highlight to users where data matches when comparing - n'Delius records, MoJ
To highlight to users matched data from a search request - Search service, Home Office

Why
The pattern has been well tested in multiple services and already exists on live services within Home Office and MoJ.
The task to compare data is common, particularly for internal case working / management services. The ability to visually highlight elements should save the user time to find what they are looking for, especially when there is a lot of content on the page, or comparing multiple sets of data at once - valuable for repeat users.
Anything else
Examples in existing services:
NHS cervical screening management - used to identify changes in medical records


MoJ - used to identity cases and merge them

(Proposed) mock up design to be used in Home Office identity verification service - used to identify differences in two data sets

Accessibility considerations
Even though we can call out the highlighted text for screen reader users, conscious that the visual colour may not be ideal for users who are partially sighted. Curious to hear any comments around this.

backlog.title: Indeterminate progress indicator
Geolocation design
backlog.body:
What
Geolocation APIs allows the user to provide their location to web applications if they so desire. For privacy reasons, the user is asked for permission to report location information.
There is currently no standard design for how this should be implemented - for example, a standard link or icon that could be added to relevant search pages.
Why
Users could automatically provide their location without manual entry and search.
This creates a lot of interesting potential for GOV.UK services, such as integrating with backend systems to provide locally specific information for the area the user is in. This could be used for services that may be used by users who are on the move, or don't know the local area:

Finding nearby flood warnings in force
Find a school inspection report for nearby schools
Find your local council
Find your rubbish collection day
Find a weighbridge

Most location search on GOV.UK relies on the user knowing a postcode or area name. If may be quicker, and easier to simply search for their current location using Geolocation APIs that are part of HTML5
Anything else
Thoughts on implementation:

Use feature detection in case a user's browser doesn't support geolocation
Agree standard design for services that use Geolocation including permission wording and icon design

ourIssues.title: Investigate making it clearer that the Design System email address is not a generic government helpline
ourIssues.body:
Adding as I think we've discussed this before but never written it up.

## What

We very frequently receive emails from members of the public who have encountered issues with a GOV.UK service (or a government service generally) and are seeking support or updates. 

This is despite displaying a warning on our [get in touch](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/get-in-touch/) page stating that we are unable to help with these queries and providing instructions on how to contact the relevant government departments. 

## Why

This is not a high-volume issue (around a dozen emails a week or fewer), but it's a persistent one.

Members of the public often include Personally Identifying Information in these emails, unnecessarily exposing Design System team members to PII and requiring every member of the team to manually delete the offending emails from their inboxes to comply with data protection laws. In Zendesk, it also means that we need to go through the data redaction process before we can proceed to forward the ticket to user support.

In addition to dealing with the irrelevant ticket, these additional PII tasks are distracting for the whole team. They don't always happen in a timely fashion (if at all) due to members being on leave or on non-working days.

By reducing the quantity of unrelated support emails the team receives, we can alleviate this source frustration and help avoid unnecessarily holding personal data. 

A non-exhaustive list of potential ways to resolve this:

- Remove the contact page from search engine results, as (assumedly) this is where members of the public are finding it.
- Rewrite and/or reformat the existing warning text to make it _extremely_ explicit that we do not provide support or information to members of the public.
  - Consider harsher language in general, such as saying that emails from the public will be deleted and not responded to. 
- Use a more visually prominent component, such as a [Notification banner](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/notification-banner/), or bespoke styling, to display the warning.
- Consider not displaying the email address or link unless a user performs an action acknowledging the warning.

## Who needs to work on this

- Content designers
- Developers (potentially)
- Designers (potentially)

## Who needs to review this

- Content designers

## Done when

- [ ] Thing to do

communityIssues.title: Radio: `heading_caption` renders at `govuk-caption-m` when `heading_level` is 0
communityIssues.body: ## Cause [_radio.html.erb](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk_publishing_components/blob/main/app/views/govuk_publishing_components/components/_radio.html.erb) works out `size` (default `m`, or `heading_size` if valid) and uses it for the caption class (`govuk-caption-#{size}`). Since #5809, the legend's `govuk-fieldset__legend--{size}` class is skipped when `heading_level == "span"` (`heading_level: 0`) but the caption still uses `size`. ## Consequences With `heading_level: 0` and a `heading_caption` a sized caption sits above regular-weight legend text: ``` Question 3 of 9 What is your favourite skittle? ``` No test covers a caption at `heading_level: 0`. ### Possible approach Decide what a caption means on a non-heading legend, then: - don't render it at level 0 or - size it to match the unsized legend or - leave it as it is and add a test that documents that ### Proposed rating (for triage) - **Impact of leaving it**: Low (edge case, needs `heading_level: 0` plus a caption, and I don't yet know of any consumers doing that) - **Effort to fix**: Low (one condition in template, plus a spec) - **Overall**: Low ### Things to check - Whether any apps pass `heading_level: 0` with `heading caption` (org-wide code search) - What the design system says about captions on non-heading legends ### Context Spotted while reviewing #5809

communityIssues.title: HasPartSchema and IsPartOfSchema are functionally identical
communityIssues.body:
### Cause
The two presenters were written to mirror the [schema.org](http://schema.org) `hasPart` and `isPartOf` properties, but they build the same hash from a URL: `@context`, `@type: "CreativeWork"` and `sameAs`. 

`CreativeWorkSchema` is the only caller, using `links.documents` for `hasPart` and `links.document_collections` for `isPartOf`, and an org-wide code search finds no other references.

### Consequences
Two classes and two specs to maintain for one behaviour and an unused public method.

### Possible approach
Use one presenter for both keys

### Proposed rating (for triage)
- **Impact of leaving it**: Low (small duplication, no known user-facing effect)
- **Effort to fix**: Low (one class and two call sites, with specs already checking the output)
- **Overall**: Low 

### Context
Spotted while adding specs in #5803

communityIssues.title: Search with autocomplete default value appearing on first click of the input field
communityIssues.body: When the user lands on a search page that already has a query parameter (e.g they started their search in the header or on the home page), on the first click of the input field they see an item in the autocomplete menu that matches the search term. This doesn't happen on subsequent clicks. Search that doesn't have autocomplete suggestions: This happens even on terms that have autocomplete suggestions. Search that would normally have autocomplete suggestions when the user types: Search that would normally have autocomplete suggestions when the user lands on the search page and clicks on the input field: It likely happens because of how [accessible autocomplete](https://github.com/alphagov/accessible-autocomplete) interprets the default value of an input field.

communityIssues.title: Request for 'grouped options' support for 'select' component
communityIssues.body:
Whitehall's [select_with_search](https://github.com/alphagov/whitehall/blob/50b8ddd41e0d1d12ba5d27dc7ac9e9b7f37a5f2a/app/views/components/docs/select_with_search.yml#L46) component is a bespoke component that wraps around the 'select' component. It adds a search input field, to make the options searchable (powered by Choices.js).

In addition, it supports `<optgroup>` via a `grouped_options` property, where instead of:

```yml
      options:
      - text: Option one
        value: option1
      - text: Option two
        value: option2
```

We have data like:

```yml
      grouped_options:
      - - England
        - - text: Bath
            value: bath
          - text: Bristol
            value: bristol
          - text: London
            value: london
          - text: Manchester
            value: manchester
      - - Northern Ireland
        - - text: Bangor
            value: bangor
          - text: Belfast
            value: belfast
```

Screenshot example:

> ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/20eaa635-ba4e-43c1-9e09-9ed46be8d082)

This is a genuinely useful feature which doesn't need to be coupled to 'select with search' - it could be supported by the 'select' component itself with minimal tweaks.

The 'search' component's lack of support for this was ultimately a factor in [deciding which component to go with](https://trello.com/c/pmbL2yId/3411-consolidate-the-autocomplete-selectwithsearch-components-in-whitehall) when we recently consolidated several similarly behaving components. We could potentially have explored killing off some of these more complex components if we were able to fall back on native 'grouped options' support from the standard Select component.

communityIssues.title: Investigate removing nested option in checkboxes component
communityIssues.body:
We have a [nested option](https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/checkboxes/checkbox_items_with_nested_checkboxes) for the checkboxes component, which looks like this:

![Screenshot 2024-06-14 at 14 57 28](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk_publishing_components/assets/861310/64e9bcc5-354a-44b0-a00e-f503b919e9bd)

The Design System component on which this component is based doesn't have this option - we added it as a custom option a few years ago. There are some possible accessibility concerns:

- no hierarchy present for screen reader users to understand that nested checkboxes belong to a parent (was previously in a list, but we've updated the markup to match the DS component, which uses DIV elements instead of lists)
- no indication for screen reader users that changing nested checkboxes can select/deselect parent checkboxes (is this a problem?)

communityIssues.title: Govspeak styling doesn't match semantics
communityIssues.body:
Some Govspeak elements don't look like what they are.

## Headings

### Level 1 headings

H1s are generally styled like paragraphs, so don't look like headings at all.
That's intentionally done because, as the [code comment](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk_publishing_components/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/govuk_publishing_components/components/helpers/_markdown-typography.scss#L23-L30) says:

> Markdown is expected to be styled within a document with a H1 title
> thus H1's are not expected and are discouraged by bare styling

### Level 4-6 headings

Something similar is happening with H4s, H5s and H6s.
They all look like H3s (except H5s and H6s don't have a top margin) [for similar reasons](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk_publishing_components/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/govuk_publishing_components/components/helpers/_markdown-typography.scss#L49-L66):

> H4, H5 and H6 are discouraged and thus styled the same

### Why it's a problem

While H1 and H4-H6 are indeed discouraged, publishers do use them.
And when they get used, they show a visible heading structure that is different from the actual heading structure.
And that is a **fail of the WCAG success criterion 1.3.1** (Info and Relationships).

This means that screen reader users and users who change styles (and search engines) will get a different experience than other users.
It also means the heading structure could be confusing for people who can see the visuals.

That could be solved by changing the styles to match the semantics (in this repo).
If you wanted to re-introduce some kind of styling that still discourages publishers from using those heading levels, it would need to be done differently.
Or this could be solved (at least for future occurrences) on the publisher side by not allowing those heading levels in the content when a page gets published.
While styling it wouldn't fix that part of the problem, it at least makes the problem visible and seeing users would get the same information.

## Italics

Text emphasized with `em` (or `*italics*` and `_italics_` in Govspeak) doesn't show any styling at all.
That is also intentional for similar reasons as italics are discouraged.
But because publishers do use them, they are in the code, just not visibly styled.

This is technically also a WCAG 1.3.1 fail, although it has hardly any practical implications as most (or all?) screen readers don't read italics/em differently.
This would still affect users who change styles, but is not likely to have a significant impact.

## What:

But sometimes they are more clearly heading things, other times they aren't. They’re not always heading something useful (like just a date on the Brexit guidance) and would be bad as headings in that case. Although inconsistency would be worse, if some were headings and others weren’t.

This needs some investigation and might not need any fixing.

Many screen reader users are used to navigating via headings. communityIssues.title: Using `true` as a default parameter value is confusing
communityIssues.body:
In the search component, there is an [option to prevent the label from appearing inside the text input][1].

The parameter that does this - `inline_label` - defaults to `true`. To set the label to appear above, you need to set that parameter to `false`.

```erb
<%= render "govuk_publishing_components/components/search", {
  inline_label: false,
} %>
```

This makes sense when using component itself, but does leave things a little confusing when updating the component markup.

An unwritten but useful convention is for components to set any parameters with defaults at the top of the component partial:

```erb
<%
  margin_bottom ||= 2
  inverse_background ||= false
  some_other_thing ||= "marmalade"
%>
```

This means that the defaults are easily found and in one place in the component, rather than being spread out across the markup.

The `||=` assignment operator is a shorthand for:

```ruby
value = value ? value : default_value
```

So when a falsey value needs to be passed in it can't override the default - so a parameter which is `true` by default can't be listed at the top of the component.

Because it's not declared at the top of the partial, a check needs to be done before the variable is used. This usually means that `local_assigns.include?(:variable_name)` is used. If the variable was declared with `||=` then this wouldn't need to be used.

**For these reasons, should a convention be added to avoid `true` as a default value for a parameter in components?**

There may be components that have a default that seems to require `true` as a default - for example, a component that has a border visible by default. This could have a `show_border` parameter that is true - but flipping the name round and having an `omit_border` that defaults to `false` gives the same end result without needing the default to be `true`.

[1]: https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/search/stop_the_label_appearing_inline

communityIssues.title: Translation fallback approach needs to be confirmed and applied
communityIssues.body:
Applications sometimes call components when the page is in a translated state. When this happens they are expected to supply the translated string to the component. The component may also augment this with strings that are internally translated, for example dates or fixed elements of the component.

We need to be able to handle what happens when either of these strings are not available in the desired language.

GOV.UK frontenders discussed this today and propose the following mechanism: 

_Since only the application can know if it has had to fall back and is supplying English, we should implement a mechanism to pass this information to the components. The component should respond to this parameter by applying lang=en to the container element so that the likes of search engines and assistive technology can recognise that the component is in English, and by using the English strings for any copy it supplies. We should present the whole component in English to avoid having to mix and match different elements within it and apply further lang attributes._ 

This does not address what to do if the content for the component is passed in the foreign language but the elements of the component don't have translations for the relevant language. In this case we should not apply the lang=en to the wrapper as we will not be changing the content back into English - this would be impossible for dynamic content. We should make best efforts to ensure we have all component strings translated to all supported languages to avoid that, but ideally when that is not possible we should label the individual component elements with lang=en where we cannot translate them. The downside of this approach is there would potentially be a lot of clutter with the language switching back and forth.

backlog.title: Card
backlog.body:
What
Panels of structured content (eg. image, title, description, link), typically organised in rows or grids:
Example 1: Home Office

Example 2: HMRC Tax Platform

Example 3: GOV.UK Notify

Example 4: GOV.UK Home page

Why
Versions of this pattern are already being used in various government services (see examples above).
HMRC have some evidence that adopting this pattern has improved the usability of their tax platform.
This specific component doesn't exist, but it's possible that it could be build from GOV.UK Frontend styles and the panel component.
Anything else
Cards: Home Office design system
Cards: HMRC Design Patterns
Recommendations
This proposal was reviewed by a panel of designers from GDS, DVLA, HMRC, DWP and Home Office on 15 Feb 2018.
The panel agreed that the pattern should be included in the GOV.UK Design System with the following recommendations.
Guidance
There were concerns that cards are often used to compensate for poor information hierarchy or content design.
Contributors to this pattern should establish what user needs the pattern is designed to meet and write appropriate guidance explaining when to use, and not to use, the pattern.
Design
Cards are already being used in many government services, but quite inconsistently. When used appropriately, cards are a good way of chunking up related content, data and links. They can also be used to highlight content on a page.
A consistent style and structure for cards should be established. A number of variants should be provided, with guidance for their appropriate use.
Accessibility
Close attention should be paid to the accessibility of the pattern, in particular colour contrast and the affordance of links.
Component or pattern
Consider whether Cards should be developed as a new component, or as a pattern built from existing styes and components.

communityIssues.title: CLS on image elements missing explicit width and height
communityIssues.body:
We have a number of images using the [figure component](https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/figure) that currently lack width and height attributes. 

### Background

SpeedCurve originally flagged historic people images for lacking explicit width and height dimensions. Without these attributes, browsers cannot calculate the image's aspect ratio before the asset finishes downloading. This causes the page layout to jump once the image loads, resulting in poor Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) scores.

### Example pages with images missing height/width

https://www.gov.uk/guidance/notify-the-defence-accident-investigation-branch
https://www.gov.uk/government/case-studies/out-of-syria-back-into-school
https://www.gov.uk/government/how-government-works
https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/jacqui-smith-speech-at-parliamentary-reception-for-worldskills-uk
https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/armenia

### Relevant links 

Historic people pages PR: https://github.com/alphagov/collections/pull/4708
Related commit setting default height and width on [Image Card](https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/image_card): https://github.com/alphagov/govuk_publishing_components/commit/86450d6066fe7e5aa8fd220e93c2319de2730b62
Responsive images: https://web.dev/learn/design/responsive-images

### Proposed solution 

Where possible (e.g. decorative images), pass width and height attributes to the figure component so browsers can calculate aspect ratios. We cannot use default dimensions for all travel advice maps as they vary in sizes and this might risk distortion or clipping.

communityIssues.title: Removing borders from (primary) white cards
communityIssues.body:
## Design hypothesis

Our card components currently have grey borders. Research suggests that removing borders may improve visual simplicity and reduce cognitive load based on minimalist design principles. For an NHS service, creating a calm, reassuring interface is particularly important for users who may be accessing health information during stressful situations.

**If we** remove the grey borders from our card components 

**Then** users will experience reduced visual clutter, improved content focus, a calmer emotional state, and more efficient information processing across multiple cards

backlog.title: Support for data saving mode
backlog.body:
What
Modern browsers are starting to come bundled with a save data mode, whereby a user can tell a website that, if possible limit the amount of data sent to the device. This is achieved by the browser sending the Save-Data header to the server. The server can then provide modified assets based on this.
Why
One of the more obvious examples of where this could be used is with our webfonts. When save data mode is enabled it would be good to stop the browser requesting the webfonts and fallback to Arial. This can be done by providing a different CSS font stack. This would remove approximately 123 KB of data for v1 fonts, and 65 KB for v2 fonts.
Now this may not sound like a huge amount but it makes quite a difference, especially on low spec devices on a poor connection. I created a prototype to display the difference it has on the GOV.UK homepage:

In the above image we see a Moto G4 on a 3G Fast connection. With Data saving mode text is displayed a full 500ms quicker.

We also see an overall improvement in visual progress, as seen in the graph above. The full results of these tests can be seen here.
I've written about a solution that uses the currently supported JavaScript API here. Browser support can be found here. Example code:
<script>if ("connection" in navigator) {if (navigator.connection.saveData === true) {document.body.className = ((document.body.className) ? document.body.className + ' js-save-data' : 'js-save-data');}}</script>
But there are plans to introduce this functionality within CSS Media queries too:
@media (prefers-reduced-data: no-preference) {....}
The specification for this can be found here. An open bug for FF can be found here. It would be worth investigating the overall support and the timeline for browsers.
We should look to see if we can capture data from users (CDN logs), as to the presence of the Save-Data header. It's also worth nothing that organisations like the BBC are already examining this header and seeing how they can use it to improve user experience.

ourIssues.title: Explore how emerging technologies could improve accessibility
ourIssues.body:
## What
**Timeline:** Ongoing, as opportunities arise
**Priority level:** 6 – what is good to do, without adding risk to the priorities above
**Category:** Areas the team is best-positioned to handle

### Potential tasks

- Research new assistive technology
- Research new browser, operating system and CSS features
- Avoid pursuing emerging technologies that lack evidence of real-world use or benefit for disabled people

## Why
As the technology we use to deliver accessible services advances, these new technologies may offer new ways to improve on accessibility. Conversely, if technology advances and we don't work to keep up, we may find our styles, components and patterns becoming out of synch and less accessible over time.

Areas that are of particular interest for exploration include:
- Updates to assistive technologies we already test with or support
- Updates to browsers we already test with or support
- Updates to operating systems that have an impact on accessibility tools or features
- New tools for accessibility testing, either manual or automated

Areas we want to be cautious around include:
- Emerging technologies that promote themselves as being assistive technologies, but don't have evidence of real-world benefit or use for disabled people
- New or updated browsers or browser features that aren't within the scope of our browser support
- Any technology which out-of-the-box is less accessible than current options

## Who needs to work on this
Developers, accessibility specialist

## Who needs to review this
Product and delivery managers, developers

## Setup tasks

- [ ] Thing to do

ourIssues.body:
## What

## Epic lead

\~@dav-idc~ @stevenjmesser

## Why

WCAG 2.2 is set to be published in 2023.

We plan to release a version of the GOV.UK Frontend library that has styles, components and patterns which meet WCAG 2.2. Our goal is to release that around 6 months after WCAG 2.2 is officially published.

Everyone: developers, interaction designers, user researcher, accessibility specialist, content designers, product manager.

Inside the team: tech leads and accessibility specialist.

communityIssues.title: Multi-file upload component: Adoption questions for Bulk Upload service
communityIssues.body:
## Context

We are building a bulk upload feature for our service. We've been looking at the [multi-file upload component](https://github.com/ministryofjustice/moj-frontend/tree/main/src/moj/components/multi-file-upload) as our design starting point.

We've built a technical proof of concept in React that demonstrates multi-file upload feasibility, and we now need to bring this into a GDS-compliant, user-tested design prototype. We'd like to understand the component's current status and capabilities before we proceed.

## Our use case

- **Users:** Internal operations managers
- **Action:** Upload up to 10 documents at once
- **File types:** PDF, JPEG, PNG (additional file types: xlsx, docs, msg)
- **Max file size:** 1GB (PDF), 100MB (images)
- **Key requirement:** Per-file status reporting (success/fail with reason) and error recovery

## Questions
### 1. Component maturity and approval status

Is the multi-file upload component considered production-ready and approved for use in live government services? We noticed the last commit was approximately 11 months ago — is this because it's stable, or is active development paused?

### 2. Per-file error handling

Does the component (or a newer unreleased version) support per-file error states? Specifically, we need to handle:

- File too large (exceeds size limit)
- Wrong file type (not in accepted list)
- Virus detected (failed scanning)
- Duplicate file warning (filename already exists in the collection)
- Network timeout / upload failure
- **Partial batch success** (e.g., 8 of 10 files succeed, 2 fail with individual reasons)

Are any of these handled out of the box, or would we need to extend the component?

### 3. GOV.UK Prototype Kit compatibility

Is there a Prototype Kit-compatible version of this component? We need to present designs at a Service review and ideally want to use the Prototype Kit for our interactive prototype. If not, is Figma + the component's HTML/CSS sufficient for demonstration purposes?

### 4. Confirmation step

Our governance requires users to review their file selection and confirm before upload begins (to prevent accidental wrong uploads). Does the component support an intermediate confirmation step between file selection and upload initiation?

### 5. Additional patterns

Does the MoJ Design System have documented patterns for:
- Upload progress indicators (per-file)
- Recovery flows when some files in a batch fail
- Post-upload metadata assignment (user categorises files after they've uploaded)

### 6. Known limitations or alternatives

Are there any known limitations, planned deprecation, or alternative components we should consider? We're aware the component doesn't currently support:
- Folder structure retention
- Custom confirmation dialogs
- Bad file type preview/rejection before upload

Are any of these on the roadmap?

## Our timeline

We're targeting a release in soon. Any guidance — even a quick pointer to the right documentation or person — would be hugely appreciated.

## Happy to contribute back

If we extend the component for our use case (error states, confirmation step), we'd be happy to contribute those patterns back to the MoJ Design System if that would be useful.

**Component:** `src/moj/components/multi-file-upload`

communityIssues.title: Improve and formalise Archiving process
communityIssues.body:
## What

Within the MOJ design system we currently have 8 Archived components. Components are usually archived due to becoming redundant, most commonly as the Gov.uk design system now contains a component that meets the need of the Archived components. The number of archived components is likely to increase over time as the Gov.uk design system adds more components. 

## Why

While we currently have an archived section in the documentation site we don't formally deprecate any designs or code as part of the archiving process. This means product teams across MOJ are free to continue using the components or even select them as a new component for their service. We need to develop a formal process to formally archive and deprecate old MOJ components. To do this we will need to review how and why teams are continuing to use archived components and develop a process to inform teams components are no longer fully supported and they should transition away from using them. 
We do not track the usage of archived components in the analytic dashboard so we do not understand the scale of the problem 

## Who needs to be involved

- Business Analyst
- User Researcher

Supported by:
- Interaction Designer
- Content Designer
- Developer
- Delivery Manager
- Product Manager


## Done

- [ ] BA and UR have completed research and analysis to document the current Archive process 
- [ ] We understand why teams are continuing to use archived components 
- [ ] We have established and agreed a checklist to confirm a component is to be archived 
- [ ] we have worked with product teams to establish reasonable timelines for deprecation 
- [ ] We have developed a communications strategy for informing teams 
- [ ] We have agreed where Archived components are to sit (Currently in the Design system)
- [ ] we can monitor the use of archived components?
- [ ] We have a fully developed and agreed formal archiving process that is easy to understand and manage

communityIssues.title: Images don't appear when using the Prototype Kit
communityIssues.body:
### Description

When using moj-frontend with the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, remote images are not correctly loaded (on Filter a liist, Timeline, and Button menu). This is because the generated path (`/assets/images/...`) is not served by the Prototype Kit. Instead, the correct path is `$govuk-extensions-url-context + "/%40ministryofjustice%2Ffrontend/moj/assets/"` (NB: symbols in NPM package name must be URL-encoded).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a prototype (`npx govuk-prototype-kit@latest create`)
2. Install moj-frontend (`npm install @ministryofjustice/frontend --save`)
3. Add a component that uses an image, such as "Filter a list"
4. Run the prototype (`npm run dev`)

**Expected behaviour:** Images should be loaded from remote paths

**Actual behaviour:** The image requests 404 and aren't loaded

**Reproduces how often:** 100%

### Versions

Prototype Kit: 13.16.0
moj-frontend: 2.0.0

### Additional Information

This could be fixed by updating [the Sass](https://github.com/ministryofjustice/moj-frontend/blob/ca8f3908f9390a835303a12c663c3ae2e241d365/src/moj/settings/_assets.scss#L6) to:
```scss
$moj-assets-path: if(
  $govuk-prototype-kit-major-version > 12,
  $govuk-extensions-url-context + "/%40ministryofjustice%2Ffrontend/moj/assets/",
  "/assets/"
) !default;
```

But doing so in the distributed file might have unintended side effects, so it would be preferable to provide a separate entrypoint for prototypes.

ourIssues.title: Support standard .html/.text input for `caption` on `table` component
ourIssues.body:
## Related component

Yes, https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/table/

## Context

Currently the `caption` argument in the nunjucks macro only takes a string, not the more standard "object with `html` and `text` options". This means users may not be able to pass through html they may need to unless they look into the implementation and find that html is possible to enter, but even then, users need to `| safe` the input themselves. This is unintuitive, and many other arguments in other macros have this object input pattern, rather than just a straight string.

## Alternatives

Yes, passing in a string I have put through the `safe` filter myself.

## Additional information (if applicable)

I wanted to do this myself recently as a result of an accessibility audit, so this isn't just a hypothetical, it's a real need.
I undertook making this change with AI assistance in my fork of govuk-frontend here https://github.com/ReedSoftware/govuk-frontend/pull/1 - after some talk with the GDS team, I'm aware that your stance on AI generated PRs isn't set yet, so I'm happy to leave it as a talking point or reference, but also happy to raise a PR against this change if you did decide you wanted it!

There was also some talk on the GDS channel in x-gov slack about this with @romaricpascal @selfthinker - thank you for your inputs here so far.

ourIssues.title: Button component without margin overhangs by 2px
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

The button component uses a 2px box shadow to provide a visual bottom border. This is used primarily instead of an actual bottom border because the other borders are already defined and this would cause a bevelling issue between the bottom and left/right borders. This means that the button component 'overhangs' by 2px at the bottom.

By default the button component has a margin bottom of 32px, which accounts for this 2px and then adds spacing in line with the spacing scale. However on GOV.UK we use the button component without bottom margin in our search filters, where it is supposed to line up with the bottom of a wrapping element. Due to this 2px of box shadow it doesn't, and we have to insert 2px of padding somewhere to account for this.

This is a very small thing, but if there were a way of preserving the look of the button while allowing it to not have this 2px of overhanging box shadow it would make integrating the button component into edge case scenarios like this a little easier.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Normal button appearance:

![Normal button appearance with margin beneath](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fa0aa19-b2de-458a-a989-d9c462484e67)

Button with zero margin applied to the bottom (note 2px overlap with containing element, highlighted):

![Button inside a highlighted form element showing 2px overlap with container when margin removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76ebdc8f-353e-4036-80c0-6918477cc91a)

Use of button in GOV.UK search (mobile view) at bottom of containing element, note slight overlap/misalign with grey left border of container:

ourIssues.title: Why do checkboxes and radios have transparent backgrounds?
ourIssues.body:
The following came from a question I asked on the design system slack channel.
https://ukgovernmentdigital.slack.com/archives/C6DMEH5R6/p1572279335253200

**TLDR:** checkboxes and radios have transparent backgrounds. This means they don't stand out visually against non white panels as text input elements do.

From thread:
---------
does anyone know why the checkboxes (and I assume radio buttons) have transparent backgrounds? Rather than a white background (which would probably be the default browser rendering of a standard checkbox).
**GOV checkbox (with transparent background):**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23551105/67845990-5e27a280-faf8-11e9-8e33-0bb7e1f6b0b5.png)
**Default checkbox (without GOV styling):**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23551105/67846092-86af9c80-faf8-11e9-8571-995a80aa3825.png)

**Anon 1:** 
I suspect that’s because they’re custom rendered rather than native checkboxes, and we want to support users who change their text and background colours.

11 replies

**Anon 2:**
Hi Dave,
This decision pre-dates the design system so I'll need to do a bit of digging to see if we can find out why - but my guess is something along the lines of what **Anon 1** said. Will come back to you.
Have you seen any problems around this, or are you just wondering?
After some investigation - it appears that his is the pertinent commit: https://github.com/alphagov/govuk_elements/commit/4972b81697fbf5b9ac12a211010c623e625ab3ab

**Dave Haigh**
I am looking at using small checkboxes as a filter for a list. The filters are located on a light grey panel (similar to the call to action blocks on GOV.UK guidance pages). As you can see in the screenshot the checkbox doesn’t stand out well as the background is transparent.

Im not sure on the answer to this but… should the scenario be:
- If user HAS NOT specified any browser background colour then they should be white;
- Else if user HAS a specified background colour in certain modes then they should be either transparent or that colour (when in that mode)
1. Is the above correct?
2. Is it possible?
3.Also, some other elements do not respect user specified background colours such as text inputs (they’re always white). Why are only the checks and radios transparent?

i’ve specified my background colour to be red (in any mode) in this screenshot:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/23551105/67846236-c5455700-faf8-11e9-868f-432708c3a31f.png)

**Anon 3**
I don’t really have a good answer for you other than that the radios and checkboxes in the Design System are based on those introduced in Elements back in 2016 by people that no longer work here. As **Anon 2** said, we don’t have the context of every historical decision. We could definitely look at changing that behaviour, but we’d need to test thoroughly to make sure they still work in all of these sorts of scenarios.

communityIssues.title: Remove moment.js and replace with native Date methods
communityIssues.body:
## What

Remove usage of `moment.js` throughout the codebase, specifically within Nunjucks date filters. Replace it with native JavaScript `Date` methods.

Update any documentation and type annotations accordingly.

## Why

`moment.js` is a legacy dependency and no longer recommended for modern JavaScript projects. It's large in size, no longer actively developed.

Removing it:
- Reduces bundle size
- Improves maintainability
- Aligns with current best practices
- Removes the need for a peer dependency

## Who needs to be involved

- [x] Developer
- [ ] Content Designer (if any date-related text needs revisiting)
- [ ] Interaction Designer (if any formatting affects UI/UX)
- [ ] Accessibility Specialist (to ensure date formatting remains readable)
- [ ] Delivery Manager (for visibility)
- [ ] Design System Lead (for awareness if this affects shared filters)

## Done

- All usages of `moment.js` have been removed
- Native `Date` methods are used instead
- Tests and existing functionality verified to work as expected
- `moment` has been removed from both `dependencies` and `peerDependencies`
- Pull request is reviewed and merged

```js
Subject: [PATCH] refactor: remove moment.js and replace with native Date methods
---
Index: src/moj/filters/all.js
IDEA additional info:
Subsystem: com.intellij.openapi.diff.impl.patch.CharsetEP
<+>UTF-8
===================================================================
diff --git a/src/moj/filters/all.js b/src/moj/filters/all.js
--- a/src/moj/filters/all.js	(revision baadd230d8985b68f25b040095a166c39586e801)
+++ b/src/moj/filters/all.js	(date 1744632178490)
@@ -1,6 +1,14 @@
-const moment = require('moment')
-
 module.exports = function () {
+  /**
+   * Pads a number to 2 digits with a leading zero if needed
+   *
+   * @param {number} n - The number to pad
+   * @returns {string} - The padded string
+   */
+  function pad2(n) {
+    return n < 10 ? `0${n}` : `${n}`
+  }
+
   /**
    * Date filter for use in Nunjucks
    * Outputs: 01/01/1970
@@ -9,11 +17,33 @@
    * ```njk
    * {{ params.date | date("DD/MM/YYYY") }}
    * ```
-   * @param {MomentInput} timestamp
+   * @param {Date | string | number} timestamp
    * @param {string} format
    */
   function date(timestamp, format) {
-    return moment(timestamp).format(format)
+    const dateObj = new Date(timestamp)
+    const day = pad2(dateObj.getDate())
+    const month = pad2(dateObj.getMonth() + 1)
+    const year = String(dateObj.getFullYear())
+
+    switch (format) {
+      case 'DD/MM/YYYY':
+        return `${day}/${month}/${year}`
+      case 'D MMMM YYYY':
+        return dateObj.toLocaleDateString('en-GB', {
+          day: 'numeric',
+          month: 'long',
+          year: 'numeric'
+        })
+      case 'D MMM YYYY':
+        return dateObj.toLocaleDateString('en-GB', {
+          day: 'numeric',
+          month: 'short',
+          year: 'numeric'
+        })
+      default:
+        return dateObj.toString()
+    }
   }
 
   /* ------------------------------------------------------------------
@@ -21,28 +51,33 @@
   ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
 
   /**
-   * @param {MomentInput} timestamp
+   * @param {Date | string | number} timestamp
    */
   function govDate(timestamp) {
-    return moment(timestamp).format('D MMMM YYYY')

   }

     }

@@ -83,7 +118,3 @@

communityIssues.title: Images don't appear when using the Prototype Kit
communityIssues.body:
### Description

When using moj-frontend with the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, remote images are not correctly loaded (on Filter a liist, Timeline, and Button menu). This is because the generated path (`/assets/images/...`) is not served by the Prototype Kit. Instead, the correct path is `$govuk-extensions-url-context + "/%40ministryofjustice%2Ffrontend/moj/assets/"` (NB: symbols in NPM package name must be URL-encoded).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a prototype (`npx govuk-prototype-kit@latest create`)
2. Install moj-frontend (`npm install @ministryofjustice/frontend --save`)
3. Add a component that uses an image, such as "Filter a list"
4. Run the prototype (`npm run dev`)

**Expected behaviour:** Images should be loaded from remote paths

**Actual behaviour:** The image requests 404 and aren't loaded

**Reproduces how often:** 100%

### Versions

Prototype Kit: 13.16.0
moj-frontend: 2.0.0

### Additional Information

This could be fixed by updating [the Sass](https://github.com/ministryofjustice/moj-frontend/blob/ca8f3908f9390a835303a12c663c3ae2e241d365/src/moj/settings/_assets.scss#L6) to:
```scss
$moj-assets-path: if(
  $govuk-prototype-kit-major-version > 12,
  $govuk-extensions-url-context + "/%40ministryofjustice%2Ffrontend/moj/assets/",
  "/assets/"
) !default;
```

But doing so in the distributed file might have unintended side effects, so it would be preferable to provide a separate entrypoint for prototypes.

communityIssues.title: Clicking on checkbox labels on dynamic filter component causes the parent container to briefly get focus
communityIssues.body:
### Description

My service is using the [filter a list pattern](https://moj-design-system.herokuapp.com/patterns/filter-a-list).

If a user clicks on a label for a checkbox, a border is drawn around the filter component whilst their mouse is down.

![filter-a-list-focus-bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2204224/89197196-43acb900-d5a3-11ea-89d8-71ea5da1bc02.gif)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the [filter a list pattern](https://moj-design-system.herokuapp.com/patterns/filter-a-list)
2. Using a mouse, click on the label for a checkbox (not the checkbox itself)
3. Observe a border appear around the wider filter.

**Expected behaviour:**

No border should appear

**Actual behaviour:** 

Border appears.

**Reproduces how often:** 
Always

### Additional Information

After a little debugging, the issue seems to be because the filter is given `tabindex=-1` so that it can be focused when it's opened as a popover on the mobile view. [This stackoverflow issue](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49662769/focus-within-styles-flash-when-clicking-an-input-label) covers a similar scenario.

Essentially, when a user clicks on the label, focus moves away from wherever it was, and _up_ to the next focusable thing - which in this case is the component container. When the mouse is released, the checkbox itself receives focus.

One solution is to make the labels focusable, and to remove their focus styles - this would 'appear' to work - though feels a bit hacky.

On my service I think I may disable focus styles entirely on the filter component - at least on the desktop view. Users can't tab in to the component, so showing visible focus doesn't seem to be essential.

backlog.title: GOV.UK Design System as an agent skill for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
backlog.body:
I've packaged the Design System as an open source agent skill so coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) use it properly instead of from memory: https://github.com/chrisjohnleah/govuk-design-system-skill
It is generated from govuk-frontend 6.5.1, this repo and govuk-frontend-docs. Every component page carries the guidance, the macro options table and the exact HTML each example renders to, plus all 35 patterns and 13 styles. A single CHOOSING file compiles every "when to use" and "when not to use" so the agent picks the right component before it writes any markup.
The bit I cared most about: without the skill, an agent building a page for a charity used the crown, the GOV.UK header and GDS Transport. With it, the agent read "Using GOV.UK Frontend without GOV.UK branding" first and switched to the Generic header, a font override and its own icons. The skill leads with that decision.
Install: npx skills add chrisjohnleah/govuk-design-system-skill
A script regenerates everything from upstream, so it can track releases rather than drift.
Not affiliated with GDS. Happy to change anything the team would rather I did differently, especially around how the licensing of the crown and typeface is worded.

backlog.title: Suggested new component - Side menu
backlog.body:
What

Give a brief description of the style, component or pattern you want to propose.

Context:
We are in the final stages of building an e-learning service using the GDS design system. We have completed numerous rounds of user testing and already gone through one Alpha and Beta Assessment.
What:
A right-hand sidebar navigation menu which allows users to easily see their progression through a course and be able to navigate back and forth through chapters.
Current version

In-situ

Iterations from user testing

Why

Explain why you think this should be added to the GOV.UK Design System.

In our alpha assessment, we were challenged to explore if there was a user need to see their progression through the course and also to be able to navigate back and forth through the chapters. We tested various variations of a sidebar navigation similar to those found in lots of e-learning platforms. During testing, we found that some users naturally used the sidebar to return to topics earlier in the course and used it to be aware of their progression and estimate their completion time.
Design-wise, we didn’t want to reinvent the wheel so we built on existing sidebar navigation patterns from GOV.UK publishing such as the contents list on the publishing service (https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/contents_list) and the related content sidebar on many start pages. We iterated the design several times to make it simple and accessible. For instance, we made some headers in the sidebar visually hidden so they would give context to screen reader users whilst avoiding confusion for sighted users who had initially struggled with the previous design.


What evidence do you have that it's needed by multiple services across government?


In the our beta assessment, we were praised on our work developing this pattern and asked to play it back into the community:
‘the team has validated the user need to track progress within training modules, has designed a pattern that is working for their beta users, and is planning to continue iterating this pattern - the panel would encourage the team to share this pattern and research findings with the design system community’


What evidence do you have that it meets the needs of the users of those services?


We have tested and validated this component in several rounds of qual research with 5-10 people in each round, and in Private Beta testing with over 1200 people (with quant showing that people successfully use this when required, and qual feedback only positive and no negative on the latest version).
Our user testing so far has validated the need for this component and as mentioned has been praised so far by assessors. But we would love to share it with the community to get a wider perspective and possible use cases.


Have you checked that it doesn't already exist in the GOV.UK Design System?


Yes
Anything else

Include links to any examples, research or code to support your proposal, if available.

backlog.title: Support for data saving mode
backlog.body:
What
Modern browsers are starting to come bundled with a save data mode, whereby a user can tell a website that, if possible limit the amount of data sent to the device. This is achieved by the browser sending the Save-Data header to the server. The server can then provide modified assets based on this.
Why
One of the more obvious examples of where this could be used is with our webfonts. When save data mode is enabled it would be good to stop the browser requesting the webfonts and fallback to Arial. This can be done by providing a different CSS font stack. This would remove approximately 123 KB of data for v1 fonts, and 65 KB for v2 fonts.
Now this may not sound like a huge amount but it makes quite a difference, especially on low spec devices on a poor connection. I created a prototype to display the difference it has on the GOV.UK homepage:

In the above image we see a Moto G4 on a 3G Fast connection. With Data saving mode text is displayed a full 500ms quicker.

We also see an overall improvement in visual progress, as seen in the graph above. The full results of these tests can be seen here.
I've written about a solution that uses the currently supported JavaScript API here. Browser support can be found here. Example code:
<script>if ("connection" in navigator) {if (navigator.connection.saveData === true) {document.body.className = ((document.body.className) ? document.body.className + ' js-save-data' : 'js-save-data');}}</script>
But there are plans to introduce this functionality within CSS Media queries too:
@media (prefers-reduced-data: no-preference) {....}
The specification for this can be found here. An open bug for FF can be found here. It would be worth investigating the overall support and the timeline for browsers.
We should look to see if we can capture data from users (CDN logs), as to the presence of the Save-Data header. It's also worth nothing that organisations like the BBC are already examining this header and seeing how they can use it to improve user experience.

ourIssues.title: Investigate ways to deliver GOV.UK logo, footer crown and OGL logo as SVG files rather than inline
ourIssues.body:
## Related component

Header and footer

## Context

Off the back of https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/6032, I wondered if you had considered changing the way the header logo and footer crown are displayed so that they use the same method as the footer crest (https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/5872), with an .svg file as a `mask-image` in CSS rather than inlining the SVG. 

This would make fixes and updates to the logo easier to roll out as they could be handled entirely as image asset and Sass changes rather than requiring developers to manually update the SVG. It would also save about 4kb of page weight on most requests as the SVG file could be cached. 

The cyan dot can be done by making the background a `linear-gradient` with hard stops between cyan and `currentColor` (to preserve forced colour compatibility). The footer crown could even reuse the same SVG file as the header logo, as the mask image can be cropped in CSS.

As in https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/5872, we could fall back to displaying the SVG as a `background-image` for Edge 17 compatibility.

I've very quickly tested that this would work as expected - I'm happy to tidy it up into a draft PR if you think it's worth pursuing.

ourIssues.title: How to adapt footer for non-GOV.UK services
ourIssues.body:
## Related component

[GOV.UK footer](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/footer/)


## Context

The new rebranded footer has the crown logo at the top of it.
But the crown shouldn't be used in non-GOV.UK services, neither in the header nor the footer.

Before this change non-GOV.UK services had to change the header but not the footer, now they also have to change the footer. But we don't have any guidance for it.

We should at least add guidance similar to what we say in the ['When to use this component' section for the GOV.UK header component](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/header/#when-to-use-this-component).

ourIssues.title: Consider adding alternative text for crown and crest
ourIssues.body:
## What

Think about alternative text for the crown in the header and the footer and the crest in the footer.
We currently don't have any alternative text to describe or even mention the crown or the crest. 

The current alternative texts (not necessarily value for `alt` parameter) are:

* The crown in the header includes the word mark. It is linked and leads to the homepage. It's an`<svg>` with an `aria-label` of "GOV.UK".
* The crown in the footer does not include the word mark. It is not linked.  It's an`<svg>` with a `role="presentation". (The crown is not in the footer yet, but it will be soon.)
* The crest in the footer does not include any text (within the image itself, unless you count the motto, which is really too small to see). It is the background image of a link that goes to a National Archives page about the Crown copyright. And that link includes the text "© Crown copyright".

To summarise the alternative texts for those images...

| Image (text approximation) | Alternative text | Is in a link? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 👑 GOV.UK | GOV.UK | yes |
| 👑 |  | no |
| 🛡️ © Crown copyright | © Crown copyright | yes |

## Why

We never describe or reference the images. We should explore if doing that would be valuable to people who cannot see the images (or cannot see them well enough).

We should find out what these images do for people who can see them. And if they do anything important, we should consider those images to be meaningful and add (to) alternative text to describe them.

My (untested) assumptions:
Visually both images give the page a more official look.
They help establishing trust.
They reference something a user might want to be looking for.
And they signal the start and the end of the page.

If that is correct, they should have alternative text that conveys those things.

It's worth noting that this has never been flagged in a WCAG audit. Therefore it might not be a problem and is not an urgent thing to fix.


## Who needs to work on this

Content designer, designer, accessibility specialist, user researcher

## Who needs to review this

The team, and maybe someone from GOV.UK should be involved as well

## Done when

- [ ] Have evidence for meaning of those images to users (either through our own research or someone else's)
- [ ] Decided if those images are meaningful to our users
- [ ] If they are, write alternative text for them and implement it

ourIssues.title: Adjust components to scale with android system font size
ourIssues.body:
## What
Ensure as many of our components as possible are responding when viewing govuk-frontend web pages on android devices and adjusting android's system font size.

## Why
Govuk-frontend web pages should respect accessibility settigns and respond to them as expected.

## Steps to replicate
Tested in chrome on browserstack's Galaxy S23 instance as it's easy to notice the issue due to the device's large font size scale.

1. Go to the settings of the testing device and locate the setting to adjust device font size
2. Increase font size (recommend max in order to visualise issue more clearly)
3. Open a govuk-frontend web page on a browser on an android device eg: [the review app's announcements page](https://govuk-frontend-review.herokuapp.com/full-page-examples/announcements)

Notice that the breadcrumbs have not increased in size. Digging into the runtime styles, you will find that rem values of other elements on the page have adjusted in response to the font size change but the breadcrumbs haven't.

![Android browser showing an announcements page with scaled up font size except for the breadcrumbs element](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/assets/64783893/66ecb7d1-bf9e-459a-987c-8c85176a26b7)

## Notes
### Considerations from the spec
The likely reason this is happening can be found in CSS Mobile Text Size section of the CSS spec, specifically [2.2: Conditions that suppress adjustment](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-size-adjust/#default-adjustment-conditions). This section notes 4 reasons that would suppress text size adjustment. From initial testing, certain components can be 'fixed' by removing their block level positioning rules eg: components that have `display: inline-block`. We should be able to use `inline-block` on components and the text size adjustment not be suppressed. Recommend using the the spec in figuring out a solution.

### Impacted components
- Accordion
- Back link
- Breadcrumbs
- Button, and places consumed
    - Cookie banner buttons
    - Exit this page
- Checkboxes
- Details (not the content)
- File upload
- Some of the footer's links
- Header menu
- Notification banner
- Pagination
- Radios
- Select
- Table
- Tabs
- Tag
- Task list
- Text input, and places consumed
    - Date input
    - Password input

## Who needs to work on this
Developers

## Who needs to review this
Developers

ourIssues.title: Add content to Skip link guidance about problem caused by preservation of fragment identifiers between pages
ourIssues.body:
The skip link component adds a `#main-content` fragment identifier to the current URL. This can persist across pages causing an unexpected jump to the main content area on load. I'd like to add a warning about this to the guidance, along with tips about ways teams could write their code to avoid this. 

## Related component

https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/skip-link/

## Context

This problem has been seen to happen in the following scenario:
- the skip link was used, thereby adding `#main-content` to the current URL
- you leave the page via a successful form submission
- the form doesn't set the `action` attribute and so POSTs to the current URL
- the server uses [the POST -> Redirect -> GET pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post/Redirect/Get) to navigate to the next page

Given all that, the browser will preserve `#main-content` in the new URL[^1] causing the next page to jump to the start of the main content area when it loads.

This was picked up as an issue by the Digital Accessibility Centre (DAC) in a recent audit of GOV.UK Notify[^2], who stated that it failed [the WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) success criteria](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG20/Understanding/focus-order).

Given [the POST -> Redirect -> GET pattern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post/Redirect/Get) is so commonly used in web apps, I think there's some value in making teams aware of this problem and helping them write their code in a way that stops it happening.

## Alternatives

N/A

## Additional information (if applicable)

Suggested changes, to stop the problem occurring are:
- setting the `action` attribute on the `<form>` tag to match the current URL, without `#main-content`
- setting the URL for the next page explicitly using the [Content-Location](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Location) header

## References

[^1]: This is correct behaviour, as defined in [Handling of fragment identifiers in redirected URLs](https://www.w3.org/Protocols/HTTP/Fragment/draft-bos-http-redirect-00.txt)
[^2]: Issue 'ID: DAC_Focus_order_01' on page 19 of [the audit report](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jRkkL3AZj-7Q0uo7yfHUv_JF9q0Ecw6g/view?usp=sharing) (needs a GDS Google account for access)

ourIssues.title: Research making the checkbox and radio button labels full width
ourIssues.body:
## What

Perform research with users as to whether making labels on checkboxes and radio buttons span the width of the container, thus increasing their touch surface, makes it easier to use these controls

## Why

Generally speaking, increasing the target area for a control makes the control easier for users to interact with.

We have some existing precendent for this in Frontend already: 

- Labels for other input types (text inputs, selects, textareas, etc.) are already full width.
- The Accordion activates expand/collapse functionality by tapping anywhere in the section header.
- The Skip Link component, when visible, is activatable by clicking anywhere in the component.

The GOV.UK team has had positive feedback when increasing target sizes for elements on the [homepage](https://insidegovuk.blog.gov.uk/2021/12/13/updating-the-gov-uk-homepage/) and [topic pages](https://insidegovuk.blog.gov.uk/2022/08/08/rolling-out-a-new-design-for-browsing-gov-uk-by-topic/) in the last year.

Various external design systems have full width checkbox and radio labels, some of which are based on or inspired by GOV.UK Frontend and have seemingly made the conscious choice to change it:

- ~~[USWDS](https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/checkbox/)~~ Update: Has since updated to no longer be full-width
- [NICE Design System](https://design-system.nice.org.uk/storybook/?path=/story/foundations-checkbox--default)
- [Transport for West Midlands Design System](https://designsystem.tfwm.org.uk/components/radios/)
- [GOLD Design System](https://gold.designsystemau.org/components/control-input/#checkbox-block) (formerly Australian Government Design System)
- [Atlassian Design System](https://atlassian.design/components/checkbox/examples)

Our inline labels date from the GOV.UK Elements days, and I couldn't immediately find any reason why they were implemented in this way at the time. We have stuck to that precedent in situations where a conflict or bug relating to the label sizing has arisen (e.g. #634).

We should validate our current approach and whether it best meets user needs when compared to alternative approaches.

## Assumptions

We've [previously found that users don't tend to click on checkbox or radio button labels](https://designnotes.blog.gov.uk/2016/11/30/weve-updated-the-radios-and-checkboxes-on-gov-uk/), even if they're styled to appear interactible. It could be assumed that the same applies here (if not moreso, as there isn't any visual indicator that interaction is possible). 

As a larger area of the screen will activate a checkbox/radio, there may be an increase in the number of accidental form inputs being made.

A seemingly 'empty' part of the page affecting a nearby input may be unexpected and cause confusion to users unless some other hint is present (e.g. a hover state). 

## Timebox
TBD

## Who is working on this?

Spike lead: TBD

Spike buddy: TBD

## Questions to answer

- [ ] Is there a tangible benefit to checkbox and radio button labels always being full width?
- [ ] Is there a tangible benefit to checkbox and radio button labels being full width in certain situations (e.g. on narrow screens)? 
- [ ] Are full width labels more likely to result in accidental and unwanted inputs?
- [ ] Is having a visually 'empty' area of the screen interactive unexpected or a source of confusion?

## Done when

- [ ] A review or prototype is produced with the modified checkbox/radio styles.
- [ ] User research has been carried out to see how these changes perform with users.
- [ ] Findings have been reviewed and shared with the team.
- [ ] Any follow up issues or actions have been written up.

ourIssues.title: Make it possible to persist tab state
ourIssues.body:
## What

Make it possible to persist the selected tab in a set of tabs so that when the user returns to the page the tab they were looking at is restored, where it makes sense to do so.

This might be better managed either partially or completely on the server side (e.g. by pre-selecting the right tab at render time) in which case we should consider writing guidance on how to do this well instead.

## Why

When the tabs interface is used as part of an interface where the user might leave the page to perform an action before returning to the original screen (for example, in a case working system), it'd be useful to be able to persist the tab that they were looking at before.

The tab state is currently preserved in navigation through the use of a fragment, but as [the fragment is not included in the referer header](https://greenbytes.de/tech/webdav/rfc2616.html#rfc.section.14.36) it's non-trivial to redirect back to it.

In #1961 a user reported an issue with the tabs 'flickering' which was caused by a delay whilst their own state-preservation mechanism kicked in. Building this functionality into the component would help with this, and avoid teams having to do it themselves.

ourIssues.title: Exit this page: Possibly note the `Clear-Site-Data` header
ourIssues.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/discussions/2932
Originally posted by **craigfrancis** July 9, 2023 Under the heading "Consider what to do with user session data", it might be worth noting that **some** websites might want to use the `Clear-Site-Data` header ([Specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/clear-site-data/), [MDN Article](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Clear-Site-Data)). This header helps if the user forgot to use Private Browsing Mode, and isn't familiar with clearing their browsing data (which in itself can be suspicious). This header does not clear the browsers history (as websites cannot/should-not be able to do this); but it does leave less traces of the website on the users computer (cookies, caches, localStorage, service workers, etc), which shows greater engagement with the website, and could include an active session showing a username and account details. I believe the Exit This Page link will need to use a redirect (i.e. go to a URL on the current website, which sets this header, and a Location header for the redirect). This will increase the loading time for the destination page, but loading time is always going to be a problem (and why a loading overlay is essential, because even a basic link to another website can take many seconds to begin loading - ref mobile phones with a poor connection, slow laptops running a virus checker, etc).

When you activate the main nav buttons they even visibly open the sub menu that shouldn't be reachable in the desktop view. Those buttons can also be explored by touch. Screenshot of the hidden "Get started" button being highlighted and activated with the "Get started" sub menu open underneath the service nav: This was first discovered as part of an [audit of the Brand Guidelines website](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-brand-guidelines/issues/138), which copies the Design System website functionality. ## Steps to reproduce the issue 1. Double tap one of the buttons to (wrongly) open the mobile menu underneath ## Actual vs expected behaviour At step 3 you shouldn't be able to access those hidden buttons. At step 4 you shouldn't be able to open the mobile menu when it desktop view. ## Environment (where applicable) - Operating system: iPadOS 18.6 - Browser: Safari - Browser version: (not sure) I don't have a recent enough iOS version to see if it happens on current iOS as well. But I can confirm it does **not** happen with: * VO on iPadOS 15.8.3 * latest VO on macOS * latest TalkBack on Android * latest NVDA on Windows * latest JAWS on Windows That means it might well be due to a bug in iPadOS (and maybe iOS). And it would be worth isolating the exact problem.

ourIssues.title: Notification component uses `govuk-brand-colour` for border colour
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

We've set our `$govuk-brand-colour` to MHCLG's teal (#00625E) and it's done the thing we expected, which is: change the header/footer border colour. But it's also changed the colour of the border on the notification component, which our designers don't like - they expected it to stay as the standard blue.

Is this intentional/expected? I can see that the header component has a separate variable, govuk-header-border-colour that is set to govuk-brand-colour - but we can't override the header border color directly because it doesn't respect a default value.

Is it expected that our notification banners should match the brand colour? To our designers it feels odd, and I can imagine if your department's colour is red and now all your notification banners are red, that would also feel odd/undesirable?

See also reference to slack thread where this was first raised (while history exists): https://ukgovernmentdigital.slack.com/archives/C6DMEH5R6/p1757328829381619. Raising/duplicating here just so I have a permalink I can reference in code while we're using a temporary workaround.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Set `govuk-brand-colour` to a non-default value.
2. Render a notification banner component

## Actual vs expected behaviour

See that the border colour changes to the value you set for govuk-brand-colour, rather than the "default" blue.

communityIssues.title: Some tables in govspeak are hard to navigate
communityIssues.body:
We're still investigating this issue but here are some initial thoughts.

## Problem

Content publishers are using govspeak tables and in some cases the data is too tall or too wide (or both) for the page. This is hard to navigate and causes some specific further problems:

- scrollbars on the bottom of tables aren't always visible or easy to get hold of (because they're so thin)
- if the table is too wide and too tall, users can't easily find the scrollbar along the bottom of the table, having to scroll a lot to get to it
- there's a further orientation issue with this - if you have to scroll many pages to move the table across, then back up again to read

Some example pages (thanks to @selfthinker for supplying many of these):

- [page with a long table](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/dbs-privacy-policies/cookies-policy)
- [page with a reeeally long table](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/skilled-worker-visa-eligible-occupations/skilled-worker-visa-eligible-occupations-and-codes)
- [page with a wide (and tall) table](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/skilled-worker-visa-going-rates-for-eligible-occupations/skilled-worker-visa-going-rates-for-eligible-occupation-codes)
- [table used for layout, a calculation formula](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/16-to-19-funding-allocations-supporting-documents-for-2022-to-2023/16-to-19-further-education-allocation-calculation-toolkit-2022-to-2023--2)

- [table used as a list](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/an-in-depth-review-of-fire-related-fatalities-and-severe-casualties-in-england-2010-to-201819/an-in-depth-review-of-fire-related-fatalities-and-severe-casualties-in-england-201011-to-201819#appendix-b)
