backlog.title: Contribution submission for Exit this page component
backlog.body:
Formerly known as 'Hide this page component'
What
What are we proposing
We are looking to implement a component, using the existing button component, that allows vulnerable users of a Government service to quickly and safely hide the page and reduce the risk of Domestic Abuse incidents.
The functionality behind the component would allow a user to quickly hide the current page and open a new, ambiguous webpage, such as BBC Weather or another such website. This would lower the risk of drawing attention to browsing habits from a perpetrator.
Why
Why are we proposing this design pattern?

Domestic abuse is physical, sexual, psychological or financial abuse that takes place within an intimate or family-type relationship and that forms a pattern of forceful and controlling behaviour. This can include forced marriage and so-called ‘honour-based crimes.” Domestic abuse may include a range of abusive behaviours, not all of which are in themselves inherently ‘violent’

The biggest risk to a victim of Domestic Abuse is homicide and serious physical assaults - this is at its greatest risk when a victim is planning to flee or escape from the perpetrator. Often, one of the first things a victim will do is to speak to someone to make a disclosure about abuse. The second thing they will do is research and find help online, often using Government services.
We need to ensure that the risk is minimised for users when using online services. Although victims and survivors can be aware of the risks, it is the Government's responsibility to protect individuals using a service. Therefore, it is crucial that there is a consistency of approach in design and functionality across Government with this component.
What evidence do you have that it's needed by multiple services across government?
From conversations between the Department for Work and Pensions, Ministry of Justice, the Cabinet Office and Scottish Government, it is already clear that other services need to ensure that this design is available.
Services are already responding to the rise in Domestic Abuse during COVID-19 by building their own minimum viable solutions to allow users to quickly hide their webpages.
There are areas of the Government site, such as “Domestic Abuse: How to get help”, that a high risk user would access for support that does not include a way to hide their browsing. This is putting those users of this service at risk.
What evidence do you have that it meets the needs of the users of those services?
Speaking with subject matter experts (SME), it is critical that we offer this feature on the GOV.UK website. It is a feature that is provided by other organisations, such as:

Scottish Government - Domestic Abuse page
Refuge
Women’s Aid
Victim Support

Each website has varied design implementations, but ultimately addresses the same user need of being able to hide browsing habits quickly.
The Ministry of Justice have carried out some initial research with an SME to establish whether the proposed solution meets the user needs.
Have you checked that it doesn't already exist in the GOV.UK Design System?
There are no outstanding issues or tickets in the Design System backlog that refer to this type of component.
Anything else
What else has been done
The MoJ have iterated twice on the design component on our live service - looking at language, design and functionality.
There are several designs that are considered minimum viable products which have been released by the DWP (Child Maintenance Service) - Cabinet Office (Coronavirus Support) and the MoJ (Legal Aid Agency). The expediency of these releases has been due to the fact that by not having something, we are putting our users at risk.
The MoJ have carried out some early rounds of testing with an SME that have looked at design, functionality and various use cases from a range of user scenarios. This has all been documented and shared with DWP and CO to share research and findings.
Designs
We looked to extend the GOV.UK Button component to act as the interactive element that a user would press to exit the website.
The Design System suggests using red for any destructive actions undertaken on a GOV.UK website - as the intention for the 'Hide this page' button was essentially closing the webpage down, it would be deemed destructive. This has been adopted by DWP and the Scottish Government.
We decided to utilise the additional space available in the 1/3 column, which is usually reserved for additional information as it allowed us to present the button within immediate view for the user.
The button would then be "sticky" in position at the top of the page on smaller devices. This prevents any conflict with the GOV.UK 'Contents' link that is positioned at the bottom of the screen. It also removes potential accidental presses by a user who doesn't need to use it.
Feedback from SME on the design

Victims of Domestic Abuse are used to using their reptilian brain and are in fight or flight mode so the red would be a trigger for them to draw their to attention to it - Comment from SME

Content
The language used in the button has recently been changed in order to create a more unified style as we continue to work with DWP, Cabinet Office and the Scottish Government. The use of 'Hide this page' presented more of a sense of immediacy, as well as being more descriptive of what the button actually does when the user interacts with it, so we have moved away from the original 'Quick Exit'.
We also use a keyboard function for the user to be able to interact with the button which is controlled by pressing the 'Esc' key.
Behaviour and Functionality
We have explored several types of behaviour for the button, however in order to provide the greatest amount of safety for users we decided to implement functionality similar to other charities and organisations.
When a user interacts with the button, they are sent to a new browser tab that opens BBC Weather. The original tab that they were on doesn't close, but redirects to Google.
This component does not prescribe which websites are to be linked to. That is best done by the individual services and their user research combined with the knowledge of their user base. Google and BBC Weather are good neutral examples pending further research.
Accessibility
The Legal Aid Agency have had an Accessibility Audit on their service and this highlighted some improvements to the component. These were:

Ensuring the button text accurately describes it's purpose
Ensure the instruction "(Or press 'Esc' key)" is presented to all users when presented as a sticky element
Include visually hidden text at the top of the page to help users of assistive technology be aware of the leave page functionality
Differentiate betwixt mobile displays and PC displays zoomed in, so the information about using the escape key is not hidden for non-mobile narrow displays

These changes have been implemented in the latest version of the component, however we will be looking to further test the accessibility of the component as we continue to iterate on it.
MoJ Data Analytics
The 'Hide this page' button has been running as an MVP on the Check Legal Aid service since 14 April 2020. It has been used with a fair amount of frequency, however at present we are are yet to analyse the data in more detail.
The gaps in data recording were due to changes on the back-end of our service that caused GA to drop out.

The below graph data also shows variations in spikes and lower use through the pandemic

ourIssues.title: Consider adding functionality to Exit this page to accept an array of redirects and use one at random
ourIssues.body:
## Related component

- [Exit this page](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/exit-this-page/)

## Context

Following a recent blog post I made about the Exit this Page component, a commenter suggested that users _always_ being directed to BBC Weather could raise suspicion in a vulnerable user. This is especially the case if they need to use the exit functionality several times in a relatively short period and are redirected to BBC Weather every time. 

To counter this, we could allow services to pass an array of multiple services into the EtP component and have the component choose one of these at random upon each activation to redirect to.

## Alternatives

A service could write server-side code to change the target for the EtP button on each page load, 

## Additional information (if applicable)

There would still need to be a 'main' redirect that exists as the `href` of the link used as a no-JS fallback. I'm not sure we have a defined format for passing an array via `data-*` attributes either, so this functionality may have to be limited to JavaScript configuration.

ourIssues.title: Issues with Exit this Page keyboard shortcut and the iOS/iPadOS virtual keyboard
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

The Exit this Page component includes a method of activating the exit functionality by pressing the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key three times (behind the scenes, three `keyup` events). We do not limit when this functionality works, so it's still possible to do this when focused on an input or textarea. This is by design, as we want the user to be able to use the function quickly and at any time. 

This does mean, however, that the function is exposed to devices that utilise virtual keyboards (aka, on-screen keyboards or software keyboards) when a text field is focused. This can be problematic, as the <kbd>Shift</kbd> function was only designed with hardware keyboards in mind and virtual keyboards can operate substantially differently than their hardware equivalents.

### An overview of iOS <kbd>Shift</kbd> operating modes

The <kbd>Shift</kbd> key on iOS has multiple modes of operation depending on the current context, attributes of the current input, and how it is pressed. In one context it is also replaced by a numbers and symbols toggle button, however this button is still treated as being a <kbd>Shift</kbd> key for the purposes of JavaScript events.

**When pressed for a short period of time**, the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key acts as a toggle switch, and changes between being 'on' or 'off' on alternating presses of the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key. The `keyup` event is fired on every second press (the 'off'), except in cases described below.

**When held down**, the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key acts transiently, being 'on' for as long as the user holds it down and turning 'off' once released. The user can press other keys when <kbd>Shift</kbd> is held down to type in uppercase. When used in this way, the `keyup` event is **not** fired when the user releases the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key.

The user can **tap <kbd>Shift</kbd> twice** in rapid succession to turn on Caps Lock mode. The user can press <kbd>Shift</kbd> a third time to turn Caps Lock mode off. When this is carried out, it's emitted as a `keyup` event by the <kbd>Caps Lock</kbd> key, not the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key.

When the user **enters numbers and symbols mode** on the keyboard, the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key is visually replaced by a button to toggle between the initial numbers and symbols view, and the extended symbols view. In this mode, tapping to view the extended symbols mode is treated as a <kbd>Shift</kbd> `keydown` event, and returning to the initial numbers and symbols view is treated as a <kbd>Shift</kbd> `keyup` event. These events are emitted to the webpage, in what feels like a bug in Safari or iOS. 

There are several situations in which **the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key is turned 'on' automatically**. When this happens, no `keydown` event is emitted to the webpage. When it is turned 'off', either automatically or by the user, no `keyup` event is emitted. 

> [!NOTE]
> The takeaway to remember from this is that <kbd>Shift</kbd> will _never_ emit a `keyup` event if the `keydown` wasn't initiated by the user, even if the `keyup` was. This holds true for all of the cases here. 

Situations where this can occur include:

* The input being empty when the user taps on it.
* The cursor being positioned at the start of a new sentence, line or paragraph when the user taps on the input.
* The cursor being positioned at the start of a new word, if the input has the `autocapitalize="words"` attribute.
* Always, if the input has the `autocapitalize="characters"` attribute.

There are a couple of situations where the virtual keyboard will **fire `keyup` events without user intent**. These include: 

* Turning <kbd>Shift</kbd> 'on' manually and switching to the numbers and symbols view will emit the `keyup` event.
* On an input where <kbd>Shift</kbd> will not turn 'on' automatically (e.g. in the middle of a word or sentence), manually activate <kbd>Shift</kbd>, close the virtual keyboard, and then tap on the input to open it again. <kbd>Shift</kbd> will be returned to the 'off' state and emit the `keyup` event.

In testing, we particularly noticed this being a problem on iOS and, presumably, are mirrored in iPadOS. 

> [!NOTE]
> These problems with the shortcut were only noted when using the virtual keyboard. The shortcut works as intended when using a hardware keyboard paired with the iOS/iPadOS device.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Visit a page that has both the Exit this Page button and an input field.
2. Focus the input so that the virtual keyboard opens.
3. Attempt to activate the EtP functionality by tapping <kbd>Shift</kbd> at least three times.

## Actual vs expected behaviour

### Expected

The Exit this Page functionality is activated and the user leaves the page.

### Actual

It is very difficult to activate the EtP shortcut behaviour intentionally.

If the user is pressing the key rapidly, and assuming an initially empty input or textarea, the most likely scenario is:

1. <kbd>Shift</kbd> was already turned on by default. Tap 1 turns it off and does not emit a `keyup` event.
2. Tap 2 happens quickly enough that Caps Lock mode is activated. <kbd>Caps Lock</kbd> emits a `keydown` event. 
3. Tap 3 turns off Caps Lock mode. <kbd>Caps Lock</kbd> emits a `keyup` event.
4. Tap 4 turns Caps Lock mode back on.
5. Repeat.

It is possible to activate the function successfully if the user takes time to wait between button presses—roughly half a second between presses. This wait is exacerbated by the need to perform more taps than usual, requiring 3 before the indicator lights are first shown, and a total of 7 to activate the functionality.

In addition, there are seemingly many scenarios that can unintentionally add to the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key activation count or cancel an activation currently in progress, most commonly, accidentally tapping fast enough to enable Caps Lock mode.

## Environment (where applicable)

- Operating system: iOS 16.4
- Browser: Safari
- Browser version: 16.4
- GOV.UK Frontend Version: 4.7.0 (however testing took place prior to this release)

backlog.title: Invite users to a private or public beta
backlog.body:
What
When testing a new version of a service, it's important to limit the number of users that use it at first.
First with an opt-in approach at Private Beta. One way of doing this would be sending out an email if you know users email before they use the service, although this is increasingly difficult to GDPR. You can promote the Private Beta ahead of time using social media and other advertising channels and collect contact details of people who are interested. Another (less public) way is to find users through professional networks they are members of. This is particularly useful for services where people are using it as part of their job.
Then, at Public Beta the service can move to an opt-out approach. The new service becomes the default promoted option, but there should include a link to the old legacy service as there may be unforeseen issues with the new service not found in Private Beta which means some users need to use the old version.
These are high-level principles – It would be good if people can populate the comments on this issue with real-life examples and how well the approach worked to de-risk the rollout of services and help teams learn and iterate.
Why


What evidence do you have that it's needed by multiple services across government?


This is something that all new government services need to do to follow the agile delivery phases.


What evidence do you have that it meets the needs of the users of those services?


I've personally not seen methodical evidence per se for this approach although it makes sense logically and is commonly used across government. As mentioned above, it would be great if people have any evidence for its efficacy.


Have you checked that it doesn't already exist in the GOV.UK Design System?


Yes
Anything else

Include links to any examples, research or code to support your proposal, if available.

Arguably this belongs more in the Service Manual than the Design System. There is already a page about how the beta phase works, but I think the detail of implementation belongs more in the Design System.

ourIssues.title: Module name missing for some `new ElementError()` calls
ourIssues.body:
<!--
    Please fill in as much of the template below as you’re able to. If you're unsure whether the issue already exists or how to fill in the template, open an issue anyway. Our team will help you to complete the rest.

    Your issue might already exist. If so, add a comment to the existing issue instead of creating a new one. You can find existing issues here:
    - an existing Github issue: https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues
    - known validation errors or warnings: https://github.com/orgs/alphagov/projects/37
-->

## Description of the issue

Component `ElementError` messages were [updated to use `moduleName` suffixes](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/5338):

```console
govuk-accordion: Root element (`$root`) is not of type HTMLElement
govuk-button: Root element (`$root`) already initialised
govuk-checkboxes: Form inputs (`<input type="checkbox">`) not found
govuk-exit-this-page: Root element (`$root`) is not of type HTMLElement
...
```

But the following error messages were missed:

```console
Password input: Form field (`.govuk-js-password-input-input`) must be of type `password`.
Password input: Button (`.govuk-js-password-input-toggle`) must be of type `button`.
Skip link: Target link (`href="#example"`) has no hash fragment
```

They use older plain english component names and not `moduleName`

<!-- A clear and concise summary of what the bug is. -->

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Trigger one of the errors shown above where `moduleName` is not used

## Actual vs expected behaviour

All component-level errors should log the correct `moduleName` for better error reporting

E.g. `Password input:` → `govuk-password-input:`

```patch
- Password input: Form field (`.govuk-js-password-input-input`) must be of type `password`.
+ govuk-password-input: Form field (`.govuk-js-password-input-input`) must be of type `password`.
```

```patch
- Password input: Button (`.govuk-js-password-input-toggle`) must be of type `button`.
+ govuk-password-input: Button (`.govuk-js-password-input-toggle`) must be of type `button`.
```

```patch
- Skip link: Target link (`href="#example"`) has no hash fragment
+ govuk-skip-link: Target link (`href="#example"`) has no hash fragment
```

ourIssues.title: HTML lint and link check skip the 404 and generic error pages
ourIssues.body:
`npm run lint:html` validates `build/**/index.html`, so `build/404.html` and `build/errors/generic.html` are never validated. `npm run check-links` crawls from `build/sitemap.xml`; `404.njk` sets `ignoreInSitemap` and no page links to it, so links on the 404 page are never checked either. Netlify serves the 404 page to everyone who reaches a missing URL. Reproduction: add `

a

b x

` under the h1 in `src/404.njk`, then `npm run build`. `npm run lint:html` returns 0 and `npm run check-links` returns 0. `npx html-validate build/404.html` directly returns 1 (duplicate ID). The same lines in `src/contact.njk` make both commands return 1. Tested at bf1d72c5. Suggested fix: widen the lint glob to `build/**/*.html` (or add the two error pages explicitly), and add `build/404.html` and `build/errors/generic.html` as extra entry points for hyperlink. Both pages pass today, so the change would not turn CI red.

## What

This ticket is for reviewing the MOJ Header and ensuring it meets accessibility standards for mobile users.

## Why

Previous discoveries uncovered an issue that some MOJ components are not compatible with mobile devices/ users. work undertaken in https://github.com/ministryofjustice/moj-frontend/issues/2183 found:

Average percentage from 17 external-facing MOJ services:
Mobile | 50.0%
Desktop | 48.9%

Average percentage from 13 internal-facing MOJ services:
Mobile | 9.31%
Desktop | 90.54%

We are also anecdotally aware that some MOJ services are considering increasing mobile usage for internal services, so we need to ensure all components are mobile compatible.

Where users are predominantly on mobile, any build with a table (like contextual date, multi select, scrollable pane, sortable table) should not be encouraged.

- Developer

- Accessibility Specialist

backlog.title: Accessibility link
backlog.body:
What
Establish how best to name and link to information about the accessibility options available to users within services.
Is referring to 'Ease of access' (or similar) more likely to be recognised by users who could benefit from the information provided?
Why
As part of meeting the legal requirements for the accessibility, teams producing websites and applications are directed to publish an accessibility statement
Within this, services can give useful information to users about the controls available to the users, such as browser options to control text size and colours, certain assistive tools and so on.
Most services seem to do this through a link named 'Accessibility' page in the footer.
However, in a Slack discussion in the cross-government 'Accessibility' channel, members of the community shared examples where users:

do not recognise the term 'Accessibility'
do not think that it is relevant to them
do not bother to look because, from past experience, they expect it to contain technical information or jargon that isn't relevant

This means some users can miss out on information about ease of access that would make it easier for them to use a service.
Quotes from Slack discussion (as of now)
A user researcher at GDS, said:
[I've seen] "all of the above (when researching how users perceived accessibility statements for the GDS accessibility team). Particularly that users don't always associate the word with their needs, potentially consider it to be about physical access, don't expect it to contain anything useful for them, or are so used to those pages containing generic/jargony info that they don't bother to look."
A user researcher at Ministry of Justice, said:
"I’ve tested accessibility pages in the past. In usability testing users didn’t recognise the link and when prompted to look under it, didn’t think the information was relevant or helpful.
In the past, accessibility pages were largely a box-ticking exercise and had little valuable info for users. They usually consisted of a standard line about WCAG compliance (even if it was not true), HTML validation and browser keyboard shortcuts. The better ones linked to BBC’s 'my web, my way'.
I expect that even those who had looked there, over time learned not to waste their time.
Having observed recent discussions about accessibility statements, I think there’s still a risk of tick-boxing. That’s why any sample statements should include a massive caveat that they shouldn’t be copied and pasted and that you should first do the work, then write about it (in that order).
I think it would be interesting to get quant data on this with analytics."
A Front-End Developer and Accessibility Specialist at GDS, said:
"Bad discoverability was one of the reasons why Microsoft renamed their accessibility settings to “Ease of access”."
(But I don't know the source for this)
In the 'Apply for a Budgeting Loan' service, feedback about the usability of the service is broadly very positive but a small percentage of users consistently give feedback that they need larger text or for text to be read to them. For this service we know some of our user base struggle in terms of literacy and can be low in confidence and ability using technology. This service doesn't currently have an accessibility statement of its own but it seems that users have not read GOV.UK's accessibility statement about the options available to them.

ourIssues.title: The expanded/collapsed state of conditional reveals is not available to all assistive technologies
ourIssues.body:
## What

As part of an internal accessibility audit of GOV.UK, conditional reveals† was flagged as failing WCAG 4.1.2:

> **4.1.2 Name, Role, Value**: For all user interface components (including but not limited to: form elements, links and components generated by scripts), the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes to these items is available to user agents, including assistive technologies. (Level A)

It was flagged as failing because:
- the additional 'role' of the checkbox or radio button is not clear
- changes to the expanded ‘state’ of the radio buttons is not available to assistive tech, and so users may be unaware that something else has changed on the page as a result of selecting a radio.

We use `aria-expanded` on these controls, but that is technically invalid according to the spec, which [only allows `aria-expanded` on certain roles](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#aria-expanded). Some screen readers still announce the expanded state, but those that don’t have no reason to implement it because it’s against the spec. ARIA 1.2 (which is currently in draft) extends support of aria-expanded to checkboxes but not radios.

The fact that `aria-expanded` is not valid is recorded as a separate but related issue (https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/979).

As of [September 2019](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/979#issuecomment-528932826), this is known to affect:

- Voiceover (https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/989)
- JAWS (https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/935)

### Update

As of June 2021, we [removed conditional reveals from our accessibility statement](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/issues/6042#issuecomment-871527458).

---

† The [page being audited](https://webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk/20200911014618/https://www.gov.uk/email-signup?link=/world/switzerland) uses the conditional reveals in an unusual way, as what’s being revealed is effectively contextual help (like a hint) that would help the user to make the right choice. Whereas the way we intend the component to be used is [to reveal additional form controls that ‘follow on’ from the initial question](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/#conditionally-revealing-content). We think that revealing text in this way is 'worse' in terms of accessibility, so we have a separate issue to discourage users from using conditional reveals to reveal text (https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/issues/1362)

ourIssues.title: Adjust components to scale with android system font size
ourIssues.body:
## What
Ensure as many of our components as possible are responding when viewing govuk-frontend web pages on android devices and adjusting android's system font size.

## Why
Govuk-frontend web pages should respect accessibility settigns and respond to them as expected.

## Steps to replicate
Tested in chrome on browserstack's Galaxy S23 instance as it's easy to notice the issue due to the device's large font size scale.

1. Go to the settings of the testing device and locate the setting to adjust device font size
2. Increase font size (recommend max in order to visualise issue more clearly)
3. Open a govuk-frontend web page on a browser on an android device eg: [the review app's announcements page](https://govuk-frontend-review.herokuapp.com/full-page-examples/announcements)

Notice that the breadcrumbs have not increased in size. Digging into the runtime styles, you will find that rem values of other elements on the page have adjusted in response to the font size change but the breadcrumbs haven't.

![Android browser showing an announcements page with scaled up font size except for the breadcrumbs element](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/assets/64783893/66ecb7d1-bf9e-459a-987c-8c85176a26b7)

## Notes
### Considerations from the spec
The likely reason this is happening can be found in CSS Mobile Text Size section of the CSS spec, specifically [2.2: Conditions that suppress adjustment](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-size-adjust/#default-adjustment-conditions). This section notes 4 reasons that would suppress text size adjustment. From initial testing, certain components can be 'fixed' by removing their block level positioning rules eg: components that have `display: inline-block`. We should be able to use `inline-block` on components and the text size adjustment not be suppressed. Recommend using the the spec in figuring out a solution.

### Impacted components
- Accordion
- Back link
- Breadcrumbs
- Button, and places consumed
    - Cookie banner buttons
    - Exit this page
- Checkboxes
- Details (not the content)
- File upload
- Some of the footer's links
- Header menu
- Notification banner
- Pagination
- Radios
- Select

- Text input, and places consumed

communityIssues.title: Back to top link fails 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
communityIssues.body: The [Back to top link component](https://govuk-government-frontend.herokuapp.com/component-guide/back_to_top) in government-frontend fails [2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)](https://w3c.github.io/wcag/understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html). Note: 2.4.11 is part of the new draft WCAG 2.2 criteria. The latest standard is WCAG 2.1. WCAG 2.2 isn't published yet, so this is potentially subject to change. As mentioned by Andy Sellick in his 2018 blog post ‘[Sticky elements: functionality and accessibility testing](https://technology.blog.gov.uk/2018/05/21/sticky-elements-functionality-and-accessibility-testing/)’, content can be obscured by a sticky element. 2.4.11 is specifically about focus that shouldn’t be obscured. There was an effort with this component to minimise that already as the sticky ‘Contents’ link only appears when scrolling the page but not when only tabbing through the page. Although that fixes some of the issue, that doesn’t mean that the focus never gets obscured. The sticky link still appears when scrolling via the keyboard (for example, with the arrow keys) or when accidentally scrolling with the mouse or touchpad only for a second. To replicate, open the [preview of the 'Contents list with body' component](https://govuk-government-frontend.herokuapp.com/component-guide/contents_list_with_body/default/preview), tab to the last link (‘Commencement of initial period notice’), scroll the page via the up arrow key so that the link is obscured, use tab and shift + tab to go back and forth to see how you can tab to a link that isn’t visible. ourIssues.title: Consider wrapping Task list onto a single column on narrow viewports
ourIssues.body: ## Related component [Task list](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/task-list/) ## Context Historically (even before it was part of the GOV.UK Design System), the Task list component has retained a two column layout across all viewport sizes, with each row displaying the task name and detail on the left and status on the right. This was originally contributed when our default font size on mobile devices was 16px equivalent, which worked quite well, with space for roughly 3 to 5 words per line. However, the new typography scale increased the font size to 19px equivalent, which became the default in Frontend 6.0.0. This has resulted in long names or detail being squashed into long, narrow, somewhat harder to read columns with anywhere from 1 to 3 words per line. We might want to update the component so that the content is displayed in a single column on narrow viewports. |Old type scale|New type scale| |:-:|:-:| ||| ## Alternatives This problem is somewhat dependent on the text of the status labels. Rows with longer statuses naturally get more squashed than shorter ones, and the shorter the task name and detail, the less there is to squash. Thus one way to 'avoid' the issue is to place less text in the component. ## Additional information (if applicable) Only started being an issue in 5.2.0, if the user enabled the new typography scale. As of 6.0.0 this is the default scale.

ourIssues.title: Suggestion: apply aria-describedby to all tasks in task list, not just links
ourIssues.body:
https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/520f2345aed725b2c29f14af2cdffcd75a5e130a/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/task-list/template.njk#L10-L20

In the current task list implementation, tasks that are links have `aria-describedby` linking the hint and the status. Tasks that do not have links do not get the same treatment.

The result of this is that (depending on screen reader), the different tasks sound different and are not consistent. I think it would be better for consistency if non-link tasks also linked the status.

I discussed this on the Cross-Gov Slack, and it seems it shouldn't hurt to implement this change. It may improve consistency, and while not all screen readers may read out the aria-describedby, if they do not, it is no worse than the current implementation.

### Example without aria-describedby (current):
https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/assets/2204224/f76d1749-6ffc-4836-9408-7d91a1e315f2

### Example with aria-describedby:
https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/assets/2204224/741fba77-844e-4f48-8578-6244b64aefe6



---

### Potential solution

Testing in VoiceOver on iOS, moving the existing `aria-describedby="{{ hintId + " " if item.hint }}{{ statusId }}"` to the parent div seems to work well. But if we wanted to keep it on the anchor itself, we could add a second copy of it to the non-link `div` for text.

ourIssues.title: Add `size` option to form input component labels
ourIssues.body:
<!--

  This is a template for any issues that aren’t bug reports or new feature requests. The headings in this section provide examples of the information you might want to include, but feel free to add/delete sections where appropriate.

-->

## What

Allow form field components to receive a new `size` option in their `label` or `legend` option for easily controlling the text size of their label or legend. The option should receive a t-shirt size and set the appropriate `.govuk-label--<T_SHIRT_SIZE>` or `.govuk-fieldset__legend--<T_SHIRT_SIZE>` on the label or legend.

For components using a `label` the option should be implemented by adding a [new option to our internal Label component](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/label) and passing the option through. For those using a `legend`, the public Fieldset component should get an update first in a similar fashion.

The affected components are:
- [Character Count](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/character-count/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Textarea)
- [Checkboxes](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/checkboxes/template.njk) (forwarding the option to either Fieldset)
- [Date Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Fieldset](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk)
- [File Upload](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/file-upload/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Label](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/label/template.njk)
- [Password Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/password-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Input)
- [Radios](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/radios/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Select](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/select/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Textarea](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/textarea/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)

## Why

Different components use different tags for the "title" of the field. This requires the user to understand internal nuances (is it a `label` or `legend`) to change its size. Having an option abstracting this and letting the component work out if it's `.govuk-label--...` or `.govuk-fieldset__legend--...` that's needed is much easier.

## Who needs to work on this

Developers, Tech writer

## Who needs to review this

Developers, Tech writer

## Done when

- [ ] The new option is available on all the components listed above
- [ ] The option is documented consistently across components

ourIssues.title: Improve documentation of `beforeInput(s)` and `afterInput(s)` options of our form control components
ourIssues.body:
<!--

  This is a template for any issues that aren’t bug reports or new feature requests. The headings in this section provide examples of the information you might want to include, but feel free to add/delete sections where appropriate.

-->

## What

Research and document which kind of content is OK/not OK to put in the `beforeInput(s)` and `afterInput(s)` options of our form components, introduced in #4567 to ensure all users (especially those using assistive technology) get proper access to the content.

## Why

Because the content ends up inside a form field, where the control is associated to the label/legend and any error/hint, there's a risk that content injected through `beforeInput(s)`/`afterInput(s)` options gets missed when navigating from field to field, the focus skipping over the content to the next form field. 

This means we may want to suggest restrictions as to which content is suitable for these options, possible techniques to link the content so it gets announced when navigating from field to field, and possibly a warning to test thoroughly.

## Who needs to work on this

Developers, Accessibility specialist, possibly Designers

## Who needs to review this

Developers, Accessibility specialist, possibly Designers 

## Done when

- [ ] We've clarified how to best use the `beforeInput(s)` and `afterInput(s)` options of our form components.

ourIssues.title: Selects in Safari are styled differently to other browsers
ourIssues.body:
`<select>`s in Safari retain quite a lot of default styling and so appear inconsistent with other form components, and with how selects appear in other browsers.

iOS 16.2 (Safari and Chrome, because Chrome uses Webkit on iOS):

![A GOV.UK-style select in iOS Safari with rounded corners](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1935173/232555588-4c5b3e95-1862-4b57-a955-a01905b2fc39.png)

Safari 16.1 on macOS Ventura:

![A GOV.UK-style select in mac OS Safari with a glossy appearance](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1935173/232555905-f7b40148-c020-4560-8e40-563eb2966e35.png)

(Chrome desktop, for reference)

![A GOV.UK-style select in Chrome with square corners](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1935173/232560523-b69a9815-f8b1-442b-ad34-6c6091cd25bd.png)


The rounded corners on iOS are quite easy to overcome with `border-radius: 0`

![A GOV.UK-style select in iOS Safari with square corners](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1935173/232557315-f6022f8c-b971-47e2-b687-ee50d53809da.png)

Unfortunately macOS is trickier. `border-radius` has no effect unless you also add `-webkit-appearance: none` - but that also removes the arrows:

![A GOV.UK-style select in mac OS Safari with a white background and square corners, but no arrows indicating it can be opened](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1935173/232558311-f551e3cb-23a5-4ca1-8545-6fd7cd654ca3.png)

[Digital Scotland Design System's select component](https://designsystem.gov.scot/components/select/) handles this by introducing a wrapper element and using a styled span for the dropdown arrow:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1935173/232559148-e2f79cad-8293-4e3f-91f0-153e36ac42df.png)

The span is overlaid on the `<select>` with `position: absolute` and has `pointer-events: none` so clicks just fall through to the `<select>`

This approach isn't ideal and would be a breaking change for the GOV.UK Frontend (but I wonder if the same effect could be achieved with an `:after` instead?)

See also https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/2435 for previous issues with selects retaining too much default styling in Firefox and Safari

ourIssues.body:
Hello,

My colleague has previously emailed about these two issues (ID: 6183982), but I'm submitting them here as you suggested just in case you get more capacity to look at them in the future. We have two similar issues with Narrator preventing users from being able to select input suggestions in text boxes and select fields.

Browsers used for all tests:
Microsoft Edge for Business
Version 137.0.3296.62 (Official build) (64-bit)

Microsoft Edge for Business
Version 137.0.3296.68 (Official build) (64-bit)

### Issue 1: Form / Narrator issues - Cannot select Input suggestion with Narrator focused on it
 
Description
When using Narrator within a form (developed using x-gov form builder), a user cannot select Input suggestions listed in the callout by using keyboard input means including the ENTER, TAB and Spacebar keys, this issue does not occur when attempting the same process with Narrator off.

We replicate the issue with the following steps, however the URL may not work for you.

a.   Activate Narrator.

b.   Navigate to URL: https://runner-stg.testwebforms.test-and-trace.nhs.uk/kls-enquiries/start

c.   Complete the "Systematic review" enquiry form process up to the "about-you" page.

d.   Tab into the "Full name" form input field (id="nBYObd") to give it focus.

e.   A list of input suggestions of previously used names are displayed in a callout box.

f.    Highlight the first input suggestion by using Down Arrow Key.

g.   The input suggestions callout box will close, the "Full name" form input field will remain blank and the Speech Reader focus moves onto the next field instead of the expected behaviour of the input suggestions callout box closing and the "Full name" form input field being populated with the chosen input suggestion.

 
### Issue 2: Narrator issues - Cannot select dropdown item with Narrator focused on it

Description
When using Narrator within a forms environment, a user cannot select Input suggestions listed in the callout by using keyboard input means including the ENTER, TAB and Spacebar keys, this issue does not occur when attempting the same process with Narrator off.
We replicate the issue with the following steps, however the URL may not work for you:

1.    Navigate to URL: https://runner-stg.testwebforms.test-and-trace.nhs.uk/kls-enquiries/start

2.    Complete the "Systematic review" enquiry form process up to the "systematic-review-questions" page.

3.    Tab into "What type of review are you doing?" Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) to give it focus.

4.    Select Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) using Spacebar or ENTER Key to display the dropdown list.

5.    Dropdown list is displayed.

6.    Highlight the first item "Fully systematic review" by using Down Arrow Key.

7.    Select item "Fully systematic review" by using ENTER Key.

8.    The dropdown list is still displayed instead of the expected behaviour of it closing and the focus returning to the "What type of review are you doing?" Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) field.

ourIssues.title: Consider adding documentation on `select[multiple]`
ourIssues.body:
The `<select>` HTML element has an alternative mode that allows for selecting multiple values, also known as a multi-select listbox. This is enabled using the `multiple` flag. We don't explicitly support using `multiple` with our Nunjucks macro, however service teams can still enable it through the attributes parameter. 

We do not support `multiple` in our CSS and discourage using it for a few reasons:
- Using multi-select is complicated, requiring the user to hold down one or more keyboard keys (<kbd>⌘ Cmd</kbd>/<kbd>⌃ Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>⇧ Shift</kbd>) whilst clicking on options. This is difficult to convey and usually not well understood by users.
- Multi-select cannot be easily used with keyboard navigation alone, practically requiring a pointer device to use.
- Multi-select is not (to my knowledge) well supported by assistive technologies.

We may also want to include information on the `size` attribute, which we also do not support in Frontend's code, although it doesn't have the same pitfalls as `multiple`. 

## Related documentation
[Select](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/select/)

## Suggestion
A user has suggested adding documentation about `select[multiple]`; specifically, adding information on why we discourage using it and don't support it: https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/3317 

In most situations, we would probably recommend using [a list of checkboxes](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/checkboxes/) instead.

## Evidence (where applicable)

- [`<select>` your poison](https://www.24a11y.com/2019/select-your-poison/) on [24 Accessibility](https://www.24a11y.com/)

ourIssues.title: Explore separating the 'core' functionality of the Character Count from the management of its configuration
ourIssues.body:
<!--

  This is a template for any issues that aren’t bug reports or new feature requests. The headings in this section provide examples of the information you might want to include, but feel free to add/delete sections where appropriate.

-->

## What

Explore extracting the core feature of the Character Count into its own class, used internally by the component and focused on:
- listening to value changes in the field it observes
- running a function to get the count
- updating the UI based on the `threshold`, a `maxlength` and the I18n messages

The original `CharacterCount` class would remain focused on managing the configuration and delegating the actual counting to that new class.

```js
// 
class CharacterCount {
  constructor(config) {
    // Do stuff with the config to figure the field to observe, the function to count, the `threshold`, `maxlength` and messages
    new CharacterCountCore({/* consistent subset of options */})
  }
}
```

Explore if we can also separate technical aspects like monitoring the value of the field and running the initial count on `show` outside of that `CharacterCountCore`.

## Why

A lot of the code in the component only manages the configuration (picking the right function based on `maxlength`/`maxwords`, ensuring the correct option takes over based on which part of the configuration defined the option). There's also some technical code (monitoring the field's value, and possibly running the initial count) which could live outside of the component so the component's instance variables remain focused on counting characters and updating the UI.

Separating the core functionality of the component from these aspect would create a better separation of concern between configuring the component, technical glue and the actual component's features, making it easier to see what's what and what can possibly be cleaned up when options are updated/removed.

## Who needs to work on this

Developers

## Who needs to review this

Developers

## Done when

- [ ] Spike to see if possible to extract such a class
- [ ] Document learnings from the spike

ourIssues.title: Define our conventions for passing complex data structures into components
ourIssues.body:
## What Currently, we have two methods of passing configuration into components: with JavaScript or with HTML `data-*` attributes. These are equivalent configurations: ```html
…
``` However, HTML `data-*` attributes are restricted to being **strings** (as all attribute values are strings in HTML). We do some work in JavaScript to detect the type and cast the strings 'true' and 'false' to **booleans**, and numbers greater than 0 to **numbers**, but these are the only types that our HTML configuration supports. On the other hand, JavaScript configuration supports all of the same data types that JavaScript does, such as arrays, objects and functions. Being able to utilise these types in configuration objects would be useful for some future work, but we cannot do so without breaking parity with the HTML configuration. As such, we should decide whether we're okay with some configuration options only being accessible with JavaScript. ourIssues.title: Components assume the `govuk-visually-hidden` utility class will exist
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

We provide an entry points for each individual component, the idea being that users should get all of the CSS they need to use that component, and ideally nothing more.

For example, including the character count component also includes the CSS for the:

- error message
- hint
- label
- textarea

However, it does _not_ include the `govuk-visually-hidden` utility class, which is used within the Nunjucks template.

From a quick check, it looks like this affects:

- Accordion (in the JavaScript)
- Character count (in the JavaScript)
- Error message (in the Nunjucks template)
- Exit this page (in the Nunjucks template and JavaScript)
- File upload (in the JavaScript)
- Footer (in the Nunjucks template)
- Pagination (in the Nunjucks template)
- Password input (in the JavaScript)
- Summary list (in the Nunjucks template)
- Warning text (in the Nunjucks template)

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Use the component-specific entrypoint to include just the CSS for any of the components listed above, then view the component

## Actual vs expected behaviour

Visually hidden text should be hidden, but it isn't because the `govuk-visually-hidden` utility class is not included in the CSS

ourIssues.title: Add support for dynamically sized textareas / character count
ourIssues.body:
## What

Our textarea and character counts have a fixed height, defaulting to 5 rows.

We hope that designers will set the height to be appropriate for the amount of content a user has to enter, but if the user enters more content than fits in the height of the box they end up needing to scroll to read it.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d675ff66-8ba1-4b13-8988-c5a9b96ad109

It seems like a good enhancement would be to allow textareas to grow as the user types, so any scrolling happens at the page level.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29748e47-74c4-4df3-9aa4-22cece134709

This is trivial to implement with the `field-sizing` property, for example we could add a modifier class:

```css
.govuk-textarea--auto-size {
  field-sizing: content;
  min-height: 5lh;
}
```

Note that the `rows` attribute has no effect on textareas using `field-sizing: content`.

## Why

Allowing the user to read back the content they've entered in the textarea without having to scroll within the textarea improves usability.

This enhancement feels particularly useful fiven the 'one thing per page' principle, as the textarea may be the only input on the page, so it doesn't make much sense to constrain its height.

## Who needs to work on this

Designers, developers

## Who needs to review this

Designers, developers

## Done when

- [ ] We understand the implications of using `field-sizing: content` on a textarea
- [ ] We've implemented a way to apply 'dynamic sizing' to the relevant components
- [ ] We've written guidance to tell users how and when to use it
- [ ] We've documented any 'gotchas', for example the fact that `rows` has no effect

The affected components are:

- [Date Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Fieldset](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk)
- [File Upload](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/file-upload/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Label](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/label/template.njk)
- [Password Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/password-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Input)
- [Radios](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/radios/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Select](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/select/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Textarea](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/textarea/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)

## Why

Different components use different tags for the "title" of the field. This requires the user to understand internal nuances (is it a `label` or `legend`) to change its size. Having an option abstracting this and letting the component work out if it's `.govuk-label--...` or `.govuk-fieldset__legend--...` that's needed is much easier.

Developers, Tech writer

- [ ] The new option is available on all the components listed above
- [ ] The option is documented consistently across components

ourIssues.title: Character count component reads out hints in an unintuitive order when initially focused
ourIssues.body:
When a the character count is rendered on a text areas the aria-describeBy attribute lists the ID (suffixed with "-info") of the character count text and the ID of the hint text of the textarea (suffixed with "-hint") in that order. 

example:
**aria-describedby**="char-count-info q-textarea-hint"

This means that screen readers read the information referenced by those ID's in that order. 
Character count info read 1st
Textarea hint read 2nd

![image](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system-backlog/assets/119854428/687a8725-0ed0-4566-83f6-0554a3afffcb)

## What
> Need to have configuration so that the "-info" ID is appended after the textarea "-hint" ID. 

## Why

ourIssues.title: WCAG 2.2: Investigate thickness of input focus state border
ourIssues.body:
## What
Investigate if the increased black border for the focus state of form inputs needs to be thicker.

## Why
During testing of components against [WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.4.13: focus appearance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html) as part of https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/4347, it was discovered that several form input components that use a similar "box highlight" style focus state fail this criterion. ourIssues.title: Change configuration API of CharacterCount
ourIssues.body:
## What

Change the configuration options that the CharacterCount component accepts and:
1. separate the `limit` from the `type` of what's counted (`"words"` or `"characters"`), instead of having `maxwords` and `maxlength` combining both `limit` and `type` and requiring that one takes precedence over the other
2. clarify that the `threshold` is indeed a `displayThreshold`, not the character/words threshold

3. I'll also throw in the mix to allow configuring the display threshold as a percentage or absolute value, but I'm not familiar as to why this is done via percentage at the moment. I find more natural to think "limit to 200 characters, warn starting at 150" rather than "limit to 200 characters, warn at 75%", but this may very well be personal and the decision to use percentage has probably stronger grounds than my feelings. This doesn't necessarily require two attributes as we could use:
- if the threshold is < 1, treat it as a percentage
- if it is >= 1, treat it as an absolute value

It's worth noting about 1 that the internals of the component kind of make that separation:
- `maxwords` and `maxlength` get translated into a unique `maxLength` instance variable
- the presence of `config.maxwords` is used in `if` similarly to checking if `type == 'words'`

As we introduce the new API, we'd deprecate the old one, which we'd remove in the next breaking release.
And we'll obviously need to document all that 😉 

## Why

[Original idea was proposed by Ollie as part of this discussion when configuring the CharacterCount component via JS](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/2837#issuecomment-1259386812). While it didn't solve the issue at hand (having to override the JS config slightly differently for the component), it did seem like a good idea to the both of us, especially as it paves the route to fix #1364 (for 1).

Second and third point are smaller changes, but could add some clarity 

## Who needs to work on this

Developers, Technical writers

## Who needs to review this

Developers, Technical writers

## Done when

- [ ] Decision on API is made
- [ ] New API is implemented
- [ ] Old API is deprecated
- [ ] Documentation is updated to reflect the new API and deprecations
- [ ] Issue is created to track removal of old API in next breaking release

ourIssues.title: Textarea hints and error messages are not read out if a value is already present (JAWS/Chrome)
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue
When using JAWS, moving focus to a textarea that already has a populated value does not read out any elements associated with the textarea by `aria-describedby`.

## Steps to reproduce the issue
1. Create an instance of the textarea or character count component that: (a) has a default value of any length; (b) has an associated hint, error message, or both; and (c) does not have a threshold, if it's a character count. 
2. With JAWS running, navigate to the page in Chrome.
3. Apply focus to the textarea using either keyboard or mouse.
4. Listen to what JAWS reads out.

An existing example can be found in [the character count's error state example](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/character-count/error/index.html) in the design system. I've also made [a bare minimum example as a fiddle](https://jsfiddle.net/querkmachine/3z6drbto/).

## Actual vs expected behaviour
Actual behaviour: JAWS will read out the input label and that it is a textarea that currently contains text.

Expected behaviour: JAWS will read out the label, that it is a textarea that currently contains text, plus any hints and error messages associated with the input via `aria-describedby`.

The issue does not appear to occur with `<input>` elements (be they empty or populated), or with empty `<textarea>`s.

## Environment 
- Operating system: Windows 10
- Browser: Google Chrome
- Browser version: 99
- GOV.UK Frontend Version: 4.0.1

Tested in both JAWS 2021.2103.174 and JAWS 2022.2202.38. 

I could not reproduce this in Firefox or IE when using JAWS, and not in any browser when using NVDA 2021.2.

ourIssues.title: Test that documented component options match the templates
ourIssues.body:
## What

Add tests that validate the documented options within our component YAML files (like [the button YAML file](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/f704053f8544e8d88acec68ca448b4cb992a76d2/src/components/button/button.yaml)) match the actual options used within the template / macro.

If the two do not match, the tests should fail.

There is as a ['work-in-progress' branch](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/test-definitions) for this work which currently does this, but needs some refactoring / documentation before it can be merged.

## Why

Currently we rely on human review to ensure that the documented options match reality. During a recent [firebreak](https://insidegovuk.blog.gov.uk/2018/05/03/firebreaks-on-gov-uk/) project, we explored whether we could do anything to catch these in our CI process.

The work found a number of inaccuracies in the documentation options:

- `attributes` not documented on the breadcrumbs and select components
- `describedBy` mistakenly documented on textarea and character count components
- `footer` component YAML misformed using `arguments` instead of `params`, which means the `meta` object is not documented correctly in the Design System
- `items[].name` mistakenly documented on radios – unlike checkboxes, this can only be set globally as having a set of radios with different names doesn't make any sense
- `title` not documented on the tabs component

This highlights the need to automate these checks, so we can make sure our documentation is correct.

ourIssues.title: Character count component counts code points, not characters
ourIssues.body:
The character count currently uses `string.length` to establish the length of the user input. `string.length` counts code units, not characters, and this can lead to some confusing results when using certain strings.

![A single emoji (👩🏻‍🚀) counted as 7 characters within the character count component](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/121939/50347110-699b5c00-052c-11e9-8944-6ad62d0014b4.png)


You can see this by trying the following strings into the character component:

| String | Result                                                                                                                                  |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| cat😹   | The emoji is counted as 2 code units, and the length is reported as *5* characters.                                                     |
| cafȩ́   | Each combining mark is counted separately, and the reported length is *6* characters.                                                   |
| 👩🏻‍🚀    | Because this emoji includes both gender and skin modifiers and a zero-width joiner, this single character is counted as *7* characters. |

We should probably find a less naive way to count characters in strings, but we also need to work out how this will work with any backend validation or data storage on a service, which may already be using a different definition of a 'character' (for example, where the backend or storage treats one character as one byte).

Further reading:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_encoding
- http://developer.teradata.com/blog/jasonstrimpel/2011/11/javascript-string-length-and-internationalizing-web-applications
- https://dmitripavlutin.com/what-every-javascript-developer-should-know-about-unicode/#33stringlength

communityIssues.title: Inconsistent components API
communityIssues.body:
The component API is inconsistent across components and in comparison with `govuk-frontend`.

In the table below there is a brief comparison in how `govuk-frontend` components are aligned in API with `govuk_publishing_components`

|Component               |API |
|---                      |---  |
Accordion                 | aligned
Back link                 | aligned
Breadcrumbs               | misaligned
Button                    | slightly misaligned (start)
Character count           | slightly misaligned (nesting)
Checkboxes                | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Date input                | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Details                   | misaligned
Error message             | aligned
Error summary             | misaligned
Fieldset                  | misaligned
File upload               | aligned
Footer                    | aligned
Header                    | slightly misaligned (navigation_items)
Inset text                | aligned
Panel                     | misaligned
Phase banner              | misaligned
Radios                    | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Select                    | slightly misaligned (options)
Skip link                 | aligned
Summary list              | slightly misaligned (items)
Table                     | aligned
Tabs                      | misaligned
Text input                | aligned
Textarea                  | aligned
Warning text              | slightly misaligned (iconFallbackText)

We can see a few common differences between to two API models:
- for arrays, `govuk-frontend` uses the generic `items` (in most cases) whereas `govuk_publishing_components` uses the name of the component (e.g. `attachments` for the attachment list component or `breadcrumbs` for the breadcrumbs component)
- for web addresses/paths `govuk-frontend` uses `href` whereas in `govuk_publishing_components` we often find `url` (e.g. breadcrumbs component)

It's worth mentioning that not even `govuk-frontend`'s API is consistent (e.g. `errorList` instead of `items` in the Error summary component, or differences in nesting)

A few advantages of making the API consistent:
- increases developers' confidence when calling components with arguments (without constantly checking examples in the guide)
- prototyping and production will use the same config object (can be easily copied over in both directions)
- applications can prepare the data to be fed into components consistently using helpers
- it would be easier to swap one component with another

I'm creating this to raise awareness of the differences, hopefully generate discussions around how good looks like and aim for consistency and convergency. API alignment requires at least a breaking change and some replacements across applications – which is not an easy process. For this reason, having a clear vision about how we want it to look like would save us from doing this more than once.

ourIssues.title: Inconsistent Nunjucks parameter names for aria-label
ourIssues.body:
There are several components which allow you to pass the text for the `aria-label` on the component's wrapper element. The names of these parameters are inconsistent despite them doing the same thing.

[Cookie banner](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/cookie-banner/template.njk#L4) and [service navigation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/service-navigation/template.njk#L95) use `ariaLabel`. 

[Pagination](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/pagination/template.njk#L53) uses `landmarkLabel` and [breadcrumbs](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/breadcrumbs/template.njk#L14) uses `labelText`.

Pagination also [includes a visuallyHiddenText param](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/pagination/template.njk#L44) for pagination items. On most components, `visuallyHiddenText` params are appended to the visible text (for example [in summary card actions](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/summary-list/template.njk#L7)); pagination is the only example I can find where `visuallyHiddenText` is passed directly to `aria-label`, completely overriding any visual label

The documentation for the params is also structured differently. For example the docs for pagination and breadcrumbs don't mention that the value will be used as the `aria-label`, while they do for cookie banner and service navigation.

Are any of these differences intentional? I think `ariaLabel` is clearest about what the params actually do, with `[thing]AriaLabel` for labels of child elements (eg password uses `showPasswordAriaLabelText`, though again the `Text` makes that inconsistent)

ourIssues.title: Adjust components to scale with android system font size
ourIssues.body:
## What
Ensure as many of our components as possible are responding when viewing govuk-frontend web pages on android devices and adjusting android's system font size.

## Why
Govuk-frontend web pages should respect accessibility settigns and respond to them as expected.

## Steps to replicate
Tested in chrome on browserstack's Galaxy S23 instance as it's easy to notice the issue due to the device's large font size scale.

1. Go to the settings of the testing device and locate the setting to adjust device font size
2. Increase font size (recommend max in order to visualise issue more clearly)
3. Open a govuk-frontend web page on a browser on an android device eg: [the review app's announcements page](https://govuk-frontend-review.herokuapp.com/full-page-examples/announcements)

Notice that the breadcrumbs have not increased in size. Digging into the runtime styles, you will find that rem values of other elements on the page have adjusted in response to the font size change but the breadcrumbs haven't.

![Android browser showing an announcements page with scaled up font size except for the breadcrumbs element](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/assets/64783893/66ecb7d1-bf9e-459a-987c-8c85176a26b7)

## Notes
### Considerations from the spec
The likely reason this is happening can be found in CSS Mobile Text Size section of the CSS spec, specifically [2.2: Conditions that suppress adjustment](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-size-adjust/#default-adjustment-conditions). This section notes 4 reasons that would suppress text size adjustment. From initial testing, certain components can be 'fixed' by removing their block level positioning rules eg: components that have `display: inline-block`. We should be able to use `inline-block` on components and the text size adjustment not be suppressed. Recommend using the the spec in figuring out a solution.

### Impacted components
- Accordion
- Back link
- Breadcrumbs
- Button, and places consumed
    - Cookie banner buttons
    - Exit this page
- Checkboxes
- Details (not the content)
- File upload
- Some of the footer's links
- Header menu
- Notification banner
- Pagination
- Radios
- Select

ourIssues.title: Improve Language Navigation guidance on not losing data in forms when navigating between languages
ourIssues.body:
<!--

  This is a template for any issues that aren’t bug reports or new feature requests. The headings in this section provide examples of the information you might want to include, but feel free to add/delete sections where appropriate.

-->

## What

Improve Language Navigation guidance on not losing data in forms when using the component so that it's clearer what the behaviour should be

> Make sure the user does not lose any data they’ve entered when they navigate to another language. Do not ask the user to re-enter information they’ve already given.

https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/language-navigation/

## Why

We have [had some feedback ](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/discussions/5620#discussioncomment-18582218)that it's not clear in practice if this means keeping the users currently inputted data on a page or just keeping the data from the overall user journey.

Since this is a non-standard thing to do, we think it's likely other developers will wonder what they're aiming for.

There's some potential improvements to this:
- improving the guidance so it's clear that it includes users' un-submitted input 
- guidance around explaining at a high level how to achieve this functionality, similar to what we do for Cookie banner and Form validation (for developers)

## Background

This content was originally added in response to HMRC's welsh language toggle guidance. They detailed why they chose to keep data between page views in some feedback of note:

> welsh users will toggle back and forth between languages to ensure understanding of unfamiliar words and/or to check that both journeys are the same

> welsh speakers familiar with uncommon english specific to the context benefit from both the ability to toggle easily, and from these terms being shown in brackets within the welsh service (to avoid having to do as much switching)

> users prefer english/welsh toggle to whole journey language switching and absence of feature to toggle within service (only being able to select at start) tested negatively

https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/discussions/5351#discussioncomment-17278309

## Who needs to work on this

Content designer, developer

## Who needs to review this

Content designer, developer

## Done when

- [ ] the guidance is clearer on exactly what data should be persisted
- [ ] we've considered if extended guidance is appropriate
