backlog.title: Suggested new component - Side menu
backlog.body:
What

Give a brief description of the style, component or pattern you want to propose.

Context:
We are in the final stages of building an e-learning service using the GDS design system. We have completed numerous rounds of user testing and already gone through one Alpha and Beta Assessment.
What:
A right-hand sidebar navigation menu which allows users to easily see their progression through a course and be able to navigate back and forth through chapters.
Current version

In-situ

Iterations from user testing

Why

Explain why you think this should be added to the GOV.UK Design System.

In our alpha assessment, we were challenged to explore if there was a user need to see their progression through the course and also to be able to navigate back and forth through the chapters. We tested various variations of a sidebar navigation similar to those found in lots of e-learning platforms. During testing, we found that some users naturally used the sidebar to return to topics earlier in the course and used it to be aware of their progression and estimate their completion time.
Design-wise, we didn’t want to reinvent the wheel so we built on existing sidebar navigation patterns from GOV.UK publishing such as the contents list on the publishing service (https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/contents_list) and the related content sidebar on many start pages. We iterated the design several times to make it simple and accessible. For instance, we made some headers in the sidebar visually hidden so they would give context to screen reader users whilst avoiding confusion for sighted users who had initially struggled with the previous design.


What evidence do you have that it's needed by multiple services across government?


In the our beta assessment, we were praised on our work developing this pattern and asked to play it back into the community:
‘the team has validated the user need to track progress within training modules, has designed a pattern that is working for their beta users, and is planning to continue iterating this pattern - the panel would encourage the team to share this pattern and research findings with the design system community’


What evidence do you have that it meets the needs of the users of those services?


We have tested and validated this component in several rounds of qual research with 5-10 people in each round, and in Private Beta testing with over 1200 people (with quant showing that people successfully use this when required, and qual feedback only positive and no negative on the latest version).
Our user testing so far has validated the need for this component and as mentioned has been praised so far by assessors. But we would love to share it with the community to get a wider perspective and possible use cases.


Have you checked that it doesn't already exist in the GOV.UK Design System?


Yes
Anything else

Include links to any examples, research or code to support your proposal, if available.

ourIssues.title: Review the use of aria-label on a <ul> element in the site navigation menu
ourIssues.body:
## What
We use an `aria-label` on our sub-navigation list `<ul>`. This causes HTML validation issues, so we need to make the call on whether we keep it as an exception, add an explicit `aria-role` to keep validation happy, or get rid of it and find another solution.

## Why
Previously, we added an `aria-label` to the main site nav's Community sub-menu to make a better experience for screenreaders:  https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/commit/4ff06e4961bcd4a147d580d1d5ac2736fe9f6ec3

Recently, we [added HTML linting](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/pull/2569), and it flagged this as `aria-label-misuse`.

If we assign an explicit `role` to the labelled list, the HTML validator is sated and complains no longer.

However, it's a bit unclear which `role` we'd want to add - `navigation` is out since this subnav is already contained within a `nav` parent, and `menu` [might not be right for this situation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/pull/2569#discussion_r1115422380).

We could avoid this debate if we just find a solution that doesn't involve ARIA. First step would probably be to just remove the `aria-label` and test whether it reads fine in multiple screenreaders.

If it’s missing context without the aria-label, we could look at using a bit of ‘visually-hidden’ instead of an aria-label. Would need to test to see if it works consistently across all screen readers though.

## Who needs to work on this
Developer, Accessibility specialist(?)

## Who needs to review this
Developer, Accessibility specialist

## Done when

- [ ] We have a solution that is both valid HTML, and a good experience for screenreaders.
- [ ] We have implemented that solution (this will likely involve [removing the inline validation exception](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/blob/9ba07459f46a6e9738067c7ec90da6dd22f3a1b6/views/partials/_navigation.njk#L14))

backlog.title: QR codes
backlog.body:
What
QR codes are a machine-readable code consisting of an array of black and white squares, typically used for storing URLs or other information for reading by the camera on a smartphone.

Whilst QR codes once generated look fairly standard and may not be too much up for debate, when and how to use them is.
Why
Government appears to be using QR codes more frequently. We are now seeing them used as part of track and trace to scan into a venue and the NHS include them in some of their letters to link users to content without having to enter the url manually.
On GOV.UK Notify, in the past few months we have seen a good handful of support requests in the past few months asking about support for QR codes.
At the moment it's not clear to me

when you should use a QR code
when you should NOT use a QR code
are they accessible?
whether users trust QR codes in terms of phishing
if you are using a QR, how you should use it. For example, maybe you should always provide the link alongside the QR code for those users not using a phone or without a camera
where/how you should you generate these (should you use a third party website for example)
any other security considerations

Anything else
https://www.revk.uk/2020/09/how-not-to-qr-nhs-c19-app.html

ourIssues.title: Transitioning Access QR Codes to Apple & Google Wallets
ourIssues.body:
We are working on a project that allows users to fill in a publicly accessible form to apply for access to maritime locations across the UK. Once a user completes an application, they receive a reference number and a QR code is shown at the end of the form. This information is also sent to them via a confirmation email.

To streamline operations on-site, this user flow allows applicants to present the QR code to be scanned by a secondary system, rather than having to manually present or read out a reference number. Currently, a user can have multiple QR codes and must download or screenshot them if they want to keep them handy on their mobile device.

During recent user testing, multiple participants raised that they would highly prefer to store these QR codes directly within their device’s native wallet (Apple Wallet and Google Wallet) for easier access and management when arriving at a maritime location.

Following this feedback, we built a proof of concept (PoC) that successfully allows users to download and add a wallet item for both iOS and Android. We have consulted the Government Digital Service (GDS) on our research and approach, and they have agreed that this is a sensible direction.

While we are aware of and have engaged with the [GOV.UK](http://gov.uk/) Wallet team, we believe that in the short term, having this native wallet functionality integrated directly into our service makes the most sense for our users.

Certificate & Licensing Management
To create and distribute native wallet items, both Apple and Google require signed certificates linked to developer licences. For our PoC, we funded and used our own team’s developer licence. However, for a production-ready solution, we believe the long-term enterprise licences, billing, and cryptographic signing keys should be managed centrally by the Home Office. We need to identify exactly which team or department handles this central governance.

Questions & Guidance Requested
To bridge the gap between our engineering team and corporate security and to move this wallet integration forward we are seeking guidance on the following:

Community Knowledge: Has anyone else in the GDS/wider government ecosystem built a similar native wallet workflow? If so, could you point us in their direction so we can learn more about their architectural approach, licensing setup, and the challenges they faced?
Licensing, Funding, & Governance Contact: Strategically, we need the official enterprise developer licences and associated billing to be handled at the departmental level. Who or which team within the Home Office should we reach out to in order to arrange central provisioning, corporate funding/billing, and security approval for these official accounts?

ourIssues.title: Confirm accessibility and use cases of using `<h2>` or deeper headings as label or legend of fields
ourIssues.body:
<!--

  This is a template for any issues that aren’t bug reports or new feature requests. The headings in this section provide examples of the information you might want to include, but feel free to add/delete sections where appropriate.

-->

## What

Confirm in which situation it can make sense and not cause accessibility issues to use an `<h2>` or deeper as a lable or legend of one of our form field components.

## Why

Our form field components can currently use an `<h1>` as their label or legend through the `isPageHeading` option. We're investigating whether a `headingLevel` option allowing arbitrary heading levels would be useful. Particularly, we'd like to understand the use cases when it makes sense and those when it doesn't, as well as possible accessibility constraints so we can document the possible future option appropriately.

This may be useful to avoid text looking like a [heading because of `govuk-label--<SIZE>` classes being flagged as an accessibility issue if the label is not marked up as a heading](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/5240).

## Who needs to work on this

Accessibility Specialist, Developers, maybe Designers?

## Who needs to review this

Accessibility Specialist, Developers, maybe Designers?

## Done when

- [ ] We've documented use case and accessibility constraints enough to inform our decision and the option's documentation.

ourIssues.title: Add `size` option to form input component labels
ourIssues.body:
<!--

  This is a template for any issues that aren’t bug reports or new feature requests. The headings in this section provide examples of the information you might want to include, but feel free to add/delete sections where appropriate.

-->

## What

Allow form field components to receive a new `size` option in their `label` or `legend` option for easily controlling the text size of their label or legend. The option should receive a t-shirt size and set the appropriate `.govuk-label--<T_SHIRT_SIZE>` or `.govuk-fieldset__legend--<T_SHIRT_SIZE>` on the label or legend.

For components using a `label` the option should be implemented by adding a [new option to our internal Label component](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/label) and passing the option through. For those using a `legend`, the public Fieldset component should get an update first in a similar fashion.

The affected components are:
- [Character Count](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/character-count/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Textarea)
- [Checkboxes](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/checkboxes/template.njk) (forwarding the option to either Fieldset)
- [Date Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Fieldset](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk)
- [File Upload](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/file-upload/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Label](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/label/template.njk)
- [Password Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/password-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Input)
- [Radios](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/radios/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Select](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/select/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Textarea](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/textarea/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)

## Why

Different components use different tags for the "title" of the field. This requires the user to understand internal nuances (is it a `label` or `legend`) to change its size. Having an option abstracting this and letting the component work out if it's `.govuk-label--...` or `.govuk-fieldset__legend--...` that's needed is much easier.

## Who needs to work on this

Developers, Tech writer

## Who needs to review this

Developers, Tech writer

## Done when

- [ ] The new option is available on all the components listed above
- [ ] The option is documented consistently across components

ourIssues.title: Hint text for radio/checkbox groups gets read out repeatedly by VoiceOver
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

When arrowing through a form with a radio (or checkbox) group that has a hint, VoiceOver on iOS reads out the hint text repeatedly.
While this is not a WCAG fail and is probably not a bug in the Design System itself, it can be annoying to screen reader users.


## Steps to reproduce the issue

Open our [inline radios example](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/inline/) and arrow through the page (VO + right arrow).


## Actual vs expected behaviour

I don't know what is supposed to happen according to the spec, I only know what happens in all other major screen readers. I don't know if this means it's a bug in VoiceOver or just a different way how VoiceOver does things.

VoiceOver reads out the hint text:

* when arrowing to the legend
* (obviously also when arrowing to the hint text itself)
* when arrowing to the first radio button
* when arrowing to the second (and potential subsequent) radio buttons

The second and third are to be expected, the first and last not.
All other major screen readers only read the hint text when arrowing to the first radio button they encounter (and to the hint text itself).


## Environment

This happens with VoiceOver on iOS but also to some degree on macOS.
(It's less bad on macOS as the hint text doesn't get read out when arrowing to the legend.)

Tested in Safari on an iPad with iOS version 18.3.1 and a MacBook with macOS version 15.3.2.

A user has reported that this issue was not happening on iOS version 16.

ourIssues.title: Improve documentation of `beforeInput(s)` and `afterInput(s)` options of our form control components
ourIssues.body:
<!--

  This is a template for any issues that aren’t bug reports or new feature requests. The headings in this section provide examples of the information you might want to include, but feel free to add/delete sections where appropriate.

-->

## What

Research and document which kind of content is OK/not OK to put in the `beforeInput(s)` and `afterInput(s)` options of our form components, introduced in #4567 to ensure all users (especially those using assistive technology) get proper access to the content.

## Why

Because the content ends up inside a form field, where the control is associated to the label/legend and any error/hint, there's a risk that content injected through `beforeInput(s)`/`afterInput(s)` options gets missed when navigating from field to field, the focus skipping over the content to the next form field. 

This means we may want to suggest restrictions as to which content is suitable for these options, possible techniques to link the content so it gets announced when navigating from field to field, and possibly a warning to test thoroughly.

## Who needs to work on this

Developers, Accessibility specialist, possibly Designers

## Who needs to review this

Developers, Accessibility specialist, possibly Designers 

## Done when

- [ ] We've clarified how to best use the `beforeInput(s)` and `afterInput(s)` options of our form components.

ourIssues.title: Suggestion: Extend heading padding-top adjustment to cover other heading like elements.
NVDA does not read hints or error messages when tabbing to checkboxes
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

This is an NVDA bug, but I'm filing an issue here because it affects the accessibility of GOV.UK Frontend so I thought you may want a record of it.

When a checkbox inside a fieldset gets focus, any hint or error message associated with the fieldset should be read out after the legend and before the checkbox label. They're associated with the fieldset via `aria-describedby`. However, NVDA only reads the legend and checkbox label, not the hint or error. This means that NVDA users may be unaware that the grouping has a hint or an error.

For example, the speech output for [this example](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/checkboxes/error/index.html) with a hint and an error is:

> What is your nationality?  grouping  clickable  British  check box  not checked    including English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish

Note that this only affects checkboxes. Radios use the same structure and are unaffected.

[An NVDA issue for this bug](https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/12718) has been open since 2021 but unfortunately it doesn't look like there's been much progress towards a fix. It looks like [this commenter](https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/12718#issuecomment-1533364655) has also come across this issue while using GOV.UK Frontend though.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

See CodePen at https://codepen.io/matteason/pen/PoyBwYM or one of the GOV.UK Design System examples (eg [checkboxes](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/checkboxes/with-none-option-in-error/index.html))

Open NVDA, navigate to the example page and tab through the form fields

## Actual vs expected behaviour

Hints should be read for all component types in the example, but they're only read for text inputs and radios

## Environment (where applicable)

- Operating system: Windows 10
- Browser: Firefox 112.0, Chrome 112.0.5615.138
- GOV.UK Frontend Version: 4.6.0

ourIssues.title: Allow `govuk-font-size` to be called with a 't-shirt size' for `$size`
ourIssues.body:
## Context

We have the concept of 't-shirt sizes' (`xl`, `l`, `m`, `s`, `xs`) for text, for example headings, labels, legends, table captions.

They use consistent font sizes, but the mapping of t-shirt size to underlying font size is not defined anywhere in the codebase – it's just defined in each place individually and kept in sync.

For example, `xl` maps to a font size of 48 (on desktop):

https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/34806961fffb5e3b43de9fbda5f9a08f376ec196/src/govuk/core/_typography.scss#L11-L19

https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/34806961fffb5e3b43de9fbda5f9a08f376ec196/src/govuk/components/table/_index.scss#L53-L56

https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/34806961fffb5e3b43de9fbda5f9a08f376ec196/src/govuk/components/label/_index.scss#L13-L16

https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/34806961fffb5e3b43de9fbda5f9a08f376ec196/src/govuk/components/fieldset/_index.scss#L37-L40

We should consider updating `govuk-typography-responsive` to accept a t-shirt size, and automatically use the underlying size from the `$govuk-typography-scale`.

This would also allow calls to govuk-font to accept a t-shirt size, for example:

```scss
@include govuk-font($size: xl, $weight: bold);
```

This would also provide a way for components (ours, and downstream) to match with the heading sizes without, for example, needing to extend a heading class.

## Alternatives

Without this, we need to keep the various 't-shirt-sized' components in the codebase in sync manually, and there is no easy way for consumers to use the xl, l sizing in their own codebase without manually keeping them in sync.

## Additional information (if applicable)

This does introduce another (optional) layer of abstraction, but it feels like a useful one?

We might also want to consider extending the typography overrides to provide e.g. `govuk-!-font-size-xl` classes.

ourIssues.title: Legend (and hint and error message) for the group of radios / checkboxes announced when focusing a conditionally revealed field whilst using VoiceOver
ourIssues.body:
Conditionally revealed controls are inside the `<fieldset>` that wraps the radios / checkboxes.

This could potentially cause confusion, as in VoiceOver the legend (and any other text associated with the fieldset using `aria-describedby`, such as a hint or error message) is read out when focusing the conditionally revealed content.

![Screenshot 2020-10-16 at 13 03 20](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/121939/96256125-fe980080-0faf-11eb-9da5-289e0c39a63e.png)

For example, when focusing the conditionally revealed 'email address' field in the example from the Design System (above), Voiceover with Safari (14) on macOS (10.15.7) announces:

> "Email address, edit text, How would you like to be contacted? Select all options that are relevant to you. You are currently on a text field. To enter text in this field, type."

The hint text "Select all options that are relevant to you" applies to the set of checkboxes, and does not make sense in the context of the email address field.

ourIssues.title: The logical order of conditionally revealed content as it appears within a set of radios or checkboxes can be confusing
ourIssues.body:
The conditionally revealed content appears immediately after the control that reveals it. This means that it’s 'mixed up' within the logical order of the set of checkboxes or radios.

![design-system service gov uk_components_checkboxes_conditional-reveal_index html (2)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/121939/96256804-3784a500-0fb1-11eb-9814-e520f593002d.png)

This can cause confusion for screen reader users, as illustrated by this research finding from the checkboxes backlog issue:

> [We've just taken] our agent facing service to usability testing with someone who uses JAWS. Our biggest issue that we kept encountering was the use of conditional reveal, we think that with familiarity this issue would go away but it's definitely something we want to just work straight away without explanation.
> 
> User was presented with radio buttons as seen below:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5321135/65248454-19b4ea00-daea-11e9-9aa2-3adef03eea9d.png)
> The user selected yes and then tabbed as they thought they had completed the section.
> It read out the label for the conditionally revealed input (although this was inconsistent, we want to get a JAWS device over the coming weeks and try and replicate the different behaviours, as sometimes the label was getting skipped)
> 
> The user then used the cursor down option in JAWS to see what else was on the page, and the next thing was "no"; this caused a lot of confusion because they thought it had jumped into the next radio button group, so this caused a lot of tabbing back and forth to try and find out where that "no" was coming from, at this point we then explained where that conditional content was in relation to the page. 
> 
> We have multiple other questions like this with similar content being revealed and this was a consistent theme, unsure which radio group they were in after entering the conditionally revealed content. This was also an issue when we had a legend explaining the question which was then being read out before the "no", because then it was as if tab had put them backwards in the form.
> 
> To summarise, user pressed tab after selecting radio button, which put them into the conditionally revealed content, they thought that was the next question so when they looked at the next part of the page and it was the remaining radio options they were completely unsure of where they were.
> 
> _Originally posted by @alexnewmannn in https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system-backlog/issue_comments/533134507_

ourIssues.title: Handle `caller` in test fixtures
Support using captions with labels and legends as headings
ourIssues.body: ## What A user requested that we make [labels and legends as page headings](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/get-started/labels-legends-headings/) support the use of [captions](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/typography/#headings-with-captions). Here's an example from their service where the page heading is a legend and also has a caption: If we decide to do this, we should: 1. Make sure that having label/legend with a caption above and a hint below makes sense visually because hints and captions look quite similar. 2. Test this with assistive technologies. With legends as headings it's not clear whether the caption should be inside the legend, fieldset or form group. ## Why This seems like a fairly common use case and at the moment it can't be achieved with the macro. You can still do this using the HTML version of the pattern. If we don't want to support the use case we could consider adding documentation to explain that. ## Who needs to know about this Devs, Chris

ourIssues.title: Limiting content width when using wider page layouts
ourIssues.body:
Raising this as it's something we've come across and perhaps other teams would too.

My service is about to move to a wider default page width - 1200px. We do this to accommodate our service's needs and take advantage of our users having more screen real estate.

In moving to 1200px width, it means lines of content inside a 2/3 column now become too long.

The design system site itself solves this by [setting max width on specific elements](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/blob/master/src/stylesheets/main.scss#L69).

We've done similar, but set a fixed width of `722px` for all elements.

Should these max-widths on content lines be set by default?

## Suggestion:

Given the design system supports other widths, I wonder if one of the following might happen:

1. Review guidance on width in [grid system](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/layout/#grid-system) - would be good to mention explicitly that services will need to limit content lines.
2. Include styles to limit specific items to no more than x width.

NB - the design system has 'Limiting width of content' - but this is not specific about textual content - which could possibly be covered separately.

## Detail

As well as the elements the design system site limits, we're also considering following elements:
* legend,
* label,
* govuk-hint,
* input,
* textarea,
* select,
* govuk-details__summary,
* govuk-details__text,
* govuk-inset-text,
* govuk-panel__body,
* govuk-warning-text__text

ourIssues.title: Make it easier to add a hint or an error message to a fieldset
ourIssues.body:
## What

If you want to use the fieldset component to group related fields, for example asking for a street address, you need to take care of including the hint / error message components separately and do extra work to associate them with the fieldset.

We do not provide any examples or guidance on how to do this, and it would be easy to get wrong (for example, by not creating the association with the fieldset)

It therefore seems like it would be useful if the fieldset component accepted `hint` and `errorMessage` objects and took care of this association itself.

## Why

This was requested by @edwardhorsford in https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/issues/778#issuecomment-459047140.

## Additional information

The radios, checkbox and date input components all use hints and error messages which are then associated with the fieldset using `aria-describedby`. However, this logic is handled (and therefore duplicated) within the individual components.

Moving this logic to the fieldset component _might_ allow us to simplify the repeated logic in the radios, checkboxes and date input components. However, it's not clear what should happen to the hint / error message [if you do not include a fieldset](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/62d3de38036b858b1dd85c5bd8c027830fab5a3d/src/components/date-input/template.njk#L79-L96).

ourIssues.title: Add label or legend param to date-input
Ability to group radio buttons / checkboxes within sub-headings
ourIssues.body:
Hi.

I'm wondering how best to support radio buttons (and checkboxes) which have sub-groups with headings?

Currently, you can use multiple `govukRadios` macros which share the same `name` attribute, however because they use a `data-module` attribute to scope the conditional reveals, these don't work properly across the groups.

Alternatively, you can using a single macro and put headings in using `divider`s, but these don't currently support HTML markup.

On a related not, it's unclear whether the best output would be nested `<fieldset>`s with `<legend>`s, or a single `<fieldset>` with headings and either aria attributes or visually-hidden prefixes to associate labels with their headings.

ourIssues.title: Expand documentation of fieldset to discuss when to add `role="group"`
ourIssues.body:
The date component has `role="group"` on its fieldset. The fieldset component example doesn't.

Via @36degrees, this is what the [code has to say](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/6c9d8d7191edb18e8a46d2a383e311f397367946/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk#L91-L94):
>We override the fieldset's role to 'group' because otherwise JAWS does not
    announce the description for a fieldset comprised of text inputs, but
    adding the role to the fieldset always makes the output overly verbose for
    radio buttons or checkboxes.

If this is still true, then it would be good to add something to the fieldset example discussing it. It may not be relevant to radios and checkboxes, but I suspect most usages of the fieldset component itself are likely for _other_ elements.

## Suggestion

ourIssues.title: Typography for labels on patterns with multiple fields
ourIssues.body:
Where patterns have multiple fields on a single page (rather than just one, where the label or legend doubles as the `<h1>`), it is currently unclear what typographic weight should be applied to the field labels (or legends).

[Addresses](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/addresses/) and [Bank details](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/bank-details/) suggest using regular weight, Address lookup (the video) and [Payment card details](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/payment-card-details/) suggest using `s`.

The Getting started page has a section on [styling options for labels and legends](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/get-started/labels-legends-headings/#styling-options-for-labels-and-legends) which also suggest that `m` is an option if needed.

Should the patterns in the Design System have consistency between them in typography (ie all use `s` or regular)? Or is there a reason for the differences?  And should those pages make clear whether the typography in the patterns can be changed if necessary, or whether they should be copied exactly as they are?

communityIssues.title: Radio: `heading_caption` renders at `govuk-caption-m` when `heading_level` is 0
communityIssues.body: ## Cause [_radio.html.erb](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk_publishing_components/blob/main/app/views/govuk_publishing_components/components/_radio.html.erb) works out `size` (default `m`, or `heading_size` if valid) and uses it for the caption class (`govuk-caption-#{size}`). Since #5809, the legend's `govuk-fieldset__legend--{size}` class is skipped when `heading_level == "span"` (`heading_level: 0`) but the caption still uses `size`. ## Consequences With `heading_level: 0` and a `heading_caption` a sized caption sits above regular-weight legend text: ``` Question 3 of 9 What is your favourite skittle? ``` No test covers a caption at `heading_level: 0`. ### Possible approach Decide what a caption means on a non-heading legend, then: - don't render it at level 0 or - size it to match the unsized legend or - leave it as it is and add a test that documents that ### Proposed rating (for triage) - **Impact of leaving it**: Low (edge case, needs `heading_level: 0` plus a caption, and I don't yet know of any consumers doing that) - **Effort to fix**: Low (one condition in template, plus a spec) - **Overall**: Low ### Things to check - Whether any apps pass `heading_level: 0` with `heading caption` (org-wide code search) - What the design system says about captions on non-heading legends ### Context Spotted while reviewing #5809

communityIssues.title: Inconsistent components API
communityIssues.body:
The component API is inconsistent across components and in comparison with `govuk-frontend`.

In the table below there is a brief comparison in how `govuk-frontend` components are aligned in API with `govuk_publishing_components`

|Component               |API |
|---                      |---  |
Accordion                 | aligned
Back link                 | aligned
Breadcrumbs               | misaligned
Button                    | slightly misaligned (start)
Character count           | slightly misaligned (nesting)
Checkboxes                | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Date input                | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Details                   | misaligned
Error message             | aligned
Error summary             | misaligned
Fieldset                  | misaligned
File upload               | aligned
Footer                    | aligned
Header                    | slightly misaligned (navigation_items)
Inset text                | aligned
Panel                     | misaligned
Phase banner              | misaligned
Radios                    | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Select                    | slightly misaligned (options)
Skip link                 | aligned
Summary list              | slightly misaligned (items)
Table                     | aligned
Tabs                      | misaligned
Text input                | aligned
Textarea                  | aligned
Warning text              | slightly misaligned (iconFallbackText)

We can see a few common differences between to two API models:
- for arrays, `govuk-frontend` uses the generic `items` (in most cases) whereas `govuk_publishing_components` uses the name of the component (e.g. `attachments` for the attachment list component or `breadcrumbs` for the breadcrumbs component)
- for web addresses/paths `govuk-frontend` uses `href` whereas in `govuk_publishing_components` we often find `url` (e.g. breadcrumbs component)

It's worth mentioning that not even `govuk-frontend`'s API is consistent (e.g. `errorList` instead of `items` in the Error summary component, or differences in nesting)

A few advantages of making the API consistent:
- increases developers' confidence when calling components with arguments (without constantly checking examples in the guide)
- prototyping and production will use the same config object (can be easily copied over in both directions)
- applications can prepare the data to be fed into components consistently using helpers
- it would be easier to swap one component with another

I'm creating this to raise awareness of the differences, hopefully generate discussions around how good looks like and aim for consistency and convergency. API alignment requires at least a breaking change and some replacements across applications – which is not an easy process. For this reason, having a clear vision about how we want it to look like would save us from doing this more than once.

communityIssues.title: Feature suggestion: ability to set global defaults
communityIssues.body:
It would be useful for a team to be able to set global defaults that can be used in components.

My specific use case is defaulting radios and checkboxes to their small variants. I work on an internal-facing service and we only ever want to use small radios and checkboxes. At the moment we need to manually set `"small": true` on each and every usage. It's very possible we could forget to do this. It would be nicer if we could provide a global settings object/config that can be applied on to components.

Something like:

```json
nhsukFrontend: {
  label: { size: "l" },
  legend: { size: "l" },
  radios: { small: true },
  checkboxes: { small: true }
}
```

communityIssues.title: Remove redundant explicit role attributes from HTML5 elements
communityIssues.body:
## What

Remove the explicit role attribute on HTML elements that have the same role implicitly, including:

* the `<span>` element in the card component, which has a `text` role on the header text
* the `<nav>` element in the contents list component, which has a `navigation` role
* the `<ul>` element in the do and don't list component, which has a `list` role
* the `<footer>` element in the footer component, which has a `contentinfo` role
* the `<header>` element in the header component, which has a `banner` role
* the `<nav>` element in the pagination component, which has a `navigation` role
* the `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tr>`, `<td>` and `<th>` elements in the table component ([see issue](https://github.com/nhsuk/nhsuk-frontend/issues/1092))

In some places we include an explicit `group` role on `<fieldset>` elements (e.g. the date input) to ensure that JAWS announces the accessible description – we should **leave this in place** unless we're able to do further investigation and understand whether this is still needed.

Update our [HTML validation rules](https://github.com/nhsuk/nhsuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/nhsuk-frontend-review/.htmlvalidate.mjs) accordingly ([see workarounds](https://github.com/nhsuk/nhsuk-frontend/commit/74aceef346383b5678b0d715ade6a8da3948f0ba)).

## Why

These have historically been set because older browsers ([noteably Internet Explorer](https://web.archive.org/web/20180103181655/https://connect.microsoft.com/IE/feedback/details/804723/html5-structural-elements-not-exposed-via-accessibility-api)) do not [map these implicit roles correctly](https://www.html5accessibility.com/).

As our browser support model has evolved, we can now remove these implicit roles.

See related issue from GOV.UK Frontend:

* https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/4708

The `data-prevent-double-click` attribute does not seem to be working with Edge.

Actual: The form submits as many times as the user can click before the next page loads

<!--

## What

Allow form field components to receive a new `size` option in their `label` or `legend` option for easily controlling the text size of their label or legend. For those using a `legend`, the public Fieldset component should get an update first in a similar fashion.

The affected components are:
- [Character Count](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/character-count/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Textarea)
- [Checkboxes](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/checkboxes/template.njk) (forwarding the option to either Fieldset)
- [Date Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Fieldset](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk)
- [File Upload](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/file-upload/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Label](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/label/template.njk)
- [Password Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/password-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Input)
- [Radios](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/radios/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Select](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/select/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Textarea](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/textarea/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)

## Why

Different components use different tags for the "title" of the field. This requires the user to understand internal nuances (is it a `label` or `legend`) to change its size. Having an option abstracting this and letting the component work out if it's `.govuk-label--...` or `.govuk-fieldset__legend--...` that's needed is much easier.

## Who needs to work on this

Developers, Tech writer

## Who needs to review this

Developers, Tech writer

## Done when

- [ ] The new option is available on all the components listed above
- [ ] The option is documented consistently across components

ourIssues.title: Add the ability to customise the classes on pagination links
ourIssues.body:
## Related component

[Pagination](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/pagination/)

## Context

Currently it isn't possible to add custom classes to individual links (neither items nor the previous/next links) within the pagination.

This limits the possibility of applying different or customised styling to them, such as [removing the visited state](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/links/#links-without-a-visited-state). 

## Alternatives

If using the Nunjucks macro, these links can only be changed through writing additional CSS that hooks onto the component's wrapper. 

Otherwise, the user must use the pure HTML version of the component or fork the macro themselves.

## Additional information

This feature was requested by a user via support.

Being able to remove visited states particularly seems like a useful function for search result pages, where the URL for a page may not be unique even though the page content is totally different.

ourIssues.title: Inconsistent Nunjucks parameter names for aria-label
ourIssues.body:
There are several components which allow you to pass the text for the `aria-label` on the component's wrapper element. The names of these parameters are inconsistent despite them doing the same thing.

[Cookie banner](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/cookie-banner/template.njk#L4) and [service navigation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/service-navigation/template.njk#L95) use `ariaLabel`. 

[Pagination](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/pagination/template.njk#L53) uses `landmarkLabel` and [breadcrumbs](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/breadcrumbs/template.njk#L14) uses `labelText`.

Pagination also [includes a visuallyHiddenText param](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/pagination/template.njk#L44) for pagination items. On most components, `visuallyHiddenText` params are appended to the visible text (for example [in summary card actions](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/a5a50ea57175c0031168d227513b7710579d9c98/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/summary-list/template.njk#L7)); pagination is the only example I can find where `visuallyHiddenText` is passed directly to `aria-label`, completely overriding any visual label

The documentation for the params is also structured differently. For example the docs for pagination and breadcrumbs don't mention that the value will be used as the `aria-label`, while they do for cookie banner and service navigation.

Are any of these differences intentional? I think `ariaLabel` is clearest about what the params actually do, with `[thing]AriaLabel` for labels of child elements (eg password uses `showPasswordAriaLabelText`, though again the `Text` makes that inconsistent)

## Related component

<!-- Does this feature relate to an existing component? -->
Radios and checkboxes

## Context

<!-- What are you trying to do? Is this something you think should behave differently, or something that you currently cannot do? Is this related to an existing issue/bug? -->
You don't always want different `name` from `text`, for example when prototyping. An array of strings is a lot simpler than an array of objects. For example:

items: ["England", "Northern Ireland", "Scotland", "Wales"]

ourIssues.title: Explore adding `id` as an attribute for all our component macros
ourIssues.body:
Investigate the feasibility of adding a default `id` attribute for applying an optional HTML id to all component nunjucks macros. This would be similar to `class` and `attributes`, the 2 current default attributes.

## Context

This has come up in conversation on support and in the following related issues:

- https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/2999
- https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/3497

The case for doing this in brief is that `id` is a standard part of the HTML spec, similar to `class`, so exposing it would be useful for teams who might need to use the `id` attribute for any reason.

Additionally, several components already feature an `id` attribute so making this consistent has value.

## Alternatives

Currently teams can do this via `attributes`:

```nunjucks
attributes: {
    "id": "my-custom-id"
}
```

ourIssues.title: Error message: Remove hardcoded content order
ourIssues.body: ## What Error messages currently contain a fixed content order, which is hardcoded into the component's Nunjucks template. This is composed of a block of visually-hidden text (`visuallyHiddenText`, defaults to 'Error') followed by a colon (:), a hardcoded space, then the configured error message (`html` or `text`). This prefixes the message with 'error' for screen readers, so that the context of the message announced up-front and is easier to understand. For example, the component may currently output this text: ```html Error: Enter an event name ``` ## Why Having a hardcoded content order can make it more difficult to appropriately localise the string. In particular, the currently hardcoded colon and space characters are incompatible with certain languages. Some logographic written languages—such as Chinese and Japanese—use a fixed-width colon character that fits better alongside logograms, and don't include a space after it. ```html 错误：输入事件名称 エラー：イベント名を入力してください ``` Translators may also find that the 'Error' label being visible is more useful to their target users—as red does not indicate incorrectness or danger in all cultures (it symbolises happiness and prosperity in Chinese culture, for example). Although it is currently possible for services to pass HTML into the error message and remove the initial 'Error:' section by setting `visuallyHiddenText` to `false`, we may want to investigate methods of either making `visuallyHiddenText` work with other languages, incorporating the colon and space into the editable area, or removing the use of a dedicated parameter and hardcoded text in favour of only using the `html` parameter. ## Who needs to work on this Developers ## Who needs to review this Developers ## Done when - [ ] Investigate methods of making the error message support non-English languages. - [ ] Make changes to the Nunjucks template and related tests, if we decide to make modifications. - [ ] Document any changes to Nunjucks parameters.

ourIssues.title: Summary list: Allow customisation of full action link content
ourIssues.body: ## What Currently, action links in the Summary list have a hardcoded content order of the action name (`html` or `text`), followed by an area of visually hidden text (`visuallyHiddenText`). The visually hidden text includes a hardcoded space separating it from the prior text, and is usually the same or similar to the key for the current row. For example: ```html change name delete address ``` ## Why This fixed ordering doesn't accommodate localisation into languages where this text appears in a different order. For example, in German we might have this: ```html Namen ändern Adresse löschen ``` Having a hardcoded space is also undesirable in certain languages, such as Chinese: ```html 更换名字 删除名称 ``` Although it is currently possible for services to pass HTML into the action links and ignore the `visuallyHiddenText` parameter completely, we may want to investigate methods of either making `visuallyHiddenText` work with other languages, or removing the use of a dedicated/hardcoded parameter in favour of using the `html` parameter. ## Who needs to work on this Developers ## Who needs to review this Developers ## Done when - [ ] Investigate ways that `visuallyHiddenText` could work with non-English languages. - [ ] Make changes to the Nunjucks template and related tests, if we decide to make modifications. - [ ] Document any changes to Nunjucks parameters.

ourIssues.title: Make it easier to add a hint or an error message to a fieldset
ourIssues.body:
## What

If you want to use the fieldset component to group related fields, for example asking for a street address, you need to take care of including the hint / error message components separately and do extra work to associate them with the fieldset.

We do not provide any examples or guidance on how to do this, and it would be easy to get wrong (for example, by not creating the association with the fieldset)

It therefore seems like it would be useful if the fieldset component accepted `hint` and `errorMessage` objects and took care of this association itself.

## Why

This was requested by @edwardhorsford in https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/issues/778#issuecomment-459047140.

## Additional information

The radios, checkbox and date input components all use hints and error messages which are then associated with the fieldset using `aria-describedby`. However, this logic is handled (and therefore duplicated) within the individual components.

Moving this logic to the fieldset component _might_ allow us to simplify the repeated logic in the radios, checkboxes and date input components. However, it's not clear what should happen to the hint / error message [if you do not include a fieldset](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/62d3de38036b858b1dd85c5bd8c027830fab5a3d/src/components/date-input/template.njk#L79-L96).

ourIssues.title: Add label or legend param to date-input
Test that documented component options match the templates
ourIssues.body:
## What

Add tests that validate the documented options within our component YAML files (like [the button YAML file](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/f704053f8544e8d88acec68ca448b4cb992a76d2/src/components/button/button.yaml)) match the actual options used within the template / macro.

If the two do not match, the tests should fail.

There is as a ['work-in-progress' branch](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/test-definitions) for this work which currently does this, but needs some refactoring / documentation before it can be merged.

## Why

Currently we rely on human review to ensure that the documented options match reality. During a recent [firebreak](https://insidegovuk.blog.gov.uk/2018/05/03/firebreaks-on-gov-uk/) project, we explored whether we could do anything to catch these in our CI process.

The work found a number of inaccuracies in the documentation options:

- `attributes` not documented on the breadcrumbs and select components
- `describedBy` mistakenly documented on textarea and character count components
- `footer` component YAML misformed using `arguments` instead of `params`, which means the `meta` object is not documented correctly in the Design System
- `items[].name` mistakenly documented on radios – unlike checkboxes, this can only be set globally as having a set of radios with different names doesn't make any sense
- `title` not documented on the tabs component

This highlights the need to automate these checks, so we can make sure our documentation is correct.

ourIssues.title: Tables: Consider enabling array iteration in macros
ourIssues.body:
## What We've got an use case, where we'd like to pass some data into the template without pre-processing it to fit the table macro. Our use case using pure HTML: ```jinja {% for product in products %} {% endfor %}
{{ product.name }} {{ product.description }} {{ product.price }}
``` What we'd like to be able to do when using macros: ```jinja {{ govukTable({ "firstCellIsHeader": true, "head":[ {"text":"Name"}, {"text":"Description"}, {"text":"Price"} ], "data": products, "rows": [ {"text": product.name}, {"text": product.description}, {"text": product.price}, ] }) }} ```

ourIssues.title: Macros Component API should not require internal classes for modifiers
ourIssues.body:
Macros abstract our class names, if we were to change our class names, macro usage would break for our users.

In our button examples, we pass the internal button modifier class to make a button into a start button.

We could consider passing a boolean instead so that if we choose to change how our classes work, macros still function.

For example instead of

```yaml
- name: start
  data:
    text: Start now button
    classes: 'govuk-c-button--start'
```

We could do:

```yaml
- name: start
  data:
    text: Start now button
    start: true
```

See also the GOV.UK Publishing component: http://govuk-static.herokuapp.com/component-guide/button/start_now_button

Link to code: https://github.com/alphagov/static/blob/a9a040a72d475ef7015c1c9e690a5d77687fcfd8/app/views/govuk_component/button.raw.html.erb#L1

We constructed the class based on booleans, then finally merge with `classes` and inject into the markup.

Edit: 
I put together an example showing how you can restructure the macro to avoid the confusing forking logic.

This approach only forks on individual parts of the template, which is easier to reason about.

https://glitch.com/edit/#!/flag-based-macro-approach?path=views/index.html:15:26

backlog.title: Pull quotes
backlog.body:
What
The DFE are building a training platform to upskill the early years workforce. In this training offer, there is a need for varying types of content, to help keep users engaged with the learning materials. We use pull quotes to highlight key theories and statements from frameworks.
The large blockquote style has a decorative speech mark, an outline and is indented from the body text. We use this for quotes that are a couple of sentences long.

The short quote is an adaptation of the inset text component, and is used for single sentence quotes.

Why

Explain why you think this should be added to the GOV.UK Design System.

What evidence do you have that it's needed by multiple services across government?

What evidence do you have that it meets the needs of the users of those services?

Users have noted that having the quotes are useful for their learning and are more visually appealing compared to an older style of pull quote that we were using previously.

ourIssues.title: Various issues under Chrome's Auto Dark Mode
ourIssues.body:
Since Chrome version 78, Google has included an experimental feature in the browser, initially named "Forced Dark Mode" and, as of writing, named "Auto Dark Mode for Web Content". 

This feature automatically modifies the appearance of webpages in order to create a "dark mode" version. This is done even if the page already supplies a "dark mode" via the `prefers-color-scheme` CSS media query. It also appears to ignore the `color-scheme` property. 

The flag comes with several different "enabled" modes (as of Chrome 99), which modify how Chrome is internally applying changes. Each mode results in subtly (sometimes radically) different resulting colours.

1. Enabled
2. Enabled with simple HSL-based inversion
3. Enabled with simple CIELAB-based inversion
4. Enabled with simple RGB-based inversion
5. Enabled with selective image inversion
6. Enabled with selective inversion of non-image elements
7. Enabled with selective inversion of everything
8. Enabled with increased text contrast

Most of these modes appear to work by first overriding neutral light background colours (such as white and light greys), and modifying any copy that it detects as existing on a modified background colour to maintain suitable contrast. Most other colours appear to be left intact. This method of alteration means that colours are not all modified in the same way: `$govuk-brand-color` in mode 1, for example, is unmodified when used as a background or border colour (#1d70b8), but is changed when it is used as a text colour (#61a1ee).

Mode 4 appears to simply invert all colours on the page, regardless of usage. 

I'm not sure how mode 1 is different from the others. It may be that this is an "automatic" mode where Chrome tries to determine which of the other seven modes works best for the given page and uses that one.

We have received at least one bug report raised by a user who was using Chrome's Auto Dark Mode feature for accessibility reasons (to make content easier to read with cataracts).

> RE the dark mode, it is now a function in Google Chrome that you can activate and it will force a dark version if the website can accommodate it. Not everyone does, BBC News for example still comes through with a traditional black text on a white background – but it works for many.

## Steps to reproduce the issue
In Google Chrome, go to `chrome://flags/#enable-force-dark` (this should jump you straight to "Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents") and enable the flag.

## Actual vs expected behaviour
Currently, a number of these modes produce colour combinations which fail the contrast requirements established in WCAG 2.1. 

Below is a non-exhaustive subset of issues currently identified in Auto Dark Mode.

### Text inputs and textareas
Text inputs are displayed with a grey background and black border in modes 1, 6, 7, and 8. This fails to meet the expected 1:3 contrast ratio for UI elements (at 1:1.68). 

![Screenshot of the design system input component, appearing grey on black.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160644743-7632dc27-cc56-4558-bd40-8fee1109717c.png)

They are displayed with a light grey background and white border in modes 3 and 5, which easily meets contrast ratio expectations.

They are displayed with the default white background and black border in all other modes.

### Input prefixes and suffixes

These are difficult to read in modes 2 and 4, where they are black on a dark grey background (1:3.23).

![Screenshot of the design system input prefix and suffix example, where the text is black on dark grey.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160646813-ac2ad0a1-083d-4ca0-b571-b1ecacd450e4.png)

These are much more difficult to read in modes 3 and 5, which renders it as black on an even darker grey (1.22).

![Screenshot of the design system input prefix and suffix example. The text is visually imperceptible from the background.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160650473-9c6f3529-5a06-4408-b20e-242b1c66a08e.png)

These are displayed with adequate contrast in other modes.

### Checkboxes and radio buttons
The border and selection states of checkboxes and radio buttons do not have sufficient contrast in modes 1, 6, 7, and 8 (at a pretty much imperceptible contrast ratio of 1:1.04)

![Screenshot of the design system checkbox component, illustrating insufficient contrast between the checkboxes and background, which are both dark grey.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160644218-1fc50370-249e-4e47-b73a-eab9a8b8ea34.png)

They are displayed with white borders and selection states in all other modes.

### Select

In modes 1, 6, 7, and 8, select boxes are rendered with a dark grey background and dark grey border (1:1.04).

![Screenshot of the design system select component, which appears to just be white text with no border or icon.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160648934-5554f80a-1794-40e1-a9b7-a7c16df83d29.png)

They are rendered with a black background and white border in all other modes.

### Skiplinks

In modes 1, 2, 6, and 7, skiplinks are rendered as white on focus-colour yellow, which does not meet contrast requirements (1:1.34).

![Screenshot of a white link on a bright yellow background.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160649767-19aecf58-2ea6-4517-9852-283a4c91f922.png)

In mode 4, it is white on light blue, which is also below expectations (1:3.24).

![Screenshot of a white link on a bright blue background.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160649982-3f7999be-3540-40c5-8d00-7b9350407360.png)

In mode 8, it is white on focus-color yellow, but additionally has a black text shadow/stroke effect applied, which makes it difficult to read.

![Screenshot of a white link with a thin, pixellated black shadow surrounding it, on a bright yellow background.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160650309-a61034bd-d400-4ca3-b312-db890c382f19.png)

This is displayed with adequate contrast (albeit, in white on brown) in all other modes.

### Iconography

Most iconography fails to meet contrast requirements in virtually all modes. This includes:
- the open and close arrows on the Accordion component.
- the arrow on the Back link component.
- the arrows on the Breadcrumbs component.
- the exclamation icon on the Warning text component.

### Other components
The good news is that, for the most part, the majority of other components we have in GOV.UK Frontend are not as badly affected as those above, with various components such as Inset text, Error summary, and Notification banner maintaining their necessary visual presence and suitable contrast even with modified colours. 

## Environment
The results specified here were taken in Chrome 99, running on macOS 15.3, whilst the operating system was set to light mode. 

Interestingly, Chrome DevTools does not give any indication that a change to the page's appearance has taken place. All HTML and CSS content, including the user agent stylesheet, computed styles, and those returned through JavaScript, appear unmodified and are not aligned with the page's actual appearance when Auto Dark Mode is enabled.

communityIssues.title: Inconsistent components API
communityIssues.body:
The component API is inconsistent across components and in comparison with `govuk-frontend`.

In the table below there is a brief comparison in how `govuk-frontend` components are aligned in API with `govuk_publishing_components`

|Component               |API |
|---                      |---  |
Accordion                 | aligned
Back link                 | aligned
Breadcrumbs               | misaligned
Button                    | slightly misaligned (start)
Character count           | slightly misaligned (nesting)
Checkboxes                | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Date input                | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Details                   | misaligned
Error message             | aligned
Error summary             | misaligned
Fieldset                  | misaligned
File upload               | aligned
Footer                    | aligned
Header                    | slightly misaligned (navigation_items)
Inset text                | aligned
Panel                     | misaligned
Phase banner              | misaligned
Radios                    | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Select                    | slightly misaligned (options)
Skip link                 | aligned
Summary list              | slightly misaligned (items)
Table                     | aligned
Tabs                      | misaligned
Text input                | aligned
Textarea                  | aligned
Warning text              | slightly misaligned (iconFallbackText)

We can see a few common differences between to two API models:
- for arrays, `govuk-frontend` uses the generic `items` (in most cases) whereas `govuk_publishing_components` uses the name of the component (e.g. `attachments` for the attachment list component or `breadcrumbs` for the breadcrumbs component)
- for web addresses/paths `govuk-frontend` uses `href` whereas in `govuk_publishing_components` we often find `url` (e.g. breadcrumbs component)

It's worth mentioning that not even `govuk-frontend`'s API is consistent (e.g. `errorList` instead of `items` in the Error summary component, or differences in nesting)

A few advantages of making the API consistent:
- increases developers' confidence when calling components with arguments (without constantly checking examples in the guide)
- prototyping and production will use the same config object (can be easily copied over in both directions)
- applications can prepare the data to be fed into components consistently using helpers
- it would be easier to swap one component with another

I'm creating this to raise awareness of the differences, hopefully generate discussions around how good looks like and aim for consistency and convergency. API alignment requires at least a breaking change and some replacements across applications – which is not an easy process. For this reason, having a clear vision about how we want it to look like would save us from doing this more than once.

backlog.title: Error messages: add guidance on how to write good ones
backlog.body:
What
Every service needs to validate what people type in and select. This update will explain how to write error messages for everyone.
View the draft guidance
View the code in GitHub
Why
#6028 and #6026 tell you how to display an error message summary and field-level error messages. There needs to be guidance that:

shows how these components work together
documents error message content design principles
gives examples of what content should be used in error messages

This is needed across every government service to improve consistency within and between services. It is important to have error messages that work for everyone and give enough information to help people easily recover.
Anything else
I drafted some principles and presented them at ConCon 6 in September 2016. I then had a lot of comments from people in different departments and made changes to the draft. This includes principles, and suggested content for the error summary box and error messages.

ourIssues.title: Consider increasing contrast between `border` functional colour and page background
ourIssues.body:

## Description of the issue

The [border colour](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/colour/#:~:text=border,-#cecece) (#cecece) has a contrast ratio of 2:1:1 with the [body-background](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/colour/#:~:text=body-background) (#ffffff) colour. This was raised as lower than the minimum of 3:1 required by the Non-text contrast (AA) WCAG success criterion in an accessibility audit done on the GOV.UK Notify service in September 2024.

It's worth noting that the auditor raised this as a usability issue, not a WCAG fail. They raised it against Notify's use of the summary list component but I've framed this around the 2 colours mentioned because it will apply to other components/patterns.

The audit can be viewed here, with the issue on page 49:

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qR8t3mcEka6sUVGqfhnjEpyhqqQhGNFi/view?usp=sharing

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Use a colour contrast checker like [webaim's online checker](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/) to check the 2 colours.

## Actual vs expected behaviour

The border colour should have a ratio of 3:1 with the body-background colour.

They use older plain english component names and not `moduleName`

Trigger one of the errors shown above where `moduleName` is not used

ourIssues.title: Inconsistent print layout behaviour cross browser
ourIssues.body:
<!--
    Please fill in as much of the template below as you’re able to. If you're unsure whether the issue already exists or how to fill in the template, open an issue anyway. Our team will help you to complete the rest.

    Your issue might already exist. If so, add a comment to the existing issue instead of creating a new one. You can find existing issues here:

    - our known validation error/warning list: https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/1280#issuecomment-509588851
-->

## Description of the issue

When you print a page in chrome it looks different to when you print the same page in firefox or safari

Chrome uses the mobile breakpoint styles when printing - so grid columns become stacked vertically - however other browsers (firefox and safari) don't do this

A lot of HMRC services use a 2/3 grid area for their main content, but don't actually have anything in the remaining 1/3 of the layout

So when you print one of these in chrome, the 2/3 grid area expands to fill the whole width of the page (what they want). In firefox and safari however, the content still only takes up 2/3 with a gap on the right

For now they've patched it with this CSS to make the the print layout consistent between browsers
```
@media print {
    .govuk-main-wrapper > .govuk-grid-row > div[class*='govuk-grid-column-'] {
        width: 100%;
    }
}
```
The following screenshot shows how the print layout looks before applying this (top pdf on the right, with blue outlines added to it's layout elements) and after (bottom pdf on the right, with red outlines added to it's layout elements):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/100650/228557746-c1377d6f-bcab-40d1-a2d8-0aac3e0f7341.png)

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Try printing this example from the design system in chrome, then try printing it in firefox

https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/layout/common-two-thirds-one-third/index.html

The print layouts will be different

## Actual vs expected behaviour

The team who raised this with us in HMRC expected the print layout to be consistent between browsers

Should there be anything in govuk-frontend to make the print layout consistent by default between browsers - or guidance in the documentation explaining why there can be a difference

ourIssues.title: Radio Button numbering is misleading for MacOS VoiceOver when conditionally revealing content is revealed
ourIssues.body: ## Description of the issue When navigating a Radio component with MacOS VoiceOver, the voiceover includes which number in the sequence the currently selected radio button is. For example, when the first radio in a group of four is highlighted, the voiceover will include "1 of 4". For example (taken from the Design System): However, when conditionally revealled content is involved and triggered, the voiceover becomes misleading - both the total number of radios and the index of the currently selected radio are incremented by one, as if there's a hidden radio button appearing in the group before the one being selected. This is better illustrated by example: This is potentially misleading for users who rely on assistive technologies for visual impairments. I'm aware this is more than likely an issue with VoiceOver rather than this repository, but considering it's a mainstream tool affecting sites on a dominant web browser, I figured it's best to at least raise it to the maintainers' attention. ## Steps to reproduce the issue 1. Visit the [conditionally revealling content radio button example](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/#conditionally-revealing-a-related-question) on the GDS Design System using Google Chrome. 2. Open up MacOS's built-in Screen Reader (`System Preferences -> Accessibility -> VoiceOver -> Enable Voiceover`) 3. Navigate around the radio buttons in the example using either the keyboard or the mouse. 4. Observe the issue via the audio read-out and the voiceover text panel. ## Actual vs expected behaviour **Expected**: VoiceOver accurately describes the selected radio button's position within the radio group, and accurately describes the total number of radio buttons within the group. **Actual**: VoiceOver erroneously increments both of the following by `1`: * the selected radio button's position within the radio group; and * the total number of radio buttons within the group ## Environment (where applicable) - **Operating system**: MacOS (Catalina 10.15.7) - **Browser**: Google Chrome - **Browser version**: 93.0.4577.63 - **GOV.UK Frontend Version**: Whichever version the GOV.UK Design System site uses.

ourIssues.title: Add the ability to customise the classes on pagination links
ourIssues.body:
## Related component

[Pagination](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/pagination/)

## Context

Currently it isn't possible to add custom classes to individual links (neither items nor the previous/next links) within the pagination.

This limits the possibility of applying different or customised styling to them, such as [removing the visited state](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/links/#links-without-a-visited-state). 

## Alternatives

If using the Nunjucks macro, these links can only be changed through writing additional CSS that hooks onto the component's wrapper. 

Otherwise, the user must use the pure HTML version of the component or fork the macro themselves.

## Additional information

This feature was requested by a user via support.

Being able to remove visited states particularly seems like a useful function for search result pages, where the URL for a page may not be unique even though the page content is totally different.

ourIssues.title: Details - last child margin rule misses nested elements
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue If we have `

` or `

    ` elements inside a Details block, then their bottom margin is removed by a rule which looks like this in the browser: ``` .govuk-details__text>:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; } ``` which comes from [here](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/4fb2d91b86a0d807902b09d070ffc38f16442f97/src/govuk/components/details/_index.scss#L85) The problem we are having is that if the `

    ` or `

      ` element is nested, e.g. inside a `
      ` or another `
        ` then it escapes this rule and the bottom margin is wrong. This general issue is discussed here: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/31457798/best-usage-of-css-last-child-selector-in-nested-elements ## Steps to reproduce the issue Page content like this is mis-styled: ``` {% macro no_nino_details() %}

        {{ "no_nino__explanation" | translate }}

        ...
        • {{ "document__birth_marriage_etc" | translate }}
          • ...
            ...
          • {{ "benefits__other" | translate }}
        {% endmacro %} {{ govukDetails({ summaryText: "no_nino" | translate, html: no_nino_details() }) }} ``` ## Actual vs expected behaviour Expected: ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1265780/189160944-faa49dca-44d5-4746-8560-9cd1d36094a7.png) Actual ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1265780/189160854-93778355-edc1-4488-a058-ffa91eea115e.png) ## Environment (where applicable) `govuk-frontend@4.2.0` ## Suggested fix We are fixing with a rule like this: ``` .govuk-details__text > *:last-child, .govuk-details__text > *:last-child > *:last-child, .govuk-details__text > *:last-child > *:last-child > *:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; } ``` ... could this be added to govuk-frontend? See also https://stackoverflow.com/questions/31457798/best-usage-of-css-last-child-selector-in-nested-elements (Other components may be affected and may benefit from similar rules; I have checked only "Details" here)
