ourIssues.title: Notification banner guidance has misleading line?
ourIssues.body:
## Related documentation

On the [notification banner](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/notification-banner/) page:

"Use a notification banner to tell the user about something they need to know about, but that’s not directly related to the page content."

## Suggestion

There are cases where you might use a notification banner that _is_ directly related to the page content, particularly when using a [green success banner](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/notification-banner/#reacting-to-something-the-user-has-done). So we might need to change the emphasis of that opening line so it doesn't mislead people.

## Evidence (where applicable)

A designer raised this when designing a page that allowed users to save changes to a content page. They wanted to show a message to confirm the saved changes to users, whilst staying on the same page. I think the green success banner is ideal for that use case. However, the content at the top of the page (about not being related to the page content) made them think this wasn't an option.

ourIssues.title: WCAG 2.2: Start using a service ‖ Consistent Help
ourIssues.body:
## What

Consider adding or updating a screenshot of a start page to include visible help or contact information on the page, displayed in a consistent manner. Related to #2882. 

This is largely a usability suggestion and may not be necessary for WCAG compliance. 

### Resources

- [Start using a service pattern guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/start-using-a-service/)
- [WCAG 2.2 criterion for 'Consistent Help'](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help.html)

## Why

The new WCAG 2.2 Level A criterion 'Consistent Help' says:

> If a [Web page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help.html#dfn-web-page) contains any of the following help [mechanisms](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help.html#), and those mechanisms are repeated on multiple Web pages within a [set of Web pages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help.html#dfn-set-of-web-pages), they occur in the same order relative to other page content, unless a change is initiated by the user:
> * Human contact details;
> * Human contact mechanism;
> * Self-help option;
> * A fully automated contact mechanism.

Although the intent of the criterion is that the contact information itself is consistently ordered with respect to the rest of the page (i.e. a help link is always in the same place in the footer, as described in #2871) we can go beyond this by advising that teams provide this information in a consistent order every time it appears.

For example, if a service has three contact mechanisms—phone, email address, post—these should be listed in the same order and format on all pages where it appears, such as the service start page, support pages, contact page, etc. 

## Who needs to work on this
- Content designer or technical writer

## Who needs to review this
- Accessibility specialist
- Content designer or technical writer

## Done when

- [ ] Guidance has been updated

backlog.title: Number output
backlog.body:
What
Display the results of a calculation or the outcome of a user action.

Why
On the ‘Submit social housing lettings and sales data (CORE)’ service, we ask users to enter values for rent and other charges tenants pay.
We only need to collect the total amount, but users may be more familiar with individual values. Rather than ask them to calculate the total value themselves, we display a live calculation, which they can check before submitting the form.

Proposed solution
This component is similar to the existing text input component taking many of the same parameters (such as prefix and suffix), but uses the output element. This element is read-only and can’t be interacted with or gain focus, but instead provides semantics and accessibility features that enable user agents to announce a newly calculated value whenever it has been updated.
Results of usability testing
We initially tested this design in December 2021 and January 2022 with 10 participants. All but 1 had JavaScript enabled and were able to see the total box, but only those with JavaScript enabled would get a live calculation. They all clearly understood that the box represented a total of all values on the page, and were reassured when this value was played back on a ‘Check your answers’ screen.
However, given the possibility of a user entering the wrong total amount, and the system calculating its own value anyway, to save any confusion, we decided not to show the total amount part of the page if JavaScript is disabled.
When to use this component
Use this component when you want to give users a calculation of 2 or more numbers. While not required by the component, these should be of the same type (don’t mix currency with weights, for example). Use the prefix and suffix options to indicate what type of output is expected.
When not to use this component
You should not use this component to display alerts or other information you might place inside a live region.
How it works
This component is designed to act as a progressive enhancement, falling back to an input element if JavaScript is not available. If JavaScript is available, an input element is replaced by an output element which listens for changes on the inputs listed in its for attribute.
Try it for yourself

Demo: https://govuk-output.glitch.me/
Code: https://glitch.com/edit/#!/govuk-output

Outstanding issues and questions

This component has not been audited for its accessibility yet, and is yet to be used in a live production environment.
The output element is not supported in Internet Explorer 11. The component currently displays correctly, but doesn’t function.
Only supports addition at the moment; should it do more?
Should it be the responsibility of this component to provide a set of calculation behaviours (addition, multiplication etc.), or should this be left to individual developers who may have specific requirements?
Does there need to be an option for formatting the output, for example the number of decimal places to display?
How should invalid values be handled? Right now, if you don’t enter a number into one of the inputs, the calculated value isn’t updated.
This component may be interpreted as a disabled input; is there a better way to represent this value?

Anything else?

The number output component - CORE design history

backlog.title: Make a Joint Application
backlog.body:
What
A pattern for multiple users to submit an application together, which they may have joint liability for.
We've been specifically designing a service where users need to see everything the other person submits as they are taking out a loan together.
This interaction has been tested from both applicants' perspectives in multiple rounds of Alpha testing on our service:

First user completes application, submitting the information about their self and their partner.
At the end of the application, the first user is given a unique code to give to the second applicant.
The second applicant receives a link to the second applicant's start page, where they must enter the unique code.
Their bit of the application is essentially checking the details submitted by the first applicant, using the check your answers pattern. If they do change any of the answers, the first applicant will receive an email and go through the same process until both applicants have seen the information being submitted.

We first considered designing it so that each applicant fills in their own info, but then realised that would need much more back and forth between the applicants for most people. Users in our research said they'd probably either know the information about their partner, or be sat with them when making the application. We're also considering adding the ability to skip the pages that asking for your partner's information as we test more in Beta.
We can update here with more information from our Beta when we have it.
Why
There are various services in Government that need to applied for my multiple users, for example married couples, who may be doing something they are both liable for like buying a house, or maybe filing for a divorce, applying for Universal Credit, etc.
Anything else
I can link individuals to our research reports on this interaction if needed.

ourIssues.title: Explore improving the text-only zoom experience for GOV.UK Frontend
ourIssues.body: ## What Explore applying `em` sizing to all spacing on GOV.UK Frontend to theoretically improve the text-only zoom experience for components and styles. ## Why Whilst GOV.UK Frontend is built to accomadate standard browser zoom and provide a good experience for zoom users, browser also include features to "zoom" text only ie: increase the size of the text on the page but not the viewport ala standard browser zoom. Chrome's default text size increase (set to Very Large): Safari's text zoom (roughly 400%) Firefox's text only zoom (roughly 400%) ### Previous issues - https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/1569 - https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/1717 ### Where we've tried to tackle this already - https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/2998 - https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/1574 ## Assumptions - Using `em` sizing will provide a good experience for text only zoom users - Replicating the appearance and behaviour of standard browser zoom in text only zoom is useful - Replicating the appearance and behaviour of standard browser zoom in text only zoom is feasible ## Timebox 1 sprint ## Questions to answer - [ ] What is the impact of replacing all instances of `px` with `em` or the `govuk-em` mixin? ## Done when - [ ] Questions have been answered or we have a clearer idea of how to get to our goal - [ ] Findings have been reviewed and agreed with at least one other person - [ ] Findings have been shared, e.g: via a write-up on the ticket, at a show & tell or team meeting

ourIssues.title: Voice Control bug with .govuk-visually-hidden
ourIssues.body:
Voice Control appears to have a bug with the 'say what you see' feature when using interactive elements which have partially obscured content. 

If the `.govuk-visually-hidden` is added to an entire element, it causes no issues. But if an interactive element has something like a `<span>` inside it to partially hide some content, such as a 'change' link on the 'check your answers' pattern, then the bug occurs. 

The issue appears to be that Voice Control does not adjust its view of the page based on what is visible, and is still maintaining a directory of the verbose versions of each element. 

For example:

Using Dragon and Windows Speech Recognition, when you say 'click change' both softwares recognise the change links as identical and each link is highlighted so the can select which one they want.

Using Voice Control, when you say 'click change' nothing happens. If you inspect each link for it's full label, you can then get Voice Control to work if you are verbose. For example, 'click change name' works, but just saying 'click change' does not. So it would only work by guessing the full link label.

The links do still work with 'show numbers' and you can still select them by using the grid, so it's unlikely to be a blocker. I have filled in a bug report with apple (FB8973238), but realistically I doubt they will fix it. 

Just wanted to raise it so people had sight of it.

backlog.title: Highlighting information
backlog.body:
What

Give a brief description of the style, component or pattern you want to propose.

A number of internal services across government (examples below) have implemented a highlight pattern to focus a user's attention to particular parts of data. The pattern is used to visually highlight text to differentiate it from other information on the screen.

The following use cases of the pattern have been identified so far:

To highlight to users where data has changed - NHS cervical screening
To highlight to users where data is different when comparing - Identity verification, Home Office
To highlight to users where data matches when comparing - n'Delius records, MoJ
To highlight to users matched data from a search request - Search service, Home Office

Why
The pattern has been well tested in multiple services and already exists on live services within Home Office and MoJ.
The task to compare data is common, particularly for internal case working / management services. The ability to visually highlight elements should save the user time to find what they are looking for, especially when there is a lot of content on the page, or comparing multiple sets of data at once - valuable for repeat users.
Anything else
Examples in existing services:
NHS cervical screening management - used to identify changes in medical records


MoJ - used to identity cases and merge them

(Proposed) mock up design to be used in Home Office identity verification service - used to identify differences in two data sets

Accessibility considerations
Even though we can call out the highlighted text for screen reader users, conscious that the visual colour may not be ideal for users who are partially sighted. Curious to hear any comments around this.

ourIssues.title: Resolve the border-underline issue in the service nav component
ourIssues.body: ## What Let's fix the double underline that happens when a user interacts with a link in the service navigation component. The current [service navigation](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/service-navigation/) uses both a bottom border on an active nav item, as well as a link underline on hover/focus. This creates a double line on certain states, such as active:hover and active:focus. The reasons for this are - The service name is the same size as the links, but bolded for differentiation - This means that bold cannot be used on the links, as they would then be difficult to differentiate from the service name - Forced colour mode/ high contrast mode also wipes out any subtle changes in colour (using background colours on the element to differentiate active states, for example) - This meant that there were very few elements that could be used to indicate an active:hover or active:focus state on both default and high contrast displays - Link underlines were chosen for this reason ## Why The upcoming changes to GOV.UK and its service estate are a good opportunity for us to ship some improvements to components. There is also a small chance that the service name styling will need to be updated in order to harmonise it with the GOV.UK product suite: GOV.UK Pay/ App/ One Login/ Notify etc. This isn't confirmed, though. We will also possibly be asked to update the background of the component from grey to pale blue. This is a purely visual change to refine the way that the nav looks. It would be great to do this as our components are populated across a huge number of domains and its likely that the current navigation styling will persist and even be replicated elsewhere. Although this isn't an upgrade to the usability, it is a visual refinement that will improve our reputation for design that is as attractive as it is functional. ## Who needs to work on this @mia-allers-gds, a dev, another designer if necessary, and @selfthinker for her keen eye ## Who needs to review this The team! Maybe the community? ## Done when - [ ] Thing to do

ourIssues.title: Inconsistent spacing between buttons and button groups, and the following elements
ourIssues.body: Raised by a user via support last week. ## Description of the issue There is a visually inconsistent amount of bottom margin when comparing button components to button groups, when they are followed by another element that has a top margin (e.g. a section break). This is because the [vertical margins collapse](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_Box_Model/Mastering_margin_collapsing) for button groups, but not for standalone buttons. ## Steps to reproduce the issue 1. Using an implementation of govuk-frontend (download, npm package, prototype kit, etc.) create a page containing a [button component](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/button/) followed by a [section break](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/typography/#section-break) that has a top margin (xl, l or m). 2. Duplicate step 1, additionally wrapping the button component in a [button group](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/button/#grouping-buttons). ## Actual vs expected behaviour Actual: The visual spacing between the button and section break are different between the two examples. Expected: The margins should probably be the same. ## Environment (where applicable) - Operating system: N/A - Browser: Reproduced in Chrome 106 and Firefox 105 - GOV.UK Frontend Version: 4.3.1

ourIssues.title: The logical order of conditionally revealed content as it appears within a set of radios or checkboxes can be confusing
ourIssues.body:
The conditionally revealed content appears immediately after the control that reveals it. This means that it’s 'mixed up' within the logical order of the set of checkboxes or radios.

![design-system service gov uk_components_checkboxes_conditional-reveal_index html (2)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/121939/96256804-3784a500-0fb1-11eb-9814-e520f593002d.png)

This can cause confusion for screen reader users, as illustrated by this research finding from the checkboxes backlog issue:

> [We've just taken] our agent facing service to usability testing with someone who uses JAWS. Our biggest issue that we kept encountering was the use of conditional reveal, we think that with familiarity this issue would go away but it's definitely something we want to just work straight away without explanation.
> 
> User was presented with radio buttons as seen below:
> ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5321135/65248454-19b4ea00-daea-11e9-9aa2-3adef03eea9d.png)
> The user selected yes and then tabbed as they thought they had completed the section.
> It read out the label for the conditionally revealed input (although this was inconsistent, we want to get a JAWS device over the coming weeks and try and replicate the different behaviours, as sometimes the label was getting skipped)
> 
> The user then used the cursor down option in JAWS to see what else was on the page, and the next thing was "no"; this caused a lot of confusion because they thought it had jumped into the next radio button group, so this caused a lot of tabbing back and forth to try and find out where that "no" was coming from, at this point we then explained where that conditional content was in relation to the page. 
> 
> We have multiple other questions like this with similar content being revealed and this was a consistent theme, unsure which radio group they were in after entering the conditionally revealed content. This was also an issue when we had a legend explaining the question which was then being read out before the "no", because then it was as if tab had put them backwards in the form.
> 
> To summarise, user pressed tab after selecting radio button, which put them into the conditionally revealed content, they thought that was the next question so when they looked at the next part of the page and it was the remaining radio options they were completely unsure of where they were.
> 
> _Originally posted by @alexnewmannn in https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system-backlog/issue_comments/533134507_

ourIssues.title: Notification component uses `govuk-brand-colour` for border colour
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

We've set our `$govuk-brand-colour` to MHCLG's teal (#00625E) and it's done the thing we expected, which is: change the header/footer border colour. But it's also changed the colour of the border on the notification component, which our designers don't like - they expected it to stay as the standard blue.

Is this intentional/expected? I can see that the header component has a separate variable, govuk-header-border-colour that is set to govuk-brand-colour - but we can't override the header border color directly because it doesn't respect a default value.

Is it expected that our notification banners should match the brand colour? To our designers it feels odd, and I can imagine if your department's colour is red and now all your notification banners are red, that would also feel odd/undesirable?

See also reference to slack thread where this was first raised (while history exists): https://ukgovernmentdigital.slack.com/archives/C6DMEH5R6/p1757328829381619. Raising/duplicating here just so I have a permalink I can reference in code while we're using a temporary workaround.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Set `govuk-brand-colour` to a non-default value.
2. Render a notification banner component

## Actual vs expected behaviour

See that the border colour changes to the value you set for govuk-brand-colour, rather than the "default" blue.

ourIssues.title: Components assume the `govuk-visually-hidden` utility class will exist
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

We provide an entry points for each individual component, the idea being that users should get all of the CSS they need to use that component, and ideally nothing more.

For example, including the character count component also includes the CSS for the:

- error message
- hint
- label
- textarea

However, it does _not_ include the `govuk-visually-hidden` utility class, which is used within the Nunjucks template.

From a quick check, it looks like this affects:

- Accordion (in the JavaScript)
- Character count (in the JavaScript)
- Error message (in the Nunjucks template)
- Exit this page (in the Nunjucks template and JavaScript)
- File upload (in the JavaScript)
- Footer (in the Nunjucks template)
- Pagination (in the Nunjucks template)
- Password input (in the JavaScript)
- Summary list (in the Nunjucks template)
- Warning text (in the Nunjucks template)

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Use the component-specific entrypoint to include just the CSS for any of the components listed above, then view the component

## Actual vs expected behaviour

Visually hidden text should be hidden, but it isn't because the `govuk-visually-hidden` utility class is not included in the CSS

ourIssues.title: Various issues under Chrome's Auto Dark Mode
ourIssues.body:
Since Chrome version 78, Google has included an experimental feature in the browser, initially named "Forced Dark Mode" and, as of writing, named "Auto Dark Mode for Web Content". 

This feature automatically modifies the appearance of webpages in order to create a "dark mode" version. This is done even if the page already supplies a "dark mode" via the `prefers-color-scheme` CSS media query. It also appears to ignore the `color-scheme` property. 

The flag comes with several different "enabled" modes (as of Chrome 99), which modify how Chrome is internally applying changes. Each mode results in subtly (sometimes radically) different resulting colours.

1. Enabled
2. Enabled with simple HSL-based inversion
3. Enabled with simple CIELAB-based inversion
4. Enabled with simple RGB-based inversion
5. Enabled with selective image inversion
6. Enabled with selective inversion of non-image elements
7. Enabled with selective inversion of everything
8. Enabled with increased text contrast

Most of these modes appear to work by first overriding neutral light background colours (such as white and light greys), and modifying any copy that it detects as existing on a modified background colour to maintain suitable contrast. Most other colours appear to be left intact. This method of alteration means that colours are not all modified in the same way: `$govuk-brand-color` in mode 1, for example, is unmodified when used as a background or border colour (#1d70b8), but is changed when it is used as a text colour (#61a1ee).

Mode 4 appears to simply invert all colours on the page, regardless of usage. 

I'm not sure how mode 1 is different from the others. It may be that this is an "automatic" mode where Chrome tries to determine which of the other seven modes works best for the given page and uses that one.

We have received at least one bug report raised by a user who was using Chrome's Auto Dark Mode feature for accessibility reasons (to make content easier to read with cataracts).

> RE the dark mode, it is now a function in Google Chrome that you can activate and it will force a dark version if the website can accommodate it. Not everyone does, BBC News for example still comes through with a traditional black text on a white background – but it works for many.

## Steps to reproduce the issue
In Google Chrome, go to `chrome://flags/#enable-force-dark` (this should jump you straight to "Auto Dark Mode for Web Contents") and enable the flag.

## Actual vs expected behaviour
Currently, a number of these modes produce colour combinations which fail the contrast requirements established in WCAG 2.1. 

Below is a non-exhaustive subset of issues currently identified in Auto Dark Mode.

### Text inputs and textareas
Text inputs are displayed with a grey background and black border in modes 1, 6, 7, and 8. This fails to meet the expected 1:3 contrast ratio for UI elements (at 1:1.68). 

![Screenshot of the design system input component, appearing grey on black.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160644743-7632dc27-cc56-4558-bd40-8fee1109717c.png)

They are displayed with a light grey background and white border in modes 3 and 5, which easily meets contrast ratio expectations.

They are displayed with the default white background and black border in all other modes.

### Input prefixes and suffixes

These are difficult to read in modes 2 and 4, where they are black on a dark grey background (1:3.23).

![Screenshot of the design system input prefix and suffix example, where the text is black on dark grey.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160646813-ac2ad0a1-083d-4ca0-b571-b1ecacd450e4.png)

These are much more difficult to read in modes 3 and 5, which renders it as black on an even darker grey (1.22).

![Screenshot of the design system input prefix and suffix example. The text is visually imperceptible from the background.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160650473-9c6f3529-5a06-4408-b20e-242b1c66a08e.png)

These are displayed with adequate contrast in other modes.

### Checkboxes and radio buttons
The border and selection states of checkboxes and radio buttons do not have sufficient contrast in modes 1, 6, 7, and 8 (at a pretty much imperceptible contrast ratio of 1:1.04)

![Screenshot of the design system checkbox component, illustrating insufficient contrast between the checkboxes and background, which are both dark grey.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160644218-1fc50370-249e-4e47-b73a-eab9a8b8ea34.png)

They are displayed with white borders and selection states in all other modes.

### Select

In modes 1, 6, 7, and 8, select boxes are rendered with a dark grey background and dark grey border (1:1.04).

![Screenshot of the design system select component, which appears to just be white text with no border or icon.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160648934-5554f80a-1794-40e1-a9b7-a7c16df83d29.png)

They are rendered with a black background and white border in all other modes.

### Skiplinks

In modes 1, 2, 6, and 7, skiplinks are rendered as white on focus-colour yellow, which does not meet contrast requirements (1:1.34).

![Screenshot of a white link on a bright yellow background.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160649767-19aecf58-2ea6-4517-9852-283a4c91f922.png)

In mode 4, it is white on light blue, which is also below expectations (1:3.24).

![Screenshot of a white link on a bright blue background.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160649982-3f7999be-3540-40c5-8d00-7b9350407360.png)

In mode 8, it is white on focus-color yellow, but additionally has a black text shadow/stroke effect applied, which makes it difficult to read.

![Screenshot of a white link with a thin, pixellated black shadow surrounding it, on a bright yellow background.](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1253214/160650309-a61034bd-d400-4ca3-b312-db890c382f19.png)

This is displayed with adequate contrast (albeit, in white on brown) in all other modes.

### Iconography

Most iconography fails to meet contrast requirements in virtually all modes. This includes:
- the open and close arrows on the Accordion component.
- the arrow on the Back link component.
- the arrows on the Breadcrumbs component.
- the exclamation icon on the Warning text component.

### Other components
The good news is that, for the most part, the majority of other components we have in GOV.UK Frontend are not as badly affected as those above, with various components such as Inset text, Error summary, and Notification banner maintaining their necessary visual presence and suitable contrast even with modified colours. 

## Environment
The results specified here were taken in Chrome 99, running on macOS 15.3, whilst the operating system was set to light mode. 

Interestingly, Chrome DevTools does not give any indication that a change to the page's appearance has taken place. All HTML and CSS content, including the user agent stylesheet, computed styles, and those returned through JavaScript, appear unmodified and are not aligned with the page's actual appearance when Auto Dark Mode is enabled.

ourIssues.title: Investigate making it clearer that the Design System email address is not a generic government helpline
ourIssues.body:
Adding as I think we've discussed this before but never written it up.

## What

We very frequently receive emails from members of the public who have encountered issues with a GOV.UK service (or a government service generally) and are seeking support or updates. 

This is despite displaying a warning on our [get in touch](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/get-in-touch/) page stating that we are unable to help with these queries and providing instructions on how to contact the relevant government departments. 

## Why

This is not a high-volume issue (around a dozen emails a week or fewer), but it's a persistent one.

Members of the public often include Personally Identifying Information in these emails, unnecessarily exposing Design System team members to PII and requiring every member of the team to manually delete the offending emails from their inboxes to comply with data protection laws. In Zendesk, it also means that we need to go through the data redaction process before we can proceed to forward the ticket to user support.

In addition to dealing with the irrelevant ticket, these additional PII tasks are distracting for the whole team. They don't always happen in a timely fashion (if at all) due to members being on leave or on non-working days.

By reducing the quantity of unrelated support emails the team receives, we can alleviate this source frustration and help avoid unnecessarily holding personal data. 

A non-exhaustive list of potential ways to resolve this:

- Remove the contact page from search engine results, as (assumedly) this is where members of the public are finding it.
- Rewrite and/or reformat the existing warning text to make it _extremely_ explicit that we do not provide support or information to members of the public.
  - Consider harsher language in general, such as saying that emails from the public will be deleted and not responded to. 
- Use a more visually prominent component, such as a [Notification banner](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/notification-banner/), or bespoke styling, to display the warning.
- Consider not displaying the email address or link unless a user performs an action acknowledging the warning.

## Who needs to work on this

- Content designers
- Developers (potentially)
- Designers (potentially)

## Who needs to review this

- Content designers

## Done when

- [ ] Thing to do

communityIssues.title: Whitehall overrides some component styles
communityIssues.body:
There are a few instances in whitehall's CSS where styles for gem components are being overridden, which violates our principle of [component isolation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk_publishing_components/blob/main/docs/component_principles.md#a-component-is-isolated-when). 

If possible, these styles should either be applied directly to the components themselves (in the form of new options) or applied to parent elements of the components within the application, so they do not impact the appearance of the components themselves.

[_overrides.scss line 21](https://github.com/alphagov/whitehall/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/admin/_overrides.scss#L21) overrides `gem-c-summary-list` child elements:

- `.govuk-summary-list__key` is given a vertical align of top, which looks redundant and can potentially be simply removed (text is already vertically aligned to the top in this element)
- images are given `display: block`. This might be trickier to unpick although the use of this component doesn't normally include images, so this might be a custom application thing that could be added to the component defaults

[_overrides.scss line 44](https://github.com/alphagov/whitehall/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/admin/_overrides.scss#L44) overrides `gem-c-checkboxes` styles:

- there's a helpful comment here explaining the issue, which is to do with not showing checkboxes when JavaScript is enabled with the Add another component. The [component guide page for Add another](https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/add_another) doesn't show any examples containing checkboxes, so this could be something that could be part of the component with a documentation update

[_overrides.scss line 50](https://github.com/alphagov/whitehall/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/admin/_overrides.scss#L50-L59) overrides reorderable list styles:

- both overrides refer to a 'read only' version of the component, which seems like it should be an option within the component

[_document-collection-group-memberships-index.scss line 2](https://github.com/alphagov/whitehall/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/admin/views/_document-collection-group-memberships-index.scss#L2) overrides heading styles:

- it looks like the heading component is being positioned inline along with a list of items, presumably to make them all appear on one line together. Not sure which page this appears on, but it might be done better with some custom CSS specifically for this purpose, rather than components

[_edit-edition.scss line 33](https://github.com/alphagov/whitehall/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/admin/views/_edit-edition.scss#L33) overrides the warning text component:

- it's setting the margin bottom of the component to 0, which can be achieved without CSS by passing a `margin_bottom: 0` option to the component (warning text uses the [component wrapper helper](https://components.publishing.service.gov.uk/component-guide/warning_text#standard-options))

[_summary.scss line 47](https://github.com/alphagov/whitehall/blob/main/app/assets/stylesheets/admin/views/_summary.scss#L47) overrides the button component:

communityIssues.title: Inconsistent components API
communityIssues.body:
The component API is inconsistent across components and in comparison with `govuk-frontend`.

In the table below there is a brief comparison in how `govuk-frontend` components are aligned in API with `govuk_publishing_components`

|Component               |API |
|---                      |---  |
Accordion                 | aligned
Back link                 | aligned
Breadcrumbs               | misaligned
Button                    | slightly misaligned (start)
Character count           | slightly misaligned (nesting)
Checkboxes                | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Date input                | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Details                   | misaligned
Error message             | aligned
Error summary             | misaligned
Fieldset                  | misaligned
File upload               | aligned
Footer                    | aligned
Header                    | slightly misaligned (navigation_items)
Inset text                | aligned
Panel                     | misaligned
Phase banner              | misaligned
Radios                    | slightly misaligned (fieldset)
Select                    | slightly misaligned (options)
Skip link                 | aligned
Summary list              | slightly misaligned (items)
Table                     | aligned
Tabs                      | misaligned
Text input                | aligned
Textarea                  | aligned
Warning text              | slightly misaligned (iconFallbackText)

We can see a few common differences between to two API models:
- for arrays, `govuk-frontend` uses the generic `items` (in most cases) whereas `govuk_publishing_components` uses the name of the component (e.g. `attachments` for the attachment list component or `breadcrumbs` for the breadcrumbs component)
- for web addresses/paths `govuk-frontend` uses `href` whereas in `govuk_publishing_components` we often find `url` (e.g. breadcrumbs component)

It's worth mentioning that not even `govuk-frontend`'s API is consistent (e.g. `errorList` instead of `items` in the Error summary component, or differences in nesting)

A few advantages of making the API consistent:
- increases developers' confidence when calling components with arguments (without constantly checking examples in the guide)
- prototyping and production will use the same config object (can be easily copied over in both directions)
- applications can prepare the data to be fed into components consistently using helpers
- it would be easier to swap one component with another

I'm creating this to raise awareness of the differences, hopefully generate discussions around how good looks like and aim for consistency and convergency. API alignment requires at least a breaking change and some replacements across applications – which is not an easy process. For this reason, having a clear vision about how we want it to look like would save us from doing this more than once.

communityIssues.title: Allow component config to be passed into initAll
communityIssues.body:
## What

MOJ Frontend components can be initialised on the page using `MOJFrontend.initAll()` method.  However this method does not support passing in component config.

To initialise the datepicker through JS with JS configuration (as opposed to `data-` attribute config would require the component to be initialised individually

```
import { DatePicker } from '@ministryofjustice/frontend'

const $datePickers = document.querySelectorAll(
  '[data-module="moj-date-picker"]'
)

$datePickers.forEach(($datePicker) => {
  new DatePicker($datePicker, { minDate: "", maxDate: "" ...})
})
```

We should match the GOV.UK style and allow `MOJFrontend.initAll` to accept a config object for all of the components:

```
initAll({
 scope: $scope,
 datepicker: {...},
 buttonMenu: {...}
 ...
})
```

This will require some wrangling with types for `optionsOrScope` parameter - see govuk frontend [init.mjs](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/init.mjs) and nhs frontend [index..mjs](https://github.com/nhsuk/nhsuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/nhsuk-frontend/src/nhsuk/index.mjs)

## Why

This allows for easier config via JS and also aligns us with GOV.UK frontend (and also NHS Frontend)

This may also require updating our docs.

## Who needs to be involved

- Content Designer
- Developer


## Done

When component config can be passed into `initAll` and the documentation has been updated.

communityIssues.title: Allow Button Menu to always render as a dropdown
communityIssues.body:
<!--

Have you read the Code of Conduct? By filing an Issue, you are expected to comply with it, including treating everyone with respect:

https://github.com/ministryofjustice/moj-frontend/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Do you want to ask a question? Are you looking for support? You can [contact the Design System team](https://design-patterns.service.justice.gov.uk/community/help-and-feedback).

---

Keep in mind that this code is customisable. Please consider the following options before filing this issue:

* Tweak the project's configuration, styles, etcetera.
* Install a community package.
* Create a package or enhance an existing package.

If none of these options is appropriate for the feature you want, please explain why that's the case by filling out the issue template below.

Also, note that the team has finite resources, so it's unlikely that we'll work on feature requests. If we're interested in a particular feature, however, we'll follow up and ask you to submit an RFC to talk about it in more detail.

-->

## Summary

We would like to add the option to force the rendering of the Button Menu as a dropdown, even when only one action is available.

## Motivation

Our service makes use of the Button Menu on several pages. In some cases, some of those actions are unavailable, and the menu renders with only one action.

When this happens, the 'Actions' button gets replaced with a single button for the only action available. We have seen users clicking on this single action when they were simply trying to open the Actions menu, which they are used to seeing in this place. This has caused confusion and could result in unwanted actions being taken.

Being able to force the Button Menu to render as a dropdown, even for a single action, would provide consistency for our users and prevent accidental clicks on single buttons.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

For the time being, we can get around this limitation by adding, then removing, an extra element to all Button Menu instances, to force the menu to be rendered as a dropdown:

```js
import { ButtonMenu } from '@ministryofjustice/frontend'

document.querySelectorAll('.moj-button-menu').forEach(container => {
  const extraElement = document.createElement('span')
  container.appendChild(extraElement)
  new ButtonMenu(container, {
    alignMenu: 'right',
  })
  extraElement.parentElement.remove()
})
```

While this works well, it seems a little hacky!

## Additional context

I believe it should be relatively straightforward to offer a `forceMenu` config option for the `ButtonMenu` component. Setting this to `false` by default should ensure complete backwards compatibility -- I'll get a PR ready for this.

communityIssues.title: Images don't appear when using the Prototype Kit
communityIssues.body:
### Description

When using moj-frontend with the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, remote images are not correctly loaded (on Filter a liist, Timeline, and Button menu). This is because the generated path (`/assets/images/...`) is not served by the Prototype Kit. Instead, the correct path is `$govuk-extensions-url-context + "/%40ministryofjustice%2Ffrontend/moj/assets/"` (NB: symbols in NPM package name must be URL-encoded).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up a prototype (`npx govuk-prototype-kit@latest create`)
2. Install moj-frontend (`npm install @ministryofjustice/frontend --save`)
3. Add a component that uses an image, such as "Filter a list"
4. Run the prototype (`npm run dev`)

**Expected behaviour:** Images should be loaded from remote paths

**Actual behaviour:** The image requests 404 and aren't loaded

**Reproduces how often:** 100%

### Versions

Prototype Kit: 13.16.0
moj-frontend: 2.0.0

### Additional Information

This could be fixed by updating [the Sass](https://github.com/ministryofjustice/moj-frontend/blob/ca8f3908f9390a835303a12c663c3ae2e241d365/src/moj/settings/_assets.scss#L6) to:
```scss
$moj-assets-path: if(
  $govuk-prototype-kit-major-version > 12,
  $govuk-extensions-url-context + "/%40ministryofjustice%2Ffrontend/moj/assets/",
  "/assets/"
) !default;
```

But doing so in the distributed file might have unintended side effects, so it would be preferable to provide a separate entrypoint for prototypes.

backlog.title: Toggle switch component
backlog.body:
What
An on/off toggle button that allows the user to make a change to that page immediately, without the need to submit an answer or navigate away from the current page.
Why
On the 'Video appointment service' project, there was a user need to change a setting on the page (microphone - on/off and camera - on/off). We have done 5 rounds of research with a variety of iterations and users and have concluded that a toggle switch design is the most recognisable, usable and understandable. We initially tested with components already in the GOV.UK design system (buttons with text, buttons with icons and text and radio buttons) but users with low digital confidence struggled to know the current state of the buttons, and radios and checkboxes are an input that needs submitting, rather than having an immediate effect on the page. (https://www.nngroup.com/articles/toggle-switch-guidelines/)
In our latest round of research, everyone understood and could use the toggle buttons designed. They have also been thoroughly accessibility tested. I have not seen any other examples of toggles across government services (except for the NHS app).
It is worth noting they currently rely on javascript which is acceptable on the 'Video appointment service' as javascript is required to take part in the video appointment.
Anything else
Mural board on iterations and high level research findings:


Addition of colour and shape has been found to increase understanding of current state.

ourIssues.title: Issues with Exit this Page keyboard shortcut and the iOS/iPadOS virtual keyboard
ourIssues.body:
## Description of the issue

The Exit this Page component includes a method of activating the exit functionality by pressing the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key three times (behind the scenes, three `keyup` events). We do not limit when this functionality works, so it's still possible to do this when focused on an input or textarea. This is by design, as we want the user to be able to use the function quickly and at any time. 

This does mean, however, that the function is exposed to devices that utilise virtual keyboards (aka, on-screen keyboards or software keyboards) when a text field is focused. This can be problematic, as the <kbd>Shift</kbd> function was only designed with hardware keyboards in mind and virtual keyboards can operate substantially differently than their hardware equivalents.

### An overview of iOS <kbd>Shift</kbd> operating modes

The <kbd>Shift</kbd> key on iOS has multiple modes of operation depending on the current context, attributes of the current input, and how it is pressed. In one context it is also replaced by a numbers and symbols toggle button, however this button is still treated as being a <kbd>Shift</kbd> key for the purposes of JavaScript events.

**When pressed for a short period of time**, the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key acts as a toggle switch, and changes between being 'on' or 'off' on alternating presses of the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key. The `keyup` event is fired on every second press (the 'off'), except in cases described below.

**When held down**, the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key acts transiently, being 'on' for as long as the user holds it down and turning 'off' once released. The user can press other keys when <kbd>Shift</kbd> is held down to type in uppercase. When used in this way, the `keyup` event is **not** fired when the user releases the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key.

The user can **tap <kbd>Shift</kbd> twice** in rapid succession to turn on Caps Lock mode. The user can press <kbd>Shift</kbd> a third time to turn Caps Lock mode off. When this is carried out, it's emitted as a `keyup` event by the <kbd>Caps Lock</kbd> key, not the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key.

When the user **enters numbers and symbols mode** on the keyboard, the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key is visually replaced by a button to toggle between the initial numbers and symbols view, and the extended symbols view. In this mode, tapping to view the extended symbols mode is treated as a <kbd>Shift</kbd> `keydown` event, and returning to the initial numbers and symbols view is treated as a <kbd>Shift</kbd> `keyup` event. These events are emitted to the webpage, in what feels like a bug in Safari or iOS. 

There are several situations in which **the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key is turned 'on' automatically**. When this happens, no `keydown` event is emitted to the webpage. When it is turned 'off', either automatically or by the user, no `keyup` event is emitted. 

> [!NOTE]
> The takeaway to remember from this is that <kbd>Shift</kbd> will _never_ emit a `keyup` event if the `keydown` wasn't initiated by the user, even if the `keyup` was. This holds true for all of the cases here. 

Situations where this can occur include:

* The input being empty when the user taps on it.
* The cursor being positioned at the start of a new sentence, line or paragraph when the user taps on the input.
* The cursor being positioned at the start of a new word, if the input has the `autocapitalize="words"` attribute.
* Always, if the input has the `autocapitalize="characters"` attribute.

There are a couple of situations where the virtual keyboard will **fire `keyup` events without user intent**. These include: 

* Turning <kbd>Shift</kbd> 'on' manually and switching to the numbers and symbols view will emit the `keyup` event.
* On an input where <kbd>Shift</kbd> will not turn 'on' automatically (e.g. in the middle of a word or sentence), manually activate <kbd>Shift</kbd>, close the virtual keyboard, and then tap on the input to open it again. <kbd>Shift</kbd> will be returned to the 'off' state and emit the `keyup` event.

In testing, we particularly noticed this being a problem on iOS and, presumably, are mirrored in iPadOS. 

> [!NOTE]
> These problems with the shortcut were only noted when using the virtual keyboard. The shortcut works as intended when using a hardware keyboard paired with the iOS/iPadOS device.

## Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Visit a page that has both the Exit this Page button and an input field.
2. Focus the input so that the virtual keyboard opens.
3. Attempt to activate the EtP functionality by tapping <kbd>Shift</kbd> at least three times.

## Actual vs expected behaviour

### Expected

The Exit this Page functionality is activated and the user leaves the page.

### Actual

It is very difficult to activate the EtP shortcut behaviour intentionally.

If the user is pressing the key rapidly, and assuming an initially empty input or textarea, the most likely scenario is:

1. <kbd>Shift</kbd> was already turned on by default. Tap 1 turns it off and does not emit a `keyup` event.
2. Tap 2 happens quickly enough that Caps Lock mode is activated. <kbd>Caps Lock</kbd> emits a `keydown` event. 
3. Tap 3 turns off Caps Lock mode. <kbd>Caps Lock</kbd> emits a `keyup` event.
4. Tap 4 turns Caps Lock mode back on.
5. Repeat.

It is possible to activate the function successfully if the user takes time to wait between button presses—roughly half a second between presses. This wait is exacerbated by the need to perform more taps than usual, requiring 3 before the indicator lights are first shown, and a total of 7 to activate the functionality.

In addition, there are seemingly many scenarios that can unintentionally add to the <kbd>Shift</kbd> key activation count or cancel an activation currently in progress, most commonly, accidentally tapping fast enough to enable Caps Lock mode.

## Environment (where applicable)

- Operating system: iOS 16.4
- Browser: Safari
- Browser version: 16.4
- GOV.UK Frontend Version: 4.7.0 (however testing took place prior to this release)

ourIssues.title: Add `size` option to form input component labels
ourIssues.body:
<!--

  This is a template for any issues that aren’t bug reports or new feature requests. The headings in this section provide examples of the information you might want to include, but feel free to add/delete sections where appropriate.

-->

## What

Allow form field components to receive a new `size` option in their `label` or `legend` option for easily controlling the text size of their label or legend. The option should receive a t-shirt size and set the appropriate `.govuk-label--<T_SHIRT_SIZE>` or `.govuk-fieldset__legend--<T_SHIRT_SIZE>` on the label or legend.

For components using a `label` the option should be implemented by adding a [new option to our internal Label component](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/label) and passing the option through. For those using a `legend`, the public Fieldset component should get an update first in a similar fashion.

The affected components are:
- [Character Count](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/character-count/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Textarea)
- [Checkboxes](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/checkboxes/template.njk) (forwarding the option to either Fieldset)
- [Date Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Fieldset](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input/template.njk)
- [File Upload](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/file-upload/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Label](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/label/template.njk)
- [Password Input](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/password-input/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Input)
- [Radios](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/radios/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Fieldset)
- [Select](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/select/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)
- [Textarea](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/main/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/textarea/template.njk) (forwarding the option to Label)

## Why

Different components use different tags for the "title" of the field. This requires the user to understand internal nuances (is it a `label` or `legend`) to change its size. Having an option abstracting this and letting the component work out if it's `.govuk-label--...` or `.govuk-fieldset__legend--...` that's needed is much easier.

## Who needs to work on this

Developers, Tech writer

## Who needs to review this

Developers, Tech writer

## Done when

- [ ] The new option is available on all the components listed above
- [ ] The option is documented consistently across components

ourIssues.title: Module name missing for some `new ElementError()` calls
ourIssues.body:
<!--
    Please fill in as much of the template below as you’re able to. If you're unsure whether the issue already exists or how to fill in the template, open an issue anyway. Our team will help you to complete the rest.

    Your issue might already exist. If so, add a comment to the existing issue instead of creating a new one. You can find existing issues here:
    - an existing Github issue: https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues
    - known validation errors or warnings: https://github.com/orgs/alphagov/projects/37
-->

## Description of the issue

Component `ElementError` messages were [updated to use `moduleName` suffixes](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/pull/5338):

```console
govuk-accordion: Root element (`$root`) is not of type HTMLElement
govuk-button: Root element (`$root`) already initialised
govuk-checkboxes: Form inputs (`<input type="checkbox">`) not found
govuk-exit-this-page: Root element (`$root`) is not of type HTMLElement
...
```

But the following error messages were missed:

```console
Password input: Form field (`.govuk-js-password-input-input`) must be of type `password`.
Password input: Button (`.govuk-js-password-input-toggle`) must be of type `button`.
Skip link: Target link (`href="#example"`) has no hash fragment
```

They use older plain english component names and not `moduleName`

<!-- A clear and concise summary of what the bug is. -->

## Steps to reproduce the issue

Trigger one of the errors shown above where `moduleName` is not used

## Actual vs expected behaviour

All component-level errors should log the correct `moduleName` for better error reporting

E.g. `Password input:` → `govuk-password-input:`

```patch
- Password input: Form field (`.govuk-js-password-input-input`) must be of type `password`.
+ govuk-password-input: Form field (`.govuk-js-password-input-input`) must be of type `password`.
```

```patch
- Password input: Button (`.govuk-js-password-input-toggle`) must be of type `button`.
+ govuk-password-input: Button (`.govuk-js-password-input-toggle`) must be of type `button`.
```

```patch
- Skip link: Target link (`href="#example"`) has no hash fragment
+ govuk-skip-link: Target link (`href="#example"`) has no hash fragment
```

ourIssues.title: WCAG 2.2: Investigate thickness of input focus state border
ourIssues.body:
## What
Investigate if the increased black border for the focus state of form inputs needs to be thicker.

## Why
During testing of components against [WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.4.13: focus appearance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html) as part of https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/4347, it was discovered that several form input components that use a similar "box highlight" style focus state fail this criterion. This is because the black border isn't thick enough to meet the size requirements for this criterion and the yellow highlight can't count towards this as it's too low contrast against the white background. Increasing the black border could fix this.

This impacts the following components:
 - [Date input](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/date-input/)
 - [Select](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/select/)
 - [Text input](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/text-input/)
 - [Textarea](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/textarea/) (which will also impact [character count](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/character-count/))

It additionally effects [radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/) and [checkboxes](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/checkboxes/) but for slightly different reasons, although it's valuable to tackle these at the same time.

### Further reading
- [Testing spreadsheet (internal only)](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PpKvhCGZJb1j0ZUUY2ZuA0CBQeu04yFD1bumiL8wGX8/edit#gid=0)
- https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/issues/3007 - related issue on focus state rationalisation
 
## Who needs to work on this
Developers, designers

## Who needs to review this
Developers, designers

ourIssues.title: Research making the checkbox and radio button labels full width
ourIssues.body:
## What

Perform research with users as to whether making labels on checkboxes and radio buttons span the width of the container, thus increasing their touch surface, makes it easier to use these controls

## Why

Generally speaking, increasing the target area for a control makes the control easier for users to interact with.

We have some existing precendent for this in Frontend already: 

- Labels for other input types (text inputs, selects, textareas, etc.) are already full width.
- The Accordion activates expand/collapse functionality by tapping anywhere in the section header.
- The Skip Link component, when visible, is activatable by clicking anywhere in the component.

The GOV.UK team has had positive feedback when increasing target sizes for elements on the [homepage](https://insidegovuk.blog.gov.uk/2021/12/13/updating-the-gov-uk-homepage/) and [topic pages](https://insidegovuk.blog.gov.uk/2022/08/08/rolling-out-a-new-design-for-browsing-gov-uk-by-topic/) in the last year.

Various external design systems have full width checkbox and radio labels, some of which are based on or inspired by GOV.UK Frontend and have seemingly made the conscious choice to change it:

- ~~[USWDS](https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/checkbox/)~~ Update: Has since updated to no longer be full-width
- [NICE Design System](https://design-system.nice.org.uk/storybook/?path=/story/foundations-checkbox--default)
- [Transport for West Midlands Design System](https://designsystem.tfwm.org.uk/components/radios/)
- [GOLD Design System](https://gold.designsystemau.org/components/control-input/#checkbox-block) (formerly Australian Government Design System)
- [Atlassian Design System](https://atlassian.design/components/checkbox/examples)

Our inline labels date from the GOV.UK Elements days, and I couldn't immediately find any reason why they were implemented in this way at the time. We have stuck to that precedent in situations where a conflict or bug relating to the label sizing has arisen (e.g. #634).

We should validate our current approach and whether it best meets user needs when compared to alternative approaches.

## Assumptions

We've [previously found that users don't tend to click on checkbox or radio button labels](https://designnotes.blog.gov.uk/2016/11/30/weve-updated-the-radios-and-checkboxes-on-gov-uk/), even if they're styled to appear interactible. It could be assumed that the same applies here (if not moreso, as there isn't any visual indicator that interaction is possible). 

As a larger area of the screen will activate a checkbox/radio, there may be an increase in the number of accidental form inputs being made.

A seemingly 'empty' part of the page affecting a nearby input may be unexpected and cause confusion to users unless some other hint is present (e.g. a hover state). 

## Timebox
TBD

## Who is working on this?

Spike lead: TBD

Spike buddy: TBD

## Questions to answer

- [ ] Is there a tangible benefit to checkbox and radio button labels always being full width?
- [ ] Is there a tangible benefit to checkbox and radio button labels being full width in certain situations (e.g. on narrow screens)? 
- [ ] Are full width labels more likely to result in accidental and unwanted inputs?
- [ ] Is having a visually 'empty' area of the screen interactive unexpected or a source of confusion?

## Done when

- [ ] A review or prototype is produced with the modified checkbox/radio styles.
- [ ] User research has been carried out to see how these changes perform with users.
- [ ] Findings have been reviewed and shared with the team.
- [ ] Any follow up issues or actions have been written up.

ourIssues.title: Narrator cannot select Input Suggestions
ourIssues.body:
Hello,

My colleague has previously emailed about these two issues (ID: 6183982), but I'm submitting them here as you suggested just in case you get more capacity to look at them in the future. We have two similar issues with Narrator preventing users from being able to select input suggestions in text boxes and select fields.

Browsers used for all tests:
Microsoft Edge for Business
Version 137.0.3296.62 (Official build) (64-bit)

Microsoft Edge for Business
Version 137.0.3296.68 (Official build) (64-bit)

### Issue 1: Form / Narrator issues - Cannot select Input suggestion with Narrator focused on it
 
Description
When using Narrator within a form (developed using x-gov form builder), a user cannot select Input suggestions listed in the callout by using keyboard input means including the ENTER, TAB and Spacebar keys, this issue does not occur when attempting the same process with Narrator off.

We replicate the issue with the following steps, however the URL may not work for you.

a.   Activate Narrator.

b.   Navigate to URL: https://runner-stg.testwebforms.test-and-trace.nhs.uk/kls-enquiries/start

c.   Complete the "Systematic review" enquiry form process up to the "about-you" page.

d.   Tab into the "Full name" form input field (id="nBYObd") to give it focus.

e.   A list of input suggestions of previously used names are displayed in a callout box.

f.    Highlight the first input suggestion by using Down Arrow Key.

g.   The input suggestions callout box will close, the "Full name" form input field will remain blank and the Speech Reader focus moves onto the next field instead of the expected behaviour of the input suggestions callout box closing and the "Full name" form input field being populated with the chosen input suggestion.

 
### Issue 2: Narrator issues - Cannot select dropdown item with Narrator focused on it

Description
When using Narrator within a forms environment, a user cannot select Input suggestions listed in the callout by using keyboard input means including the ENTER, TAB and Spacebar keys, this issue does not occur when attempting the same process with Narrator off.
We replicate the issue with the following steps, however the URL may not work for you:

1.    Navigate to URL: https://runner-stg.testwebforms.test-and-trace.nhs.uk/kls-enquiries/start

2.    Complete the "Systematic review" enquiry form process up to the "systematic-review-questions" page.

3.    Tab into "What type of review are you doing?" Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) to give it focus.

4.    Select Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) using Spacebar or ENTER Key to display the dropdown list.

5.    Dropdown list is displayed.

6.    Highlight the first item "Fully systematic review" by using Down Arrow Key.

7.    Select item "Fully systematic review" by using ENTER Key.

8.    The dropdown list is still displayed instead of the expected behaviour of it closing and the focus returning to the "What type of review are you doing?" Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) field.

9.    Tab out of the "What type of review are you doing?" Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) dropdown list to select the item "Fully systematic review".

10.  The item "Fully systematic review" will be cleared from the "What type of review are you doing?" Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) field, instead of the expected behaviour of it being populated with the item "Fully systematic review" and the dropdown list closing.

 

The only way to make this work when the Narrator is on is to do the following:

1.    Complete Step 1 through to Step 6.

2.    Position the pointer/cursor directly over an item in the list so it is highlighted in grey.

3.    Select item "Fully systematic review" by using Spacebar or ENTER Key.

4.    Tab out of the "What type of review are you doing?" Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) dropdown list to select the item "Fully systematic review".

5.    The "What type of review are you doing?" Combobox (id="lIUPMw”) field is populated with the item "Fully systematic review" and the dropdown list closes as expected.

ourIssues.title: Add guidance around print styles and behaviour
ourIssues.body:
## Related documentation

No existing equivalent.

Should likely be a new page, but could be spread across several pages (colours, typography, accordion, tabs, details, etc.) otherwise. 

## Suggestion

The Design System doesn't currently provide any guidance relating to print styles. The only mention of them is on the [layout styles](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/layout/), where there's a override class specific to hiding elements when printed.

This is a question that comes up on support channels and is discussed on Slack semi-frequently, and we have made various choices when developing styles and components that are undocumented. This guidance could also be useful for teams developing new components built on Frontend's code. 

### Things that could be documented

**Remember printing is expensive.** Ink and paper are not free (ink especially) for both users and the environment. Where possible, we should minimise how much of each is used by hiding superfluous elements on the page when printing (e.g. the site's navigation) and making considered decisions over the use and quantity of colour.

**Maintain the page's current state.** A user is often printing the page because they need a hard copy of some piece of information. This could be a particular section on a guidance page, a reference number for an application, or the answers they've provided to a service. Generally, don't alter parts page the user is likely to want to print, when they print it (e.g. expanding or collapsing accordion sections, changing tabs, blanking form inputs).

**Remove background colours.** Don't rely on the presence of a background colour for text contrast. If anything, we likely want to encourage proactively removing background colours to ensure the readability of any text placed on top of them. Use borders to preserve the separation and grouping of elements instead.[^FE]

**Don't use colour to convey information.** Pages may be printed in greyscale, making it difficult to determine the colours of elements. Supplement with text labels, shapes or patterns.

**Use system fonts.** Printers can occassionally struggle to correctly understand web font formats. Reset to a system font or font keyword (e.g. `sans-serif`) to avoid this issue.[^FE]

**Provide context for invisible information.** Some information is usually only visible within a browser, such as a tooltip expanding on an `<abbr>` or the browser status bar showing the URL that a link directs to. When printed, this important information can be lost. Use print styles to re-insert this content on the page.[^FE]

[^FE]: Already a thing GOV.UK Frontend or Frontend components do. Still good to include so teams don't inadvertently override it or forget to implement or test in their own styles.

### Caveats

A user's individual printer configuration will change what the output looks like, and each browser additionally handles things differently when printing, such as whether they respect media queries and what breakpoints they use for calculating them. In this regard, a content author doesn't have a huge amount of control over how some aspects of a page look when printed. Related issue: https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/issues/3441

ourIssues.title: Replace what's new Mailchimp signup form with a custom signup form using server-side validation
ourIssues.body:
## What

The 'what's new' email signup form should use GOV.UK Design System components, including using server-side validation to show form errors to the user.

As currently the Design System website is a set of static pages, this will require an additional server app to be able to:

1. serve the HTML form (possibly?)
2. receive the form submission
3. validate the form submission
4. generate a page with error messages and serve it to the user OR
5.  submit the request to the Mailchimp API

There are a number of ways to achieve this; the first part of this epic will be to choose one that fits our needs.

## Why

Currently the 'what's new' mailing list signup form is a regular hosted Mailchimp form. This has a number of downsides:

- the form HTML has accessibility issues
- the form error handling has accessibility issues
- the form design is not consistent with GOV.UK Design System
- the solution is tied to Mailchimp

We looked at using an embedded Mailchimp form, but this would require using JavaScript to do input validation and error handling.

We used the Mailchimp signup form as a 'minimum viable product' for the initial launch of the 'what's new' feature because: a) we had tested it in user research and found that users were able to complete the journey b) we hadn't yet got usage analytics to validate that an email list fulfils the user need.

However, for a permanent solution, server side validation is the best and only way to get an accessible and consistent experience for all users.

## Who needs to know about this

Product manager, Developer, User researcher (possibly)

## Done when

- [ ] we've scoped out the different options for server-side validation, and chosen one
- [ ] the 'what's new' signup form uses Design System components (design has already been done, see commit [5bca1b64a](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/blob/5bca1b64acb67a372f9cec84e37ba42277fd92dc/src/email-updates.njk))
- [ ] we have a server-side validation solution for the form input
- [ ] the form and validation are connected so that form errors are shown to the user using Design System components
- [ ] the form is reachable from the Design System website
- [ ] user journey to signup to emails has been validated with user testing (possibly?)

backlog.title: GOV.UK Design System as an agent skill for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor
backlog.body:
I've packaged the Design System as an open source agent skill so coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) use it properly instead of from memory: https://github.com/chrisjohnleah/govuk-design-system-skill
It is generated from govuk-frontend 6.5.1, this repo and govuk-frontend-docs. Every component page carries the guidance, the macro options table and the exact HTML each example renders to, plus all 35 patterns and 13 styles. A single CHOOSING file compiles every "when to use" and "when not to use" so the agent picks the right component before it writes any markup.
The bit I cared most about: without the skill, an agent building a page for a charity used the crown, the GOV.UK header and GDS Transport. With it, the agent read "Using GOV.UK Frontend without GOV.UK branding" first and switched to the Generic header, a font override and its own icons. The skill leads with that decision.
Install: npx skills add chrisjohnleah/govuk-design-system-skill
A script regenerates everything from upstream, so it can track releases rather than drift.
Not affiliated with GDS. Happy to change anything the team would rather I did differently, especially around how the licensing of the crown and typeface is worded.

ourIssues.title: Add 'The following links open in a new tab' option to footer component
ourIssues.body:
## What

If a footer has multiple links that open in a new tab or window, our [guidance](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-design-system/pull/1179) says you could (in order to save space and avoid repetition) consider adding a line of text before the links saying 
> The following links open in a new tab

We should make it possible to add this text to the footer, at the moment it's not obvious where the text 
> 'The following links open in a new tab' 

should go in the footer. Should it be below the section headings or next to them? How should the text be marked up?

## Why
There should be a consistent, accessible way of including the text in the footer sections following our guidance.

## Who needs to know about this
Designer, developer, tech writer 

## Done when

- [ ] We've documented the option in the Nunjucks options table
